---
title: "Wastewater 12S"
author: "Emma Copen"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup}
# =========================================================================
# 12S vertebrate eDNA in municipal wastewater: analysis and figures
# =========================================================================
# This file reproduces every figure, supplementary figure, supplementary
# table and statistic in the manuscript, from the raw per-sample .tsv files
# where they are available and from the released parsed files otherwise.
# Chunks run top to bottom in manuscript order. Each chunk starts with a
# comment block that states its purpose, its inputs and its outputs.
#
# Outputs
#   figures/                main figures (PNG at 600 dpi and SVG)
#   figures/supplemental/   supplementary figures, plus one CSV per
#                           supplementary table and the combined workbook
#                           Supplementary_Tables.xlsx
#   stats/                  intermediate results (.rds and .csv) that
#                           manuscript-stats reads back
#   analysis/               internal checks that are not in the manuscript
#
# Packages from CRAN: tidyverse, janitor, fs, cowplot, svglite, gtable,
# vegan, ape, lme4, glmmTMB, ggtext, ggnewscale, lubridate, scatterpie,
# maps, openxlsx, png, officer. rphylopic is optional (Figure 6 silhouettes).

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(stringr)
library(fs)
library(cowplot)
library(svglite)
library(gtable)
library(vegan)       # PERMANOVA, betadisper, envfit
library(ape)         # pcoa()
library(lme4)        # glmer() for the virus-host models
library(glmmTMB)     # per-taxon mixed models
library(ggtext)      # markdown text in strips and labels
library(ggnewscale)  # second fill scale in the heatmaps
library(lubridate)
library(scatterpie)  # Figure 7 pies
library(maps)        # Figure 7 basemap (map_data). maps masks purrr::map,
                     # so purrr::map() is always written out in full.
library(openxlsx)    # supplementary tables workbook

# ---- Paths --------------------------------------------------------------
# All raw input files (the .tsv files plus the metadata/label CSVs) live
# directly in working_dir. The raw .tsv files are read from
# Samples_for_Paper.zip without unzipping it. If the zip is not there, the
# unzipped Samples_for_Paper folder is used instead. Everything this file
# produces is split into subfolders by type: parsed data, figures, stats,
# and analysis outputs.
# Folder that holds the input files. Change this if the inputs are
# somewhere other than the folder this file is knit from.
# ---- Private copy and public copy -------------------------------------------
# This script exists as two copies that differ only in PUBLIC_RELEASE below.
#   Figures_12S_Wastewater_private.Rmd  PUBLIC_RELEASE <- FALSE. Run by the
#       authors with every input file. Makes every figure, table and statistic,
#       and writes the release/ folder (release-files chunk, private copy only).
#   Figures_12S_Wastewater.Rmd          PUBLIC_RELEASE <- TRUE. Written by the
#       private copy into release/. Runs from the released files alone and
#       ignores every held-back file, even one that happens to be present.
#
# Released with the public copy (written to release/ by the private copy):
#   parsed/all_samples_parsed.csv, parsed/chordate_perfect_match.csv
#   site_labels_master.csv (site code, Table S1 name, state, region only)
#   supp_table_1_site.csv, taxon_common_names_lookup.csv
#   fish_taxa_classification_by_resolved_name.tsv
#   virus_weekly_reads.csv, passerivirus_a1_blast_results.tsv
#
# Held back, because they would identify treatment plants that asked not to
# be named, or show where plants are:
#   the raw per-sample files and sample_metadata.csv (raw reads are in the
#       SRA under the accession in the Data availability statement)
#   the crosswalks from each utility's own site labels to the site codes used
#       here (site, dashboard and BLAST label maps)
#   the metagenomic dashboard export (virus_weekly_reads.csv holds the same
#       numbers)
#   plant coordinates
# Without coordinates the public copy skips the Figure 7a map and fits
# Supplementary Figure (pcoa_site_metadata) without latitude and longitude.
# Every other figure, table and statistic is the same in both copies.

working_dir <- "."

# TRUE in the public copy, FALSE in the private copy (see header)
PUBLIC_RELEASE <- TRUE
data_zip    <- file.path(working_dir, "Samples_for_Paper.zip")  # raw .tsv files (zipped)
data_dir    <- file.path(working_dir, "Samples_for_Paper")      # raw .tsv files (unzipped)
parsed_dir  <- file.path(working_dir, "parsed")
fig_dir     <- file.path(working_dir, "figures")
stats_dir   <- file.path(working_dir, "stats")
supp_dir    <- file.path(fig_dir, "supplemental")
analysis_dir <- file.path(working_dir, "analysis")

dir_create(parsed_dir)
dir_create(fig_dir)
dir_create(stats_dir)
dir_create(supp_dir)
dir_create(analysis_dir)

metadata_path     <- file.path(working_dir, "sample_metadata.csv")
labels_path       <- file.path(working_dir, "site_labels_master.csv")
parsed_path       <- file.path(parsed_dir, "all_samples_parsed.csv")
chordate_path     <- file.path(parsed_dir, "chordate_perfect_match.csv")
# Fish classification (figure5-fish)
fish_taxon_resolved_path <- file.path(working_dir, "fish_taxa_classification_by_resolved_name.tsv")
taxon_common_names_path <- file.path(working_dir, "taxon_common_names_lookup.csv")

# ---- Minimum reads per sequence per sample ---------------------------------
# Used by parse-raw-tsvs, which drops chordate rows below this count when it
# writes chordate_perfect_match.csv. apply_standard_filter() (post-parse
# chunk) applies the same threshold again.
MIN_READS <- 8

# ---- Figure standards and saving helper ------------------------------------
# Nature Communications: 88 mm (single column), 136 mm (1.5 column) or
# 180 mm (double column) wide, at most 170 mm tall. Each figure is set to
# the smallest of these sizes at which its text does not overlap. Text 5-7 pt, bold panel letters 8 pt, lines
# 0.25-1 pt. Supplementary figures use the same width and fit on one page.
# save_figure() writes a 600 dpi PNG and an SVG at the same size, and warns
# when a figure is larger than these limits.
# Shared text sizes (pt). Dense labels (many sites or taxa) use FONT_SMALL.
FONT_BASE  <- 6.5
FONT_AXIS  <- 6
FONT_TITLE <- 6.5
FONT_SMALL <- 5

FIG_MAX_WIDTH_MM       <- 180
FIG_MAX_HEIGHT_MM      <- 170
FIG_MAX_HEIGHT_SUPP_MM <- 230
FIG_PANEL_LABEL_PT     <- 8

# Grey line showing each site's sampling period, drawn behind detections in
# the site-by-date figures (Figures 6 and 7b).
SAMPLING_RANGE_COLOR <- "grey55"
SAMPLING_RANGE_WIDTH <- 0.35
SAMPLING_RANGE_ALPHA <- 0.4   # lines are drawn faint so detection dots on top stay visible

save_figure <- function(plot, name, width, height, dir = fig_dir, units = "mm", dpi = 600) {
  max_h <- if (dir == supp_dir) FIG_MAX_HEIGHT_SUPP_MM else FIG_MAX_HEIGHT_MM
  if (dir != analysis_dir && (width > FIG_MAX_WIDTH_MM || height > max_h)) {
    warning(sprintf("%s is %g x %g mm; limit is %g x %g mm.", name, width, height, FIG_MAX_WIDTH_MM, max_h))
  }
  ggsave(file.path(dir, paste0(name, ".png")), plot, width = width, height = height, units = units, dpi = dpi)
  ggsave(file.path(dir, paste0(name, ".svg")), plot, width = width, height = height, units = units)
}

# ---- Figure and supplementary table numbering -------------------------------
# Every figure and supplementary table is numbered from the vectors below,
# in the order each is first cited in the manuscript. To renumber, reorder
# a vector here. File names, the workbook sheet names and the contents sheet
# all follow, so nothing else needs to change.
MAIN_FIGURES <- c(
  sample_collection          = "Sample collection timeline",
  composition                = "Vertebrate composition by site",
  distinctiveness_similarity = "Taxon distinctiveness and site similarity",
  pcoa_drivers               = "Sample-level Jaccard PCoA and what its axes track",
  fish                       = "Fish composition by production origin and habitat",
  distinctive_detections     = "Site-specific detections",
  rats                       = "Rattus species by site",
  temporal_variation         = "Temporal variation in detection of wild taxa",
  virus_host                 = "Virus detections and host nucleic acid"
)
SUPP_FIGURES <- c(
  composition_with_without_human = "Pooled class composition with and without human reads",
  boston_detections              = "All detections over time, Boston DITP North and Boston DITP South",
  hawaii_detections              = "All detections over time, Hawaii County and Kauai County",
  alpha_diversity                = "Shannon diversity and evenness by site",
  pcoa_by_site                   = "Jaccard PCoA, one panel per site",
  fish_dominated_samples         = "Fish-dominated samples on the Jaccard PCoA",
  pcoa_site_metadata             = "Site metadata fitted onto the Jaccard PCoA",
  bray_curtis_pcoa               = "Bray-Curtis PCoA and what its axes track",
  rat_species_virus_weeks        = "Rat species detected in weeks with each rat virus"
)
SUPP_TABLES <- c(
  sites               = "Sampling sites",
  composition         = "Read composition by site, with and without human reads",
  taxa_by_site        = "Taxa by number of sites detected",
  alpha_diversity     = "Alpha diversity tests",
  jaccard_similarity  = "Pairwise Jaccard similarity between sites",
  fish_classification = "Fish taxon classification by production origin and habitat",
  fish_by_site        = "Fish composition by site",
  notable_detections  = "Site-specific detections",
  rats_by_site        = "Rattus species composition by site and metro area",
  per_taxon_glmm      = "Per-taxon mixed models: site and sampling month",
  elevated_months     = "Months with elevated detection for wild taxa",
  virus_host          = "Virus detections and host nucleic acid in paired site-weeks"
)

fig_file <- function(id) {
  n <- match(id, names(MAIN_FIGURES))
  if (is.na(n)) stop("Unknown figure id: ", id)
  paste0("figure", n, "_", id)
}
supp_fig_file <- function(id) {
  n <- match(id, names(SUPP_FIGURES))
  if (is.na(n)) stop("Unknown supplementary figure id: ", id)
  paste0("supp_fig", n, "_", id)
}
supp_table_path <- function(id) {
  n <- match(id, names(SUPP_TABLES))
  if (is.na(n)) stop("Unknown supplementary table id: ", id)
  file.path(supp_dir, sprintf("supp_table_S%d_%s.csv", n, id))
}

# Figure and table names as the manuscript writes them, numbered from the
# vectors above, in Nature Portfolio style ("Supplementary Table 12",
# "Supplementary Fig. 5"). CSV file names keep an S prefix
# (supp_table_S12_*.csv) so they sort correctly on disk. Every table
# description and printed label uses these, so reordering a vector
# renumbers the text too.
fig_ref <- function(id) {
  n <- match(id, names(MAIN_FIGURES))
  if (is.na(n)) stop("Unknown figure id: ", id)
  paste("Fig.", n)
}
supp_fig_ref <- function(id) {
  n <- match(id, names(SUPP_FIGURES))
  if (is.na(n)) stop("Unknown supplementary figure id: ", id)
  paste0("Supplementary Fig. ", n)
}
supp_table_ref <- function(id) {
  n <- match(id, names(SUPP_TABLES))
  if (is.na(n)) stop("Unknown supplementary table id: ", id)
  paste0("Supplementary Table ", n)
}

# Each chunk that makes a supplementary table registers it here. The table
# is written as a CSV right away, and supp-tables-workbook later writes all
# registered tables into one Excel file, one sheet per table, with a
# contents sheet. description is the note printed above the table in its
# sheet: what one row is, what the columns mean, and how values were
# calculated.
supp_table_registry <- list()
add_supp_table <- function(id, data, description) {
  write_csv(data, supp_table_path(id), na = "")
  supp_table_registry[[id]] <<- list(data = data, description = description)
  invisible(data)
}

# Same shape as add_supp_table(), for tables that are kept in the repository
# but are not part of the manuscript. Writes to analysis/ and does NOT
# register, so the table never reaches the supplementary workbook and never
# takes a supplementary table number. description is written beside the CSV
# so the file is self-documenting.
add_analysis_table <- function(id, data, description) {
  write_csv(data, file.path(analysis_dir, paste0(id, ".csv")), na = "")
  writeLines(description, file.path(analysis_dir, paste0(id, "_description.txt")))
  invisible(data)
}

# ---- Region / site ordering, shared across figures ------------------------
REGION_MAP <- c(MA = "Northeast", IL = "Midwest", IA = "Midwest", MO = "Midwest",
                FL = "South", TX = "South", CA = "West", ID = "West", HI = "West")
REGION_ORDER <- c("Northeast", "Midwest", "South", "West")
STATE_COLORS <- c(
  MA = "#4B91C3", # blue
  IA = "#A0786E", # muted brown/rose
  IL = "#55AF55", # green
  MO = "#DC5050", # red
  FL = "#A582C8", # purple
  TX = "#C8C84B", # olive-yellow
  CA = "#FF963C", # orange
  HI = "#32A0A0", # teal
  ID = "#E691CD"  # pink/magenta
)
# Order above matches region, then state alphabetically within region, the
# same order the site axis uses everywhere else. Any scale_*_manual() using
# STATE_COLORS should also set limits = names(STATE_COLORS) so the legend
# follows this order too, since ggplot otherwise sorts a character column
# alphabetically regardless of this vector's order.

# ---- Vertebrate class colors, shared across figures ------------------------
# One color per class (Mammal/Bird/Fish/Other), used by every figure so a
# class is the same color everywhere. CLASS_STEPS gives darker-to-lighter
# shades within each class for figures that split a class into taxa.
CLASS_COLORS <- c(Mammal = "#B12694", Bird = "#0F8C5D", Fish = "#3959EA", Other = "#8B8B8B")
CLASS_STEPS <- list(
  Mammal = c("#B12694", "#DC4CAE", "#FD7EC4", "#FEC5DB"),
  Bird   = c("#0F8C5D", "#20B36B", "#48DA78"),
  Fish   = c("#3959EA", "#6887FD", "#A2B6FF"),
  Other  = c("#8B8B8B")
)
# ---- Site names (Table S1) ----------------------------------------------------
# Table S1 (supp_table_1_site.csv) is the hand-made site table. Its site names
# are the names each sewershed approved, and every figure and table uses
# them. site_table links Table S1 to the site IDs in the data
# (current_site_label in site_labels_master.csv). A site whose name differs
# between the two files is matched by state when it is the only site in
# that state.
# Hand-made input file, kept with the other inputs in working_dir.
# Site identity is held in input files rather than in this script. Several
# utilities asked that their plant not be named, so the site codes used here
# carry no plant, city or street name, and the crosswalks that would reveal
# one (plant coordinates, the metagenomic dashboard's own site codes, and the
# raw sample labels in the Passerivirus BLAST file) are read from files that
# are not released with this script. Every figure and table is produced from
# the site names each utility approved, which are in Table S1.
MANUAL_COORDS_FILE      <- "site_coords_manual.csv"       # current_site_label, lat, lon
DASHBOARD_SITE_MAP_FILE <- "dashboard_site_map.csv"       # dashboard_code, canonical_site
PASV_SITE_ALIAS_FILE    <- "passerivirus_site_aliases.csv" # blast_site_label, canonical_site
SITE_CODE_FILE          <- "site_code_map.csv"            # raw_site_label, canonical_site
# Each of these is optional. See the header for what is skipped without it.
has_private_file <- function(f) !PUBLIC_RELEASE && file.exists(file.path(working_dir, f))

# Raw sample filenames carry each utility's own site label. recode_site()
# turns those into the site codes used throughout this script, and is applied
# wherever site labels first enter the data. Labels that are not in the map
# pass through unchanged.
SITE_CODE_MAP <- if (has_private_file(SITE_CODE_FILE)) {
  k <- read_csv(file.path(working_dir, SITE_CODE_FILE), show_col_types = FALSE)
  setNames(k$canonical_site, k$raw_site_label)
} else {
  character(0)   # released parsed files already carry the site codes
}
recode_site <- function(x) {
  hit <- match(x, names(SITE_CODE_MAP))
  ifelse(is.na(hit), x, unname(SITE_CODE_MAP)[hit])
}

TABLE_S1_PATH <- file.path(working_dir, "supp_table_1_site.csv")
supp_table_site_metadata <- read_csv(TABLE_S1_PATH, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  # Published as study start and study end: the first and last collection date
  # at the site. Older column names in supp_table_1_site.csv still work.
  rename(any_of(c(`Study start` = "Collection start", `Study end` = "Collection end")))

labels_key <- read_csv(labels_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  select(canonical_site = current_site_label, label_name = shorthand_for_figures, state)
one_site_states <- labels_key %>% count(state) %>% filter(n == 1) %>% pull(state)

# Population served as written in Table S1: "1.1M" -> 1100000, "26k" -> 26000
parse_pop <- function(x) {
  x <- str_trim(as.character(x))
  mult <- case_when(str_detect(x, "[Mm]$") ~ 1e6, str_detect(x, "[Kk]$") ~ 1e3, TRUE ~ 1)
  suppressWarnings(as.numeric(str_remove(x, "[MmKk]$"))) * mult
}

site_table <- supp_table_site_metadata %>%
  left_join(labels_key %>% select(canonical_site, Site = label_name), by = "Site") %>%
  left_join(labels_key %>% filter(state %in% one_site_states) %>%
              select(State = state, by_state = canonical_site), by = "State") %>%
  mutate(canonical_site = coalesce(canonical_site, by_state),
         region     = factor(Region, levels = REGION_ORDER),
         system     = str_remove(`Sewer system type`, "(?i)\\s*sewer system$"),
         population = parse_pop(`Population served`)) %>%
  select(-by_state)

unmatched <- site_table$Site[is.na(site_table$canonical_site)]
if (length(unmatched) > 0) stop("Table S1 sites not matched to the data: ", paste(unmatched, collapse = ", "))

# Every site in Table S1 must have these fields filled in. Population
# served may be blank for sites that do not report it (those sites are left
# out of anything that uses population).
TABLE_S1_REQUIRED <- intersect(c("Site", "Region", "State", "Sample type", "Sewer system type",
                                 "Local collection partner", "Study start", "Study end",
                                 "n samples"),
                               names(supp_table_site_metadata))
incomplete_s1 <- supp_table_site_metadata %>%
  filter(if_any(all_of(TABLE_S1_REQUIRED), ~ is.na(.x) | as.character(.x) == "")) %>%
  pull(Site)
if (length(incomplete_s1) > 0) {
  stop("Table S1 has missing values for: ", paste(incomplete_s1, collapse = ", "))
}

add_supp_table("sites", supp_table_site_metadata,
  paste("One row per sampling site (wastewater treatment plant or sewershed).",
        "Site names are the names approved by each utility and are used in every figure and table.",
        "Population served is as reported by the utility; blank where not reported.",
        "Sewer system type: combined systems carry both sewage and stormwater; sanitary",
        "systems carry sewage only. Study start and study end are the first and last",
        "collection dates at the site. n samples counts one sample per site and",
        "collection date, after technical replicates were merged."))

# ---- Site coordinates ---------------------------------------------------------
# Latitude and longitude for every site, from lat_lon in
# site_labels_master.csv (degrees north, then degrees west, e.g. "dd.dd N ddd.dd W"). MANUAL_COORDS fills sites
# where that field is missing or describes a county rather than a plant.
# Used by the Figure 7 map and the site-metadata ordination.
MANUAL_COORDS <- if (has_private_file(MANUAL_COORDS_FILE)) {
  m <- read_csv(file.path(working_dir, MANUAL_COORDS_FILE), show_col_types = FALSE)
  stopifnot(all(c("current_site_label", "lat", "lon") %in% names(m)))
  m %>% mutate(current_site_label = recode_site(current_site_label))
} else {
  tibble(current_site_label = character(), lat = numeric(), lon = numeric())
}
parse_lat_lon <- function(s) {
  parts <- str_match(s, "([\\d.]+)\\s*N\\s+([\\d.]+)\\s*W")
  tibble(lat = as.numeric(parts[, 2]), lon = -as.numeric(parts[, 3]))
}

# ---- Shared colors -------------------------------------------------------------
# Color rules for every figure:
#   STATE_COLORS   anything drawn per site or sample (sites are never colored
#                  by region; region is shown by grouping, header bands or
#                  ellipse line type)
#   CLASS_COLORS / CLASS_STEPS   vertebrate class and taxa within a class
#   HEAT_12S_COLORS  every 12S heatmap and the 12S host line in Figure 9
#   HEAT_VIRUS_COLORS  every virus heatmap and virus line in Figure 9
#   greys          neutral elements (sampling ranges, fits, gaps, "not" groups)
HEADER_FILL <- "#F2E2B8"   # region header bands (Figures 1 and 2)
GAP_FILL    <- "#D6DCE5"   # no sample that week (site-by-week heatmaps)
HEAT_12S_COLORS   <- c("#FFEDA0", "#FED976", "#FD8D3C", "#E31A1C", "#800026")
HEAT_VIRUS_COLORS <- c("#bfd3e6", "#9ebcda", "#8c96c6", "#8856a7", "#810f7c")
# Region ellipses in the site-metadata ordination (line type, not color)
REGION_LINETYPES <- c(Northeast = "solid", Midwest = "longdash", South = "dotted", West = "dotdash")

# Heatmap tiles: every tile, including empty and unsampled ones, gets a
# thin grey border so rows and columns can be followed by eye.
HEAT_GRID_COLOR <- "grey80"
HEAT_GRID_WIDTH <- 0.12

# Padding inside every boxed legend (top, right, bottom, left, in pt)
LEGEND_BOX_MARGIN <- margin(3, 4, 5, 4)

# Common-name lookup, read the same way by every chunk. A scientific name
# listed twice would duplicate rows in every table it is joined to, so only
# the first entry is kept and the duplicates are named in a warning.
read_common_names <- function() {
  cn <- read_csv(taxon_common_names_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  dup <- unique(cn$scientific_name[duplicated(cn$scientific_name)])
  if (length(dup) > 0) {
    warning(basename(taxon_common_names_path), " lists these names more than once (first entry kept): ",
            paste(dup, collapse = ", "))
  }
  distinct(cn, scientific_name, .keep_all = TRUE)
}

# Site labels file with shorthand_for_figures replaced by the Table S1 name.
# Every chunk reads site labels through this function.
read_site_labels <- function() {
  read_csv(labels_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    left_join(site_table %>% select(current_site_label = canonical_site, s1_name = Site),
              by = "current_site_label") %>%
    mutate(shorthand_for_figures = coalesce(s1_name, shorthand_for_figures)) %>%
    select(-s1_name, -any_of(if (PUBLIC_RELEASE) "lat_lon" else character(0)))
}
```


```{r parse-raw-tsvs}
# Reads the raw per-sample .tsv files, when they are present, and writes
# two CSVs used by every chunk below:
#   all_samples_parsed.csv     every zOTU and the ranks it resolved to
#   chordate_perfect_match.csv chordate, perfect-match zOTUs with at least
#                              MIN_READS reads
# No rank or date filtering happens here. That is done downstream by
# apply_standard_filter() (post-parse-filters), so these files stay general.

# Reparsing needs the raw files and sample_metadata.csv, neither of which is
# released. When they are absent, the parsed files from a previous run are
# used, which is what a clone of this repository does.
REPARSE <- !PUBLIC_RELEASE && file.exists(metadata_path) && (file_exists(data_zip) || dir_exists(data_dir))
if (!REPARSE) {
  if (!file.exists(chordate_path) || !file.exists(parsed_path)) {
    stop("Neither the raw files nor parsed/ are present. See the header of this script.")
  }
  message("Raw files not present; using parsed/ from a previous run. ",
          "Raw reads are in the SRA, see Data availability.")
  all_parsed       <- read_csv(parsed_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  chordate_perfect <- read_csv(chordate_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
}

if (REPARSE) {

# ---- sample_metadata.csv ---------------------------------------------------
# Generated by generate_sample_metadata.py whenever new .tsv files are added
# to Samples_for_Paper. The date cutoff, exclusions, and category are set
# there. Only category == "main" is applied again here.
metadata_all <- read_csv(metadata_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>% clean_names()
metadata <- metadata_all %>% filter(category == "main")

# ---- Raw file source ---------------------------------------------------------
# Raw .tsv files are read straight from Samples_for_Paper.zip (data_zip),
# one file at a time, without unzipping. If the zip is not found, the
# unzipped Samples_for_Paper folder (data_dir) is read instead. Files are
# matched to sample_metadata.csv by file name, so it does not matter
# whether the zip stores them at its top level or inside a folder.
use_zip <- file_exists(data_zip)
if (use_zip) {
  zip_index <- utils::unzip(data_zip, list = TRUE) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    filter(str_detect(Name, "\\.tsv$"),
           !str_detect(Name, "(^|/)__MACOSX/"),   # macOS zip metadata
           !str_detect(Name, "(^|/)\\._")) %>%   # macOS resource-fork files
    mutate(filename = path_file(Name))
  dup_names <- unique(zip_index$filename[duplicated(zip_index$filename)])
  if (length(dup_names) > 0) {
    stop(length(dup_names), " file name(s) appear more than once in ", data_zip, ":\n",
         paste(head(dup_names, 10), collapse = "\n"))
  }
  raw_tsv_files <- zip_index$filename
  raw_source    <- data_zip
} else if (dir_exists(data_dir)) {
  raw_tsv_files <- path_file(dir_ls(data_dir, glob = "*.tsv"))
  raw_source    <- data_dir
} else {
  stop("Raw .tsv files not found. Expected ", data_zip, " or the folder ", data_dir, ".")
}
cat("Reading raw .tsv files from", raw_source, "\n")

# Path to each raw file: the entry name inside the zip, or the file path
# in the folder.
raw_file_path <- function(filename) {
  if (use_zip) zip_index$Name[match(filename, zip_index$filename)] else path(data_dir, filename)
}
# Open a raw file for reading. Inside the zip this is an unz() connection.
open_raw <- function(path) if (use_zip) unz(data_zip, path) else path

# Stop if a raw file is missing from the manifest. This usually means
# sample_metadata.csv is out of date.
unlisted_files  <- setdiff(raw_tsv_files, metadata_all$filename)
if (length(unlisted_files) > 0) {
  stop(
    length(unlisted_files), " .tsv file(s) in ", raw_source, " are not in sample_metadata.csv ",
    "(any category):\n", paste(head(unlisted_files, 10), collapse = "\n"),
    if (length(unlisted_files) > 10) "\n...(truncated)" else "",
    "\n\nRegenerate sample_metadata.csv (generate_sample_metadata.py) and re-knit."
  )
}

# well and s_number are identifiers, so they are read as character. Merged
# replicate rows set them to NA below.
metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    filename       = as.character(filename),
    well           = as.character(well),
    s_number       = as.character(s_number),
    replicate_flag = as.logical(replicate_flag)
  )

cat("Manifest after filtering:", nrow(metadata), "files\n")

missing    <- setdiff(metadata$filename, raw_tsv_files)
if (length(missing) > 0) {
  warning(
    length(missing), " files listed in metadata are missing from ", raw_source, ":\n",
    paste(head(missing, 10), collapse = "\n"),
    if (length(missing) > 10) "\n...(truncated)" else ""
  )
}
metadata   <- metadata %>% filter(filename %in% raw_tsv_files)
file_paths <- raw_file_path(metadata$filename)

# ---- Taxonomy string parsing helpers --------------------------------------

nzchar_or_empty <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "", x)

extract_rank_candidates <- function(x, rank) {
  x <- nzchar_or_empty(x)
  pattern <- paste0("(?i)(?<![A-Za-z])", rank, "_([^;,:]+)")
  mats <- str_match_all(x, pattern)
  lapply(mats, function(m) if (!length(m)) character(0) else unique(trimws(m[, 2])))
}

last_token <- function(x) {
  x <- nzchar_or_empty(x)
  sapply(strsplit(x, ";", fixed = TRUE), function(v) {
    if (length(v) == 0) NA_character_ else trimws(v[length(v)])
  })
}

extract_species_candidates <- function(x) {
  tok <- last_token(x)
  mats <- str_match_all(tok, "\\b([A-Z][a-z][A-Za-z-]*\\s[a-z][a-z-]+)\\b")
  lapply(mats, function(m) if (!length(m)) character(0) else unique(m[, 2]))
}

# A rank resolves only when there is exactly one candidate name for it.
# More than one candidate means the reference match was ambiguous, so the
# rank is left NA.
pick_unambig <- function(cand_vec) if (length(cand_vec) == 1) cand_vec[1] else NA_character_

is_perfect  <- function(x) str_to_lower(nzchar_or_empty(x)) %in% c("p", "pu")
is_multiple <- function(x) str_to_lower(nzchar_or_empty(x)) == "m"
is_chordate <- function(phylum_vec) phylum_vec == "Chordata"

raw_col_names <- c("perfect_flag", "multiple_flag", "taxonomy", "zotu_size", "sequence")
raw_col_types <- cols(.default = col_character())

# Some files have a header row and some do not. The first line is checked
# for "sequence" to tell them apart. Source files are never modified.
read_raw_file <- function(path, meta_row) {
  first_line <- read_lines(open_raw(path), n_max = 1)
  has_header <- str_detect(first_line, regex("sequence", ignore_case = TRUE))

  raw <- if (has_header) {
    suppressWarnings(read_tsv(open_raw(path), col_names = raw_col_names, col_types = raw_col_types, skip = 1))
  } else {
    suppressWarnings(read_tsv(open_raw(path), col_names = raw_col_names, col_types = raw_col_types))
  }

  zotu_id <- str_extract(raw$zotu_size, "^[^;]+")
  reads   <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(str_match(raw$zotu_size, "(?i)size=(\\d+)")[, 2]))

  tibble(
    filename       = meta_row$filename,
    canonical_site = meta_row$canonical_site,
    state          = meta_row$state,
    city           = meta_row$city,
    sewershed      = meta_row$sewershed,
    date           = meta_row$date,
    well           = meta_row$well,
    s_number       = meta_row$s_number,
    replicate_flag = meta_row$replicate_flag,

    zotu_id  = zotu_id,
    reads    = reads,
    sequence = raw$sequence,

    perfect_flag_raw  = raw$perfect_flag,
    multiple_flag_raw = raw$multiple_flag,
    taxonomy          = raw$taxonomy
  )
}

raw_list <- map2(
  file_paths,
  split(metadata, seq_len(nrow(metadata))),
  ~ read_raw_file(.x, .y),
  .progress = TRUE
)

all_raw <- list_rbind(raw_list)
cat("Read", nrow(all_raw), "raw rows from", nrow(metadata), "files\n")

# ---- Collapse same-site, same-date replicates --------------------------------
# Two or more raw files with the same canonical_site and date are repeat
# reactions of one sample, so they are merged into one sample here, by
# sequence, before taxonomy is resolved. Reads for a sequence are averaged
# only over the files where that sequence was found. filename, well, and
# s_number are set to NA for merged rows; canonical_site + date identifies
# a sample from here on. Sites sampled on different dates in the same week
# are not merged.

all_raw <- all_raw %>%
  group_by(canonical_site, date) %>%
  mutate(n_files_in_group = n_distinct(filename)) %>%
  ungroup()

n_multi_file_groups <- all_raw %>%
  distinct(canonical_site, date, n_files_in_group) %>%
  filter(n_files_in_group > 1) %>%
  nrow()
cat(n_multi_file_groups, "site+date combinations have >1 contributing file and will be collapsed\n")

singletons <- all_raw %>%
  filter(n_files_in_group == 1) %>%
  select(-n_files_in_group) %>%
  mutate(n_source_files = 1L)

collapsed <- all_raw %>%
  filter(n_files_in_group > 1) %>%
  group_by(canonical_site, state, city, sewershed, date, sequence) %>%
  summarise(
    reads              = mean(reads, na.rm = TRUE),
    zotu_id            = first(zotu_id),
    perfect_flag_raw   = first(perfect_flag_raw),
    multiple_flag_raw  = first(multiple_flag_raw),
    taxonomy           = first(taxonomy),
    n_source_files     = n_distinct(filename),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    filename       = NA_character_,
    well           = NA_character_,
    s_number       = NA_character_,
    replicate_flag = NA
  )

all_raw_collapsed <- bind_rows(singletons, collapsed)
cat("After collapsing:", nrow(all_raw_collapsed), "rows (from", nrow(all_raw), "pre-collapse)\n")

# ---- Taxonomy resolution ----------------------------------------------------
# Each rank resolves when there is exactly one candidate name; otherwise it
# is NA. resolved_rank and resolved_name are the finest rank that resolved.

taxonomy_vec <- all_raw_collapsed$taxonomy

k_cand <- extract_rank_candidates(taxonomy_vec, "kingdom")
p_cand <- extract_rank_candidates(taxonomy_vec, "phylum")
c_cand <- extract_rank_candidates(taxonomy_vec, "class")
o_cand <- extract_rank_candidates(taxonomy_vec, "order")
f_cand <- extract_rank_candidates(taxonomy_vec, "family")
g_cand <- extract_rank_candidates(taxonomy_vec, "genus")
s_cand <- extract_species_candidates(taxonomy_vec)

k_uni <- vapply(k_cand, pick_unambig, character(1)); k_n <- vapply(k_cand, length, integer(1))
p_uni <- vapply(p_cand, pick_unambig, character(1)); p_n <- vapply(p_cand, length, integer(1))
c_uni <- vapply(c_cand, pick_unambig, character(1)); c_n <- vapply(c_cand, length, integer(1))
o_uni <- vapply(o_cand, pick_unambig, character(1)); o_n <- vapply(o_cand, length, integer(1))
f_uni <- vapply(f_cand, pick_unambig, character(1)); f_n <- vapply(f_cand, length, integer(1))
g_uni <- vapply(g_cand, pick_unambig, character(1)); g_n <- vapply(g_cand, length, integer(1))
s_uni <- vapply(s_cand, pick_unambig, character(1)); s_n <- vapply(s_cand, length, integer(1))

perfect  <- is_perfect(all_raw_collapsed$perfect_flag_raw)
multiple <- is_multiple(all_raw_collapsed$multiple_flag_raw)
phylum   <- ifelse(p_n == 1, p_uni, NA_character_)
chordate <- is_chordate(phylum)

all_parsed <- all_raw_collapsed %>%
  mutate(canonical_site = recode_site(canonical_site)) %>%
  transmute(
    filename, canonical_site, state, city, sewershed, date, well, s_number,
    replicate_flag, n_source_files,

    zotu_id  = zotu_id,
    reads    = reads,
    sequence = sequence,

    perfect  = perfect,
    multiple = multiple,
    chordate = chordate,

    kingdom = ifelse(k_n == 1, k_uni, NA_character_),
    phylum  = phylum,
    class   = ifelse(c_n == 1, c_uni, NA_character_),
    order   = ifelse(o_n == 1, o_uni, NA_character_),
    family  = ifelse(f_n == 1, f_uni, NA_character_),
    genus   = ifelse(g_n == 1, g_uni, NA_character_),
    species = ifelse(s_n == 1, s_uni, NA_character_),

    resolved_rank = case_when(
      s_n == 1 ~ "species",
      g_n == 1 ~ "genus",
      f_n == 1 ~ "family",
      o_n == 1 ~ "order",
      c_n == 1 ~ "class",
      p_n == 1 ~ "phylum",
      k_n == 1 ~ "kingdom",
      TRUE     ~ NA_character_
    ),
    resolved_name = case_when(
      resolved_rank == "species" ~ species,
      resolved_rank == "genus"   ~ genus,
      resolved_rank == "family"  ~ family,
      resolved_rank == "order"   ~ order,
      resolved_rank == "class"   ~ class,
      resolved_rank == "phylum"  ~ phylum,
      resolved_rank == "kingdom" ~ kingdom,
      TRUE                       ~ NA_character_
    ),

    taxonomy_raw = taxonomy_vec,
    kingdom_n = k_n, phylum_n = p_n, class_n = c_n, order_n = o_n,
    family_n = f_n, genus_n = g_n, species_n = s_n
  )

write_csv(all_parsed, parsed_path)
cat("Wrote", nrow(all_parsed), "rows to", parsed_path, "\n")

# ---- Chordate + perfect-match subset ---------------------------------------
chordate_perfect <- all_parsed %>%
  filter(chordate, perfect, reads >= MIN_READS)

write_csv(chordate_perfect, chordate_path)
cat("Chordate + perfect-match rows (reads >=", MIN_READS, "):", nrow(chordate_perfect),
    "of", nrow(all_parsed), "total\n")

}   # end if (REPARSE)

# Read totals for the manuscript. These are reads assigned to zOTUs after
# denoising and replicate merging, not raw sequencing reads.
read_totals <- tibble(
  samples            = n_distinct(paste(all_parsed$canonical_site, all_parsed$date)),
  sites              = n_distinct(all_parsed$canonical_site),
  zotu_reads_total   = sum(all_parsed$reads, na.rm = TRUE),
  chordate_reads     = sum(all_parsed$reads[all_parsed$chordate %in% TRUE], na.rm = TRUE),
  chordate_perfect_reads = sum(chordate_perfect$reads, na.rm = TRUE)
)
write_csv(read_totals, file.path(stats_dir, "read_totals.csv"))
```


```{r post-parse-filters}
# =========================================================================
# Post-parse filters and taxon handling, used by every chunk below
# =========================================================================
# Everything here works on the parsed data (chordate_perfect_match.csv),
# so it is defined after parse-raw-tsvs.

# ---- Detection filter -------------------------------------------------------
# A sequence needs at least MIN_READS reads (setup chunk) on a given date to
# count, and has to clear that bar on at least MIN_DATES separate sampling
# dates at a site before it is treated as a real detection there. The same
# rule applies at every rank. Sequences that resolve to the same name are
# tracked separately here and only summed once something downstream reports
# by name. Only family, genus and species calls are kept; order, class,
# phylum and kingdom calls are too coarse for a site fingerprint or a
# named detection.
#
# The study window (STUDY_START_DATE to STUDY_END_DATE) is enforced in
# wastewater_lib.py, so samples outside it never reach the parsed data.
# apply_standard_filter() also drops anything after STUDY_END_DATE as a
# safety check. STUDY_START_DATE sets the left edge of the time axis in the
# time-series figures.
RANKS_KEEP <- c("family", "genus", "species")
MIN_DATES  <- 3
STUDY_START_DATE <- as.Date("2025-03-30")  # Sunday of the first study week (Mar 30 - Apr 5, 2025)
STUDY_END_DATE   <- as.Date("2026-09-05")  # Saturday of the last study week, inclusive

# Weeks run Sunday to Saturday, starting on STUDY_START_DATE. Every weekly
# bin and time axis uses these.
study_week  <- function(d) floor_date(as.Date(d), "week", week_start = 7)
STUDY_WEEKS <- seq(STUDY_START_DATE, study_week(STUDY_END_DATE), by = "7 days")
stopifnot(weekdays(STUDY_START_DATE) == "Sunday")

# ---- Ambiguous-family exclusion ---------------------------------------------
# Family-level calls in these families cannot be assigned to one genus.
# Phasianidae: Gallus (chicken) vs. Meleagris (turkey).
# Bovidae: Bos (cattle) vs. Capra (goat) vs. Ovis (sheep) vs. other genera.
DROP_AMBIGUOUS_NAMED_FAMILIES <- c("Phasianidae", "Bovidae")

# ---- Curated genus-to-species merges ----------------------------------------
# A genus-level call is merged into its species only when the genus is
# biologically one animal in this context (Ovis = domestic sheep, Bos =
# domestic cattle), not merely because one species was detected. Genera
# with several plausible species (Canis: dog or wolf; Anas: several ducks,
# kept as its own ASV-level taxon; Larus, Sebastes, etc.) are NOT merged
# and stay as their own taxa. Applied by apply_standard_filter() AFTER the
# read and date checks, so filtering still runs on the original sequences
# and only the names are merged. merge = FALSE returns the original names
# (used by nested-taxa-review, which checks each merge against the BLAST
# tie set).
TAXON_MERGES <- c(Ovis = "Ovis aries", Bos = "Bos taurus")

merge_taxa <- function(data) {
  data %>%
    mutate(
      merge_to      = unname(TAXON_MERGES[resolved_name]),
      resolved_rank = if_else(!is.na(merge_to), "species", resolved_rank),
      species       = if_else(!is.na(merge_to), merge_to, species),
      resolved_name = coalesce(merge_to, resolved_name)
    ) %>%
    select(-merge_to)
}

apply_standard_filter <- function(data, min_reads = MIN_READS, min_dates = MIN_DATES,
                                  merge = TRUE) {
  passed <- data %>%
    filter(resolved_rank %in% RANKS_KEEP,
           reads >= min_reads,
           as.Date(date) <= STUDY_END_DATE)

  qualifying <- passed %>%
    distinct(canonical_site, sequence, date) %>%
    count(canonical_site, sequence, name = "n_dates") %>%
    filter(n_dates >= min_dates)

  result <- semi_join(passed, qualifying, by = c("canonical_site", "sequence"))
  if (merge) merge_taxa(result) else result
}

# ---- Filtered detections -------------------------------------------------------
# Every analysis starts from the same data: chordate_perfect_match.csv,
# with family-level Phasianidae and Bovidae calls dropped and the standard
# filter applied. drop_human removes human reads (genus Homo or family
# Hominidae, so reads resolved only to Hominidae are caught too).
is_human <- function(genus, family) {
  (!is.na(genus) & genus == "Homo") | (!is.na(family) & family == "Hominidae")
}

load_detections <- function(drop_human = TRUE, merge = TRUE) {
  d <- read_csv(chordate_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    filter(!(resolved_rank == "family" & family %in% DROP_AMBIGUOUS_NAMED_FAMILIES)) %>%
    mutate(date = as.Date(date), canonical_site = recode_site(canonical_site))
  if (drop_human) d <- d %>% filter(!is_human(genus, family))
  apply_standard_filter(d, merge = merge)
}

# ---- Broad vertebrate class grouping ---------------------------------------
# Groups detections into Mammal, Bird, Fish, and Other. Reptiles and
# amphibians are in Other. A few reptile calls (alligator, several turtles)
# have class = NA in the reference taxonomy but a reptile order (Testudines,
# Crocodylia); they are kept and fall into Other.
broad_cat <- function(class) {
  case_when(
    class == "Aves"                                                    ~ "Bird",
    class == "Mammalia"                                                ~ "Mammal",
    class %in% c("Actinopteri", "Actinopterygii", "Chondrichthyes",
                 "Cephalaspidomorphi")                                  ~ "Fish",
    TRUE                                                                ~ "Other"
  )
}

# ---- Site-occurrence bins (Figure 3a and fingerprint-stats) ----------------
# n = number of sites a taxon was detected at, including the site being
# plotted. Labels give that number, so the bins cover 1 to 27 sites with no
# gaps.
N_SITES_TOTAL <- 27

# This is the only definition of the bins. fingerprint-stats writes them
# into distinctiveness_data, and Figure 3a and Supplementary Table (taxa_by_site) read
# them from there, so the figure and the data cannot disagree. The last
# bin (all 27 sites) is also the set removed in the PERMANOVA sensitivity
# check (fingerprint-stats, section 1c).
DIST_LEVELS <- c(
  "1 site (unique)",                    # n = 1
  "2 sites",                            # n = 2
  "3-5 sites",                          # n = 3-5
  "6-13 sites",                         # n = 6-13
  "14-26 sites",                        # n = 14-26
  "All 27 sites"                        # n = 27
)

bin_occurrence_fig3a <- function(n) {
  case_when(
    n == 1                          ~ DIST_LEVELS[1],
    n == 2                          ~ DIST_LEVELS[2],
    n >= 3  & n <= 5                ~ DIST_LEVELS[3],
    n >= 6  & n <= 13               ~ DIST_LEVELS[4],
    n >= 14 & n <= 26               ~ DIST_LEVELS[5],
    n == N_SITES_TOTAL              ~ DIST_LEVELS[6]
  )
}

DIST_RARE_BINS   <- DIST_LEVELS[1:3]   # 1, 2, 3-5 sites
DIST_COMMON_BINS <- DIST_LEVELS[4:6]   # 6-13, 14-26, all 27 sites
DIST_COLORS <- setNames(
  c("#c51b7d", "#e9a3c9", "#fde0ef",   # rare: dark (1 site) to light (3-5)
    "#e6f5d0", "#a1d76a", "#4d9221"),  # common: light (6-13) to dark (all 27)
  DIST_LEVELS
)
```


```{r nested-taxa-review}
# =========================================================================
# Nested taxa review (analysis only, not in the manuscript)
# =========================================================================
# A sequence resolved only to genus or family can share its name with a
# finer taxon detected elsewhere in the data (e.g., Ovis and Ovis aries).
# Counted as separate taxa, one animal can count twice toward richness and
# the Jaccard and Bray-Curtis matrices. TAXON_MERGES (post-parse-filters)
# lists the genus-to-species merges that apply_standard_filter() makes.
# This chunk documents every nested sequence and checks those merges
# against BLAST.
#
# The last field of taxonomy_raw lists every name a sequence tied with in
# BLAST, as "name: n_hits, name: n_hits". The review table has one row per
# genus- or family-level sequence that has a finer relative in the data (a
# species in the same genus, or a genus or species in the same family),
# with its tie set and which finer relatives appear in it. Hit counts are
# shown but not used to decide anything, since they reflect how many
# reference sequences each species has in NCBI, not how likely it is to be
# the source.
#
# The table is built from the same data fingerprint-stats uses (ambiguous
# families and human removed, then the standard filter), but with
# merge = FALSE so the original names are visible. The chunk stops if a
# merged sequence's tie set does not contain its merge target, since
# merge_taxa() merges by name and would otherwise relabel it silently.
# Output: stats_dir/nested_taxa_review.csv

# ---- Parse the BLAST tie set from taxonomy_raw ------------------------------
# Rank prefixes (e.g., "genus_Columba", "no rank_...") are removed so tied
# names can be compared with resolved_name.
parse_tie_set <- function(taxonomy_raw) {
  last_field <- str_trim(str_extract(taxonomy_raw, "[^;]+$"))
  entries <- str_trim(str_split(last_field, ",")[[1]])
  tibble(
    tied_name = str_remove(str_trim(str_remove(entries, ":\\s*\\d+$")), "^[a-z ]+_"),
    n_hits    = as.integer(str_extract(entries, "\\d+$"))
  )
}

# ---- Data, filtered as in fingerprint-stats but not merged ------------------
review_input <- load_detections(merge = FALSE)

# ---- Finer relatives of each genus and family name ---------------------------
finer_lookup <- bind_rows(
  review_input %>%
    filter(resolved_rank == "species", !is.na(genus)) %>%
    distinct(parent = genus, finer = resolved_name) %>%
    mutate(parent_rank = "genus"),
  review_input %>%
    filter(resolved_rank %in% c("genus", "species"), !is.na(family)) %>%
    distinct(parent = family, finer = resolved_name) %>%
    mutate(parent_rank = "family")
)

# ---- Coarse sequences with at least one finer relative -----------------------
coarse_seqs <- review_input %>%
  filter(resolved_rank %in% c("genus", "family")) %>%
  group_by(sequence, resolved_name, resolved_rank) %>%
  summarise(
    n_sites            = n_distinct(canonical_site),
    reads              = sum(reads),
    n_taxonomy_strings = n_distinct(taxonomy_raw),
    taxonomy_raw       = first(taxonomy_raw),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  semi_join(finer_lookup, by = c("resolved_name" = "parent", "resolved_rank" = "parent_rank"))

if (any(coarse_seqs$n_taxonomy_strings > 1)) {
  stop("Some sequences have more than one taxonomy_raw string. Check parse-raw-tsvs.")
}

tie_long <- coarse_seqs %>%
  select(sequence, taxonomy_raw) %>%
  mutate(tie = purrr::map(taxonomy_raw, parse_tie_set)) %>%
  select(-taxonomy_raw) %>%
  unnest(tie)

# A finer relative is in the tie set if a tied name equals it, is a species
# within it (finer "Brevoortia", tied "Brevoortia tyrannus"), or is the genus
# containing it (finer "Thoburnia rhothoeca", tied "Thoburnia").
finer_check <- coarse_seqs %>%
  select(sequence, resolved_name, resolved_rank) %>%
  inner_join(finer_lookup, by = c("resolved_name" = "parent", "resolved_rank" = "parent_rank"),
             relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  left_join(tie_long %>% select(sequence, tied_name), by = "sequence",
            relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  group_by(sequence, finer) %>%
  summarise(in_tie_set = any(tied_name == finer |
                             str_starts(tied_name, fixed(paste0(finer, " "))) |
                             str_starts(finer, fixed(paste0(tied_name, " ")))),
            .groups = "drop")

# ---- Review table -------------------------------------------------------------
nested_review <- coarse_seqs %>%
  select(-n_taxonomy_strings, -taxonomy_raw) %>%
  left_join(
    finer_check %>%
      group_by(sequence) %>%
      summarise(finer_detected   = paste(sort(finer), collapse = " | "),
                finer_in_tie_set = paste(sort(finer[in_tie_set]), collapse = " | "),
                .groups = "drop"),
    by = "sequence") %>%
  left_join(
    tie_long %>%
      group_by(sequence) %>%
      summarise(n_tied  = n(),
                tie_set = paste0(tied_name, ": ", n_hits, collapse = ", "),
                .groups = "drop"),
    by = "sequence") %>%
  mutate(
    merged_to = unname(TAXON_MERGES[resolved_name]),
    target_in_tie_set = map2_lgl(sequence, merged_to, function(s, t) {
      !is.na(t) && any(tie_long$tied_name[tie_long$sequence == s] == t)
    }),
    decision = if_else(is.na(merged_to), "kept", "merged")
  ) %>%
  arrange(resolved_rank, resolved_name, desc(reads)) %>%
  select(decision, resolved_name, resolved_rank, merged_to, target_in_tie_set, n_sites, reads,
         finer_detected, finer_in_tie_set, n_tied, tie_set, sequence)

write_csv(nested_review, file.path(stats_dir, "nested_taxa_review.csv"))

# ---- Checks on TAXON_MERGES ---------------------------------------------------
bad_merges <- nested_review %>% filter(decision == "merged", !target_in_tie_set)
if (nrow(bad_merges) > 0) {
  stop("Merged sequences whose tie set lacks the merge target: ",
       paste(unique(bad_merges$resolved_name), collapse = ", "),
       ". Review TAXON_MERGES in post-parse-filters.")
}

unused_merges <- setdiff(names(TAXON_MERGES),
                         nested_review$resolved_name[nested_review$decision == "merged"])
if (length(unused_merges) > 0) {
  warning("TAXON_MERGES entries that matched no nested sequence: ",
          paste(unused_merges, collapse = ", "))
}

# ---- Summary -------------------------------------------------------------------
cat(sprintf("Nested coarse sequences reviewed: %d (%d names)\n",
            nrow(nested_review), n_distinct(nested_review$resolved_name)))
print(count(nested_review, decision))
cat("\nMerged by TAXON_MERGES:\n")
print(as.data.frame(nested_review %>% filter(decision == "merged") %>%
                      select(resolved_name, merged_to, n_sites, tie_set)), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nKept, but a finer relative is in the tie set:\n")
print(as.data.frame(nested_review %>% filter(decision == "kept", finer_in_tie_set != "") %>%
                      select(resolved_name, n_sites, finer_in_tie_set)), row.names = FALSE)
```


```{r figure1-sample-collection}
# ---- Figure 1: sample collection timeline --------------------------------
# One dot per collected sample, grouped by region and colored by state.
# Layout follows Justen et al. 2026, Figure 2a, and uses the same state
# colors. Site names are on the right, colored by state. States are shown as
# outlined boxes on the left that span each state's rows, so no state legend
# is needed.
FIG1_WIDTH_MM   <- 136   # 1.5 column
FIG1_HEIGHT_MM  <- 90
FIG1_BASE_SIZE  <- FONT_BASE
FIG1_AXIS_TEXT  <- FONT_AXIS
FIG1_AXIS_TITLE <- FONT_TITLE

# Site labels drop the ", XX" state suffix because the state box shows it.
FIG1_DROP_STATE_SUFFIX <- TRUE

# State box placement, in days left of the first collection date. The panel
# is ~520 days wide, so ~5.5 days is about 1 mm at this figure width.
FIG1_BOX_GAP_DAYS   <- 7    # gap between box and panel edge
FIG1_BOX_WIDTH_DAYS <- 20   # box width
FIG1_LEFT_MARGIN_PT <- 20   # room outside the panel for the boxes (other margins stay 2 pt)

sample_counts <- all_parsed %>%
  distinct(canonical_site, date) %>%
  count(canonical_site, name = "n_samples")

merged <- read_site_labels() %>%
  select(current_site_label, state, region, shorthand_for_figures) %>%
  left_join(sample_counts, by = c("current_site_label" = "canonical_site")) %>%
  mutate(
    n_samples = replace_na(n_samples, 0),
    region = factor(region, levels = REGION_ORDER)
  )

row_list <- list()
for (reg in REGION_ORDER) {
  row_list[[length(row_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
    label = reg, type = "header", canonical_site = NA_character_, n_samples = NA_integer_
  )
  sub <- merged %>%
    filter(region == reg) %>%
    arrange(state, shorthand_for_figures) %>%
    transmute(
      label = shorthand_for_figures,
      type = "site",
      canonical_site = current_site_label,
      n_samples = n_samples,
      state = state
    )
  row_list[[length(row_list) + 1]] <- sub
}

row_df <- bind_rows(row_list) %>%
  mutate(
    y = n() - row_number() + 1,
    site_name = if (FIG1_DROP_STATE_SUFFIX) str_remove(label, ",\\s*[A-Z]{2}$") else label,
    display_label = if_else(type == "site", paste0(site_name, "  (n=", n_samples, ")"), label)
  )

samples_long <- all_parsed %>%
  distinct(canonical_site, date) %>%
  left_join(row_df %>% filter(type == "site") %>% select(canonical_site, y, state), by = "canonical_site")

header_df    <- row_df %>% filter(type == "header")
site_axis_df <- row_df %>% filter(type == "site")
date_range   <- c(STUDY_START_DATE, STUDY_END_DATE)

# One box per state, spanning that state's rows
state_box_df <- site_axis_df %>%
  group_by(state) %>%
  summarise(ymin = min(y) - 0.45, ymax = max(y) + 0.45, n_rows = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    xmax = date_range[1] - FIG1_BOX_GAP_DAYS,
    xmin = xmax - FIG1_BOX_WIDTH_DAYS,
    xmid = xmin + FIG1_BOX_WIDTH_DAYS / 2,
    ymid = (ymin + ymax) / 2,
    # Single-site states are one row tall, too short for vertical text
    text_angle = if_else(n_rows > 1, 90, 0)
  )

p_timeline <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(
    data = header_df,
    aes(xmin = date_range[1], xmax = date_range[2], ymin = y - 0.5, ymax = y + 0.5),
    fill = HEADER_FILL
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = header_df,
    aes(x = mean(date_range), y = y, label = label),
    hjust = 0.5, fontface = "bold", size = FIG1_AXIS_TITLE / .pt, color = "black"
  ) +
  geom_point(data = samples_long, aes(x = date, y = y, color = state), size = 0.6, alpha = 0.9) +
  # State boxes, drawn outside the panel (coord_cartesian clip = "off")
  geom_rect(
    data = state_box_df,
    aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, color = state),
    fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = state_box_df,
    aes(x = xmid, y = ymid, label = state, color = state, angle = text_angle),
    fontface = "bold", size = FIG1_AXIS_TEXT / .pt
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = STATE_COLORS, limits = names(STATE_COLORS), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = site_axis_df$y, labels = site_axis_df$display_label,
                     position = "right", expand = expansion(add = 0.4)) +
  # limits set in coord_cartesian, not here, so the boxes left of the first
  # date are kept instead of dropped as out-of-range
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%m-%Y", expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = date_range, clip = "off") +
  labs(x = "Collection date", y = "Site") +
  theme_bw(base_size = FIG1_BASE_SIZE) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(color = "black", size = FIG1_BASE_SIZE),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = FIG1_AXIS_TEXT),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "black", size = FIG1_AXIS_TITLE),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    # Vectorized color: each site label in its state's color. ggplot2 warns
    # this isn't officially supported, but it renders correctly.
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(margin = margin(l = 1), hjust = 0,
                                     color = unname(STATE_COLORS[site_axis_df$state])),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey85", linewidth = 0.3),
    plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, FIG1_LEFT_MARGIN_PT)
  )

save_figure(p_timeline, fig_file("sample_collection"), width = FIG1_WIDTH_MM, height = FIG1_HEIGHT_MM)
p_timeline

# The site table (Supplementary Table (sites)) is curated by hand. It is read and
# registered in the setup chunk, not rebuilt here.

# =========================================================================
# Analysis only (not in the manuscript): weekly sample coverage heatmap
# =========================================================================
# One row per site, one column per week. A tile is filled when at least one
# sample was collected at that site that week. Uses the same sample source
# as figure1-sample-collection (all_parsed, every parsed sample regardless
# of what it detected) and the same region and site order.
#
# Weeks run Sunday to Saturday, so the last column is the August 30 -
# September 5, 2026 week that contains STUDY_END_DATE. The first column is
# the week containing STUDY_START_DATE.
#
# Tiles are colored three ways so gaps stand out:
#   Sampled      at least one sample that week
#   Gap          no sample, but the week falls between the site's first and
#                last sampled weeks
#   Outside      before the site's first sampled week or after its last
# Row labels show sampled weeks / weeks between first and last sample.
# Samples dated outside the study window are listed, not plotted.
# Outputs (analysis_dir): qc_weekly_sample_coverage.png/.svg,
# qc_missing_weeks.csv (one row per gap week)

local({
  samples <- all_parsed %>%
    distinct(canonical_site, date) %>%
    mutate(date = as.Date(date))

  outside_window <- samples %>%
    filter(date < STUDY_START_DATE | date > STUDY_END_DATE) %>%
    arrange(canonical_site, date)
  if (nrow(outside_window) > 0) {
    cat("Samples outside the study window (not plotted):\n")
    print(as.data.frame(outside_window), row.names = FALSE)
  }

  weekly <- samples %>%
    filter(date >= STUDY_START_DATE, date <= STUDY_END_DATE) %>%
    mutate(week = study_week(date)) %>%
    count(canonical_site, week, name = "n_samples")

  all_weeks <- STUDY_WEEKS

  site_info <- read_site_labels() %>%
    select(canonical_site = current_site_label, state, region, shorthand_for_figures) %>%
    mutate(region = factor(region, levels = REGION_ORDER)) %>%
    arrange(region, state, shorthand_for_figures)

  site_range <- weekly %>%
    group_by(canonical_site) %>%
    summarise(first_week = min(week), last_week = max(week), .groups = "drop")

  grid <- expand_grid(canonical_site = site_info$canonical_site, week = all_weeks) %>%
    left_join(weekly, by = c("canonical_site", "week")) %>%
    left_join(site_range, by = "canonical_site") %>%
    left_join(site_info, by = "canonical_site") %>%
    mutate(
      n_samples = replace_na(n_samples, 0L),
      status = case_when(
        n_samples > 0                                            ~ "Sampled",
        !is.na(first_week) & week > first_week & week < last_week ~ "Gap",
        TRUE                                                     ~ "Outside"
      )
    )

  site_summary <- grid %>%
    group_by(canonical_site, shorthand_for_figures) %>%
    summarise(
      weeks_sampled  = sum(status == "Sampled"),
      weeks_in_range = sum(status %in% c("Sampled", "Gap")),
      gap_weeks      = sum(status == "Gap"),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(row_label = paste0(shorthand_for_figures, "  (", weeks_sampled, "/", weeks_in_range, ")"))

  grid <- grid %>%
    left_join(site_summary %>% select(canonical_site, row_label), by = "canonical_site") %>%
    mutate(row_label = factor(row_label,
                              levels = rev(site_summary$row_label[match(site_info$canonical_site,
                                                                        site_summary$canonical_site)])))

  missing_weeks <- grid %>%
    filter(status == "Gap") %>%
    transmute(canonical_site, site = shorthand_for_figures, state,
              week_start = week, week_end = week + 6) %>%
    arrange(match(canonical_site, site_info$canonical_site), week_start)
  write_csv(missing_weeks, file.path(analysis_dir, "qc_missing_weeks.csv"))

  cat(sprintf("Weeks in study window: %d (%s to %s)\n", length(all_weeks),
              format(min(all_weeks)), format(max(all_weeks) + 6)))
  cat("Gap weeks per site (sites with any gaps):\n")
  print(as.data.frame(site_summary %>% filter(gap_weeks > 0) %>%
                        arrange(desc(gap_weeks)) %>%
                        select(site = shorthand_for_figures, weeks_sampled, weeks_in_range, gap_weeks)),
        row.names = FALSE)

  p <- ggplot(grid, aes(x = week + 3.5, y = row_label, fill = status)) +
    geom_tile(width = 7, height = 0.9, color = HEAT_GRID_COLOR, linewidth = HEAT_GRID_WIDTH) +
    facet_grid(region ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(Sampled = "grey25", Gap = "#D7263D", Outside = "grey92"),
                      breaks = c("Sampled", "Gap", "Outside"),
                      labels = c("Sampled", "No sample (gap)", "Before first / after last sample"),
                      name = NULL) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%m-%Y",
                 limits = c(min(all_weeks), max(all_weeks) + 7), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = "Week (Sunday to Saturday)", y = NULL,
         title = "Weekly sample coverage",
         subtitle = "Row label: weeks sampled / weeks between first and last sample") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 7) +
    theme(
      text = element_text(color = "black"),
      axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      strip.placement = "outside",
      strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold"),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = HEADER_FILL, color = NA),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.key.size = unit(3, "mm")
    )

  save_figure(p, "qc_weekly_sample_coverage", width = 260, height = 150, dir = analysis_dir)
  print(p)
})
```


```{r figure2-composition}
# =========================================================================
# Figure 2: vertebrate composition by site
# =========================================================================
# Share of each site's reads by vertebrate category, (a) with human reads
# and (b) without. Categories are the dominant animals (human, pig, cattle,
# chicken, turkey, salmon/trout, cod family) plus "Other mammal / bird /
# fish". Reads are summed over every sample at the site after the standard
# filter. Ambiguous Phasianidae and Bovidae family calls are dropped.
# Supplementary Table (composition) gives every percentage shown.

FIG2_WIDTH_MM     <- 180
FIG2_HEIGHT_MM    <- 100
FIG2_BASE_SIZE    <- 6.5
FIG2_AXIS_TEXT    <- 6
FIG2_AXIS_TITLE   <- 6.5
FIG2_LEGEND_TITLE <- 6.5
FIG2_LEGEND_TEXT  <- 6

# Colors come from CLASS_STEPS (setup chunk). Each class's shades are
# assigned to its categories in the order listed below, darkest first
# (e.g., Human = Mammal shade 1, Pig = shade 2).

MAMMAL_SCHEME <- c(Homo = "Human", Sus = "Pig", Bos = "Cattle")
BIRD_SCHEME   <- c(Gallus = "Chicken", Meleagris = "Turkey")
FISH_SCHEME   <- c(Salmo = "Salmon/trout", Oncorhynchus = "Salmon/trout",
                    Salvelinus = "Salmon/trout")

FAMILY_FOLD_IN <- list(
  Mammal = c(Hominidae = "Human", Suidae = "Pig"),
  Bird   = character(0),
  Fish   = c(Gadidae = "Cod family", Salmonidae = "Salmon/trout")
)

# ---- Site labels and sample counts -----------------------------------------
sample_counts <- all_parsed %>%
  distinct(canonical_site, date) %>%
  count(canonical_site, name = "n_samples")

site_labels <- read_site_labels()

site_meta <- site_labels %>%
  select(canonical_site = current_site_label, state, shorthand = shorthand_for_figures) %>%
  left_join(sample_counts, by = "canonical_site") %>%
  mutate(
    n_samples = replace_na(n_samples, 0),
    label = paste0(shorthand, "  (n=", n_samples, ")"),
    region = factor(REGION_MAP[state], levels = REGION_ORDER)
  )

LABEL_LOOKUP <- setNames(site_meta$label, site_meta$canonical_site)

# ---- Detection data: standard filter, genus display -------------------------
raw_all <- read_csv(chordate_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date), canonical_site = recode_site(canonical_site))

raw <- raw_all %>%
  filter(!(resolved_rank == "family" & family %in% DROP_AMBIGUOUS_NAMED_FAMILIES))

df <- apply_standard_filter(raw) %>%
  mutate(genus_label = genus, broad_cat = broad_cat(class))

assign_category_label <- function(broad_cat, genus_label, family) {
  case_when(
    broad_cat == "Mammal" & genus_label %in% names(MAMMAL_SCHEME)        ~ unname(MAMMAL_SCHEME[genus_label]),
    broad_cat == "Mammal" & family %in% names(FAMILY_FOLD_IN$Mammal)     ~ unname(FAMILY_FOLD_IN$Mammal[family]),
    broad_cat == "Mammal"                                                ~ "Other mammal",
    broad_cat == "Bird"   & genus_label %in% names(BIRD_SCHEME)          ~ unname(BIRD_SCHEME[genus_label]),
    broad_cat == "Bird"   & family %in% names(FAMILY_FOLD_IN$Bird)       ~ unname(FAMILY_FOLD_IN$Bird[family]),
    broad_cat == "Bird"                                                  ~ "Other bird",
    broad_cat == "Fish"   & genus_label %in% names(FISH_SCHEME)          ~ unname(FISH_SCHEME[genus_label]),
    broad_cat == "Fish"   & family %in% names(FAMILY_FOLD_IN$Fish)       ~ unname(FAMILY_FOLD_IN$Fish[family]),
    broad_cat == "Fish"                                                  ~ "Other fish",
    TRUE                                                                 ~ "Other"
  )
}
df <- df %>% mutate(category_label = assign_category_label(broad_cat, genus_label, family))

# ---- Ambiguous-family exclusion check ----------------------------------------
# Family-level Phasianidae and Bovidae calls are excluded (post-parse-filters).
# This flags any site where those excluded reads would be at least
# AMBIG_CHECK_THRESHOLD_PCT of the site's reads.
AMBIG_CHECK_THRESHOLD_PCT <- 1

ambig_candidates <- raw_all %>%
  filter(resolved_rank == "family", family %in% DROP_AMBIGUOUS_NAMED_FAMILIES, reads >= MIN_READS)

ambig_qualifying_keys <- ambig_candidates %>%
  distinct(canonical_site, sequence, date) %>%
  count(canonical_site, sequence, name = "n_dates") %>%
  filter(n_dates >= MIN_DATES) %>%
  select(canonical_site, sequence)

ambig_would_qualify <- ambig_candidates %>%
  semi_join(ambig_qualifying_keys, by = c("canonical_site", "sequence")) %>%
  group_by(canonical_site) %>%
  summarise(excluded_reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop")

site_totals_check <- df %>% group_by(canonical_site) %>% summarise(site_total = sum(reads), .groups = "drop")

ambig_check <- ambig_would_qualify %>%
  left_join(site_totals_check, by = "canonical_site") %>%
  mutate(pct_of_site = 100 * excluded_reads / (site_total + excluded_reads))

flagged <- ambig_check %>% filter(pct_of_site >= AMBIG_CHECK_THRESHOLD_PCT)
if (nrow(flagged) > 0) {
  warning(
    "Ambiguous-family exclusion (Phasianidae/Bovidae) hides >= ", AMBIG_CHECK_THRESHOLD_PCT,
    "% of a site's bar at: ", paste(flagged$canonical_site, collapse = ", "),
    ". Check whether this materially affects Figure 2 and update the manuscript text if so."
  )
} else if (nrow(ambig_check) > 0) {
  cat("Ambiguous-family exclusion check: largest hidden fraction is",
      round(max(ambig_check$pct_of_site), 4), "% of a site's total (",
      ambig_check$canonical_site[which.max(ambig_check$pct_of_site)], "), below the",
      AMBIG_CHECK_THRESHOLD_PCT, "% flag threshold.\n")
} else {
  cat("Ambiguous-family exclusion check: no excluded sequence clears the standard detection filter at any site.\n")
}

# Excluded reads vs reads in the same family that resolved to genus or
# species. "Qualifying" = would have passed the standard filter if not
# excluded. Network-wide totals print here and are saved for
# manuscript-stats; per-site values are saved to stats_dir.
ambig_excluded <- ambig_candidates %>%
  semi_join(ambig_qualifying_keys, by = c("canonical_site", "sequence")) %>%
  transmute(canonical_site, family, resolved = "Excluded (family level only)", reads)

ambig_resolved <- df %>%
  filter(family %in% DROP_AMBIGUOUS_NAMED_FAMILIES) %>%
  transmute(canonical_site, family, resolved = resolved_name, reads)

ambig_summary <- bind_rows(ambig_excluded, ambig_resolved) %>%
  group_by(family, resolved) %>%
  summarise(reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(family) %>%
  mutate(pct_of_family = 100 * reads / sum(reads)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(family, desc(resolved == "Excluded (family level only)"), desc(reads))

ambig_by_site <- bind_rows(ambig_excluded, ambig_resolved) %>%
  mutate(status = if_else(resolved == "Excluded (family level only)", "excluded", "resolved")) %>%
  group_by(canonical_site, family, status) %>%
  summarise(reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = status, values_from = reads, values_fill = 0)
if (!"excluded" %in% names(ambig_by_site)) ambig_by_site$excluded <- 0
ambig_by_site <- ambig_by_site %>% mutate(pct_excluded = 100 * excluded / (excluded + resolved))

write_csv(ambig_summary, file.path(stats_dir, "ambiguous_family_exclusion_summary.csv"))
write_csv(ambig_by_site, file.path(stats_dir, "ambiguous_family_exclusion_by_site.csv"))

cat("\n[Ambiguous-family exclusion: excluded vs resolved reads, network-wide]\n")
print(as.data.frame(ambig_summary %>% mutate(pct_of_family = round(pct_of_family, 4))), row.names = FALSE)

# ---- Aggregation to site x category -----------------------------------------
build_composition <- function(data) {
  site_totals <- data %>% group_by(canonical_site) %>% summarise(site_total = sum(reads), .groups = "drop")
  data %>%
    group_by(canonical_site, broad_cat, category_label) %>%
    summarise(reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
    left_join(site_totals, by = "canonical_site") %>%
    mutate(
      pct = reads / site_total * 100,
      genus_display = paste(broad_cat, category_label, sep = "::")
    )
}

scheme_order_dict <- function() {
  list(
    Mammal = c(unique(c(unname(MAMMAL_SCHEME), unname(FAMILY_FOLD_IN$Mammal))), "Other mammal"),
    Bird   = c(unique(c(unname(BIRD_SCHEME), unname(FAMILY_FOLD_IN$Bird))), "Other bird"),
    Fish   = c(unique(c(unname(FISH_SCHEME), unname(FAMILY_FOLD_IN$Fish))), "Other fish"),
    Other  = c("Other")
  )
}

# Assigns each class's fixed shades (CLASS_STEPS) to its categories in
# scheme order. Stops if a class has more categories than shades, so a new
# category can't silently end up uncolored.
build_palette <- function() {
  scheme <- scheme_order_dict()
  pal <- c()
  for (cat in names(CLASS_STEPS)) {
    ordered_labels <- scheme[[cat]]
    if (length(ordered_labels) == 0) next
    steps <- CLASS_STEPS[[cat]]
    if (length(ordered_labels) > length(steps)) {
      stop(cat, " has ", length(ordered_labels), " categories but only ", length(steps),
           " shades in CLASS_STEPS. Add a shade in the setup chunk.")
    }
    shades <- setNames(steps[seq_along(ordered_labels)], paste(cat, ordered_labels, sep = "::"))
    pal <- c(pal, shades)
  }
  pal
}

# ---- Region-header row layout (shared y-position lookup) --------------------
# HEADER_FILL is set in the setup chunk
GROUP_GAP <- 0.15

compute_group_layout <- function(site_order, group_breaks) {
  y <- 0
  y_pos <- c()
  header_rows <- tibble(y = numeric(), label = character())
  idx <- 1
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(group_breaks))) {
    n <- group_breaks$n[i]
    header_y <- y
    if (nzchar(group_breaks$label[i])) {
      header_rows <- bind_rows(header_rows, tibble(y = header_y, label = group_breaks$label[i]))
    }
    y <- y - 1
    block_sites <- site_order[idx:(idx + n - 1)]
    block_y <- y - (seq_len(n) - 1)
    names(block_y) <- block_sites
    y_pos <- c(y_pos, block_y)
    idx <- idx + n
    y <- block_y[n] - 1 - GROUP_GAP
  }
  list(y_pos = y_pos, header_rows = header_rows, min_y = min(c(y_pos, header_rows$y)))
}

measure_label_width_mm <- function(label, size) {
  grid::convertWidth(grid::grobWidth(grid::textGrob(label, gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = size))), "mm", valueOnly = TRUE)
}

# ---- Legend: one gtable for all four classes --------------------------------
# Built as a single table so every swatch and title shares one left edge.
# Separate ggplot legends pad themselves differently and do not line up.
build_grouped_legend <- function(comp, total_height_mm,
                                  key_size_mm = 3, key_gap_mm = 1.3,
                                  row_h_mm = 3.3, title_row_h_mm = 3.8,
                                  section_gap_mm = 2.2,
                                  title_size = FIG2_LEGEND_TITLE, text_size = FIG2_LEGEND_TEXT,
                                  border_pad_mm = 1.5) {
  scheme <- scheme_order_dict()
  pal_full <- build_palette()
  cats <- c("Mammal", "Bird", "Fish", "Other")

  rows <- list()
  for (j in seq_along(cats)) {
    cat <- cats[j]
    present <- comp %>% filter(broad_cat == cat) %>% distinct(category_label) %>% pull(category_label)
    ordered <- scheme[[cat]][scheme[[cat]] %in% present]
    ordered <- c(ordered, setdiff(present, ordered))
    if (length(ordered) == 0) next
    if (length(rows) > 0) rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- list(type = "gap")
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- list(type = "title", label = cat)
    for (lab in ordered) {
      key <- paste(cat, lab, sep = "::")
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- list(type = "key", label = lab, fill = unname(pal_full[key]))
    }
  }

  # Off-screen device so text widths can be measured without opening a
  # visible plot window or side-effecting the active graphics device.
  grDevices::pdf(NULL)
  label_widths_mm <- vapply(rows, function(r) {
    if (r$type == "gap") return(0)
    w <- measure_label_width_mm(r$label, if (r$type == "title") title_size else text_size)
    if (r$type == "key") w <- w + key_size_mm + key_gap_mm
    w
  }, numeric(1))
  grDevices::dev.off()

  label_col_w_mm <- max(label_widths_mm) - key_size_mm - key_gap_mm
  total_width_mm <- key_size_mm + key_gap_mm + label_col_w_mm

  row_heights <- vapply(rows, function(r) {
    if (r$type == "gap") section_gap_mm else if (r$type == "title") title_row_h_mm else row_h_mm
  }, numeric(1))

  gt <- gtable::gtable(
    widths  = grid::unit(c(key_size_mm, label_col_w_mm + key_gap_mm), "mm"),
    heights = grid::unit(row_heights, "mm")
  )

  for (i in seq_along(rows)) {
    r <- rows[[i]]
    if (r$type == "gap") next
    if (r$type == "title") {
      gt <- gtable::gtable_add_grob(
        gt,
        grid::textGrob(r$label, x = 0, hjust = 0, gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = title_size, fontface = "bold")),
        t = i, l = 1, r = 2
      )
    } else {
      gt <- gtable::gtable_add_grob(
        gt,
        grid::rectGrob(width = grid::unit(key_size_mm, "mm"), height = grid::unit(key_size_mm, "mm"),
                        gp = grid::gpar(fill = r$fill, col = "black", lwd = 0.6)),
        t = i, l = 1
      )
      gt <- gtable::gtable_add_grob(
        gt,
        grid::textGrob(r$label, x = grid::unit(key_gap_mm, "mm"), hjust = 0, gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = text_size)),
        t = i, l = 2
      )
    }
  }

  content_height_mm <- sum(row_heights)
  box_width_mm  <- total_width_mm + 2 * border_pad_mm
  box_height_mm <- content_height_mm + 2 * border_pad_mm

  legend_bordered <- cowplot::ggdraw(gt) +
    theme(
      plot.background = element_rect(color = "black", fill = "white", linewidth = 0.3),
      plot.margin = margin(border_pad_mm, border_pad_mm, border_pad_mm, border_pad_mm, unit = "mm")
    )

  side_gap_mm <- max((total_height_mm - box_height_mm) / 2, 0)
  legend_final <- cowplot::plot_grid(
    NULL, legend_bordered, NULL,
    ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(side_gap_mm, box_height_mm, side_gap_mm)
  )

  list(plot = legend_final, box_width_mm = box_width_mm)
}

# ---- Combined long dataset (both panels, one plot) --------------------------
comp_with_human    <- build_composition(df) %>% mutate(panel = "a")
comp_without_human <- build_composition(df %>% filter(category_label != "Human")) %>% mutate(panel = "b")
comp_long <- bind_rows(comp_with_human, comp_without_human) %>%
  mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = c("a", "b")))

sort_tbl_master <- site_meta %>% arrange(region, state, shorthand)
site_order_master <- sort_tbl_master$canonical_site
group_breaks_master <- sort_tbl_master %>%
  count(region, name = "n") %>%
  filter(!is.na(region)) %>%
  transmute(label = as.character(region), n)

layout      <- compute_group_layout(site_order_master, group_breaks_master)
y_pos       <- layout$y_pos
header_rows <- layout$header_rows

comp_long <- comp_long %>% mutate(y_num = y_pos[canonical_site])

scheme <- scheme_order_dict()
stacking_levels <- character(0)
for (cat in c("Mammal", "Bird", "Fish", "Other")) {
  present <- comp_long %>% filter(broad_cat == cat) %>% distinct(category_label) %>% pull(category_label)
  ordered <- scheme[[cat]][scheme[[cat]] %in% present]
  ordered <- c(ordered, setdiff(present, ordered))
  if (length(ordered) > 0) stacking_levels <- c(stacking_levels, paste(cat, ordered, sep = "::"))
}
comp_long <- comp_long %>% mutate(genus_display = factor(genus_display, levels = stacking_levels))

y_breaks <- y_pos[site_order_master]
y_labels <- LABEL_LOOKUP[site_order_master]
pal <- build_palette()

header_rows_both <- bind_rows(

) %>% mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = c("a", "b")))

# Panel letters are bold lowercase at 8 pt, followed by the panel title
FIG2_PANEL_TITLES <- c(
  a = sprintf("<span style='font-size:%gpt'>**a**</span>&nbsp;&nbsp;With human", FIG_PANEL_LABEL_PT),
  b = sprintf("<span style='font-size:%gpt'>**b**</span>&nbsp;&nbsp;Without human", FIG_PANEL_LABEL_PT)
)

p_composition <- ggplot(comp_long, aes(x = y_num, y = pct, fill = genus_display)) +
  geom_rect(data = header_rows_both, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            aes(xmin = y - 0.5, xmax = y + 0.5, ymin = 0, ymax = 100),
```
