```{r figure2-composition}
            aes(x = y, y = 50, label = label),
            fontface = "bold", size = FIG2_AXIS_TITLE / .pt, hjust = 0.5, color = "black") +   # same as Figure 1
  geom_col(width = 0.72, color = "black", linewidth = 0.2,
           position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, nrow = 1, axes = "margins",
             labeller = labeller(panel = FIG2_PANEL_TITLES)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = y_breaks, labels = y_labels, expand = expansion(add = 0.4)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal, name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(v) paste0(v, "%"),
                      expand = expansion(mult = 0, add = 0),
                      limits = c(0, 100),
                      oob = scales::oob_keep) +  # stacked tops can exceed 100 by rounding; keep them
  labs(x = "Site", y = "% of reads") +
  theme_bw(base_size = FIG2_BASE_SIZE) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(color = "black", size = FIG2_BASE_SIZE),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = FIG2_AXIS_TEXT),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = FIG2_AXIS_TEXT, margin = margin(r = 2)),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "black", size = FIG2_AXIS_TITLE),
    axis.ticks.length = unit(0, "pt"),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = unit(6.5, "mm"),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = ggtext::element_markdown(size = FIG2_AXIS_TITLE, hjust = 0),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(4, 2, 2, 1)
  )

legend_result <- build_grouped_legend(comp_with_human, total_height_mm = FIG2_HEIGHT_MM)

GAP_MM <- 3
p_final <- cowplot::plot_grid(
  p_composition, NULL, legend_result$plot,
  nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(FIG2_WIDTH_MM - legend_result$box_width_mm - GAP_MM, GAP_MM, legend_result$box_width_mm)
)
p_final <- cowplot::ggdraw(p_final) +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))

save_figure(p_final, fig_file("composition"), width = FIG2_WIDTH_MM, height = FIG2_HEIGHT_MM)
p_final

# =========================================================================

# One row per site and category. Reads are the same in both panels; the

add_supp_table("composition", supp_table_composition,

        "after the standard filter. The two percentage columns give the category's share of the site's",

        "read count is the same in both. Human rows have no value in the without-human column.",
        "Sites follow the region order used in every figure."))

cat("\n", supp_table_ref("composition"), ":", nrow(supp_table_composition), "rows,",
    n_distinct(supp_table_composition$Site), "sites.\n")

# ---- Birds: chicken and turkey vs other birds --------------------------------

bird_breakdown <- df %>%
```

```{r supp-fig-composition-with-without-human}
# Supplementary Figure (composition_with_without_human): pooled Mammal, Bird, and Fish composition with and
# without human reads. A line connects each class's two pooled values; faint
# dots show each site's value.
#
# Also writes an outlier check to analysis/ (analysis only, not in the manuscript): site
# values outside Tukey's IQR fences within each class and with/without-human
# group, flagged for review.

SUPPFIG1_WIDTH_MM     <- 88    # single column
SUPPFIG1_HEIGHT_MM    <- 65
SUPPFIG1_BASE_SIZE    <- FONT_BASE
SUPPFIG1_AXIS_TEXT    <- FONT_AXIS
SUPPFIG1_LEGEND_TITLE <- FONT_TITLE
SUPPFIG1_LEGEND_TEXT  <- FONT_AXIS

CAT_COLOR <- CLASS_COLORS[c("Mammal", "Bird", "Fish")]
STATE_LEVELS <- c("With human", "Without human")

df <- load_detections(drop_human = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    broad_cat = broad_cat(class),
    is_human  = is_human(genus, family)
  )

pooled_pct <- function(data) {
  data %>%
    group_by(broad_cat) %>%
    summarise(reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(pct = reads / sum(reads) * 100)
}

site_pct <- function(data) {
  site_totals <- data %>% group_by(canonical_site) %>% summarise(site_total = sum(reads), .groups = "drop")
  data %>%
    group_by(canonical_site, broad_cat) %>%
    summarise(reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
    left_join(site_totals, by = "canonical_site") %>%
    mutate(pct = reads / site_total * 100)
}

df_no_human <- df %>% filter(!is_human)

with_human    <- pooled_pct(df) %>% mutate(state = "With human")
without_human <- pooled_pct(df_no_human) %>% mutate(state = "Without human")

site_with_human    <- site_pct(df) %>% mutate(state = "With human")
site_without_human <- site_pct(df_no_human) %>% mutate(state = "Without human")

site_data <- bind_rows(site_with_human, site_without_human) %>%
  filter(broad_cat != "Other") %>%
  mutate(
    broad_cat = factor(broad_cat, levels = c("Mammal", "Bird", "Fish")),
    state     = factor(state, levels = STATE_LEVELS)
  )

pooled_data <- bind_rows(with_human, without_human) %>%
  filter(broad_cat != "Other") %>%
  mutate(
    broad_cat = factor(broad_cat, levels = c("Mammal", "Bird", "Fish")),
    state     = factor(state, levels = STATE_LEVELS)
  )

pooled_data <- pooled_data %>%
  mutate(
    text_x = if_else(state == "With human", as.numeric(state) - 0.14, as.numeric(state) + 0.14),
    text_hjust = if_else(state == "With human", 1, 0)
  )

set.seed(42)

# ---- Figure ----------------------------------------------------------------
p_dotplot <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = site_data,
             aes(x = state, y = pct, color = broad_cat),
             position = position_jitter(width = 0.08, height = 0),
             size = 0.9, alpha = 0.2, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_line(data = pooled_data,
            aes(x = state, y = pct, group = broad_cat, color = broad_cat),
            linewidth = 0.45, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = pooled_data,
             aes(x = state, y = pct, color = broad_cat),
             size = 2.6) +
  geom_text(data = pooled_data,
            aes(x = text_x, y = pct, label = paste0(round(pct), "%"), hjust = text_hjust, color = broad_cat),
            size = 5.5, size.unit = "pt", fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = CAT_COLOR, name = "Class") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(y) paste0(y, "%"), limits = c(0, 100),
                      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.02))) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.35, 0.35))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% of pooled reads") +
  guides(color = guide_legend()) +
  theme_bw(base_size = SUPPFIG1_BASE_SIZE) +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    text = element_text(color = "black"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = SUPPFIG1_AXIS_TEXT),
    axis.title.y = element_text(color = "black", margin = margin(r = 4)),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = SUPPFIG1_LEGEND_TITLE, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(color = "black", size = SUPPFIG1_LEGEND_TEXT),
    legend.key.size = unit(2.5, "mm"),
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    legend.box.background = element_rect(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3, fill = "white"),
    legend.margin = LEGEND_BOX_MARGIN,
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(4, 6, 2, 3)
  )

save_figure(p_dotplot, supp_fig_file("composition_with_without_human"), dir = supp_dir,
            width = SUPPFIG1_WIDTH_MM, height = SUPPFIG1_HEIGHT_MM)
p_dotplot

# ---- Analysis only (not in the manuscript): outlier check ------------------
IQR_MULTIPLIER <- 1.5   # Tukey default; raise for a stricter (fewer-flags) cutoff

n_samples_by_site <- all_parsed %>%
  distinct(canonical_site, date) %>%
  count(canonical_site, name = "n_samples")

outlier_report <- site_data %>%
  left_join(n_samples_by_site, by = "canonical_site") %>%
  group_by(broad_cat, state) %>%
  mutate(
    group_median = median(pct),
    q1 = quantile(pct, 0.25, type = 7),
    q3 = quantile(pct, 0.75, type = 7),
    iqr = q3 - q1,
    lower_fence = q1 - IQR_MULTIPLIER * iqr,
    upper_fence = q3 + IQR_MULTIPLIER * iqr,
    is_outlier = pct < lower_fence | pct > upper_fence,
    direction = case_when(
      pct > upper_fence ~ "high",
      pct < lower_fence ~ "low",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    iqr_units_beyond_fence = case_when(
      pct > upper_fence ~ (pct - upper_fence) / iqr,
      pct < lower_fence ~ (lower_fence - pct) / iqr,
      TRUE ~ 0
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(is_outlier), broad_cat, state, desc(iqr_units_beyond_fence))

flagged <- outlier_report %>%
  filter(is_outlier) %>%
  select(canonical_site, broad_cat, state, pct, direction,
         group_median, q1, q3, lower_fence, upper_fence,
         iqr_units_beyond_fence, reads, site_total, n_samples) %>%
  mutate(across(c(pct, group_median, q1, q3, lower_fence, upper_fence, iqr_units_beyond_fence),
                ~ round(., 2)))

cat("\n=========================================================\n")
cat(" OUTLIER REPORT --", nrow(flagged), "flagged points, IQR multiplier =", IQR_MULTIPLIER, "\n")
cat("=========================================================\n\n")

if (nrow(flagged) == 0) {
  cat("No outliers flagged at this threshold.\n")
} else {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(flagged))) {
    r <- flagged[i, ]
    cat(sprintf(
      "%-28s | %-6s | %-14s | %6.2f%% (%s, %.2f IQRs beyond fence)\n",
      r$canonical_site, r$broad_cat, r$state, r$pct, r$direction, r$iqr_units_beyond_fence
    ))
    cat(sprintf(
      "    group median = %.2f%%  |  fences = [%.2f%%, %.2f%%]  |  reads = %s of %s total  |  n_samples at site = %s\n\n",
      r$group_median, r$lower_fence, r$upper_fence,
      format(round(r$reads), big.mark = ","), format(round(r$site_total), big.mark = ","), r$n_samples
    ))
  }
}

write_csv(flagged, file.path(analysis_dir, "dotplot_outliers.csv"))
write_csv(outlier_report %>% select(-q1, -q3) %>%
            rename(iqr_lower_fence = lower_fence, iqr_upper_fence = upper_fence),
          file.path(analysis_dir, "dotplot_all_points_with_fences.csv"))

cat("Saved:\n  ", file.path(analysis_dir, "dotplot_outliers.csv"), " (flagged points only)\n",
    "  ", file.path(analysis_dir, "dotplot_all_points_with_fences.csv"), " (every point, for reference)\n", sep = "")
```


```{r fingerprint-stats}
# Site-fingerprint stats: PERMANOVA and dispersion tests, sample-level PCoA,
# pooled site-level similarity (for the heatmap), and per-site
# distinctiveness (how many sites share each taxon). Nothing here makes a
# plot. Everything is written to stats_dir as .rds (for the figures chunk to
# read back exactly) and .csv (to look at directly).
#
# PERMANOVA and the PCoA are done at the SAMPLE level (one row per site-date
# sample), not pooled to one profile per site first. Pooling first is
# sensitive to how many samples a site happened to have, since sites with
# more samples get more chances to catch rare taxa. The correlation between
# pooled site richness and samples per site is printed in the summary below.
#
# The heatmap and the distinctiveness chart are still pooled to one profile
# per site, for different reasons. The heatmap is a "who looks like whom"
# companion, not a second statistical test; PERMANOVA carries that at the
# sample level. Distinctiveness has no per-sample equivalent ("was this taxon
# ever found at this site" is a site-level question).


set.seed(42)
N_PERM <- 999  # permutations for every PERMANOVA and betadisper test below

save_both <- function(obj, name) {
  saveRDS(obj, file.path(stats_dir, paste0(name, ".rds")))
  if (is.data.frame(obj)) write_csv(obj, file.path(stats_dir, paste0(name, ".csv")))
}

# ---- Load + filter ----------------------------------------------------------
# filename/well/s_number are NA for collapsed-replicate rows, so
# canonical_site + date is the sample identity from here on.
# Human reads are excluded by genus/family rather than by resolved_name.
# resolved_name only catches reads resolved all the way to "Homo sapiens";
# reads resolved only to Hominidae would otherwise pass through as a
# non-human taxon. apply_standard_filter() also applies TAXON_MERGES
# (post-parse-filters), after its read and date checks.
df <- load_detections()

df <- df %>% mutate(sample_id = paste(canonical_site, date, sep = "_"))

cat("Non-human taxa:", n_distinct(df$resolved_name), "\n")
cat("Sites:", n_distinct(df$canonical_site), "\n")
cat("Site-date samples:", n_distinct(df$sample_id), "\n")

site_state_lookup <- df %>% distinct(canonical_site, state)

# Sort key is the shorthand label (what figures display), not the internal
# canonical_site code. For example, CHI-A should sort before CHI-B, and the
# underlying canonical_site names do not alphabetize that way.
shorthand_lookup <- read_site_labels() %>%
  select(current_site_label, shorthand_for_figures) %>%
  deframe()

site_order_regional <- site_state_lookup %>%
  mutate(region = factor(REGION_MAP[state], levels = REGION_ORDER),
         shorthand = unname(shorthand_lookup[canonical_site])) %>%
  arrange(region, state, shorthand) %>%
  pull(canonical_site)
saveRDS(site_order_regional, file.path(stats_dir, "site_order_regional.rds"))
write_csv(tibble(canonical_site = site_order_regional, regional_rank = seq_along(site_order_regional)),
          file.path(stats_dir, "site_order_regional.csv"))

# ---- Sample-level presence/absence matrix -----------------------------------

sample_long <- df %>%
  distinct(sample_id, canonical_site, resolved_name) %>%
  mutate(present = 1)

sample_meta <- sample_long %>% distinct(sample_id, canonical_site)

sample_mat <- sample_long %>%
  select(-canonical_site) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = resolved_name, values_from = present, values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample_id") %>%
  as.matrix()

sample_meta <- sample_meta[match(rownames(sample_mat), sample_meta$sample_id), ]
stopifnot(all(sample_meta$sample_id == rownames(sample_mat)))

# =============================================================================
# 1. PERMANOVA, Jaccard (presence/absence)
# =============================================================================

sample_jaccard <- vegdist(sample_mat, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE)
saveRDS(sample_jaccard, file.path(stats_dir, "sample_jaccard.rds"))

permanova_result <- adonis2(
  sample_jaccard ~ canonical_site,
  data = sample_meta,
  permutations = N_PERM,
  by = NULL
)
print(permanova_result)
saveRDS(permanova_result, file.path(stats_dir, "permanova_result.rds"))
capture.output(permanova_result, file = file.path(stats_dir, "permanova_result.txt"))

# =============================================================================
# 1b. PERMANOVA + PCoA on relative read abundance (Bray-Curtis)
# =============================================================================
# Jaccard asks whether sites differ in WHICH taxa are present. Bray-Curtis on
# relative abundance asks whether they differ in HOW MUCH of each taxon they
# carry. Sequences resolving to the same name are summed to one abundance
# value per sample before normalizing.
#
# Read proportion in metabarcoding data reflects PCR amplification efficiency
# as well as biological abundance, so this result is compositional, not
# quantitative.

sample_abund_long <- df %>%
  group_by(sample_id, canonical_site, resolved_name) %>%
  summarise(reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop")

sample_abund_mat <- sample_abund_long %>%
  select(-canonical_site) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = resolved_name, values_from = reads, values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample_id") %>%
  as.matrix()

# match row order to sample_mat/sample_meta established above
sample_abund_mat <- sample_abund_mat[rownames(sample_mat), , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(all(rownames(sample_abund_mat) == sample_meta$sample_id))

sample_relabund_mat <- sample_abund_mat / rowSums(sample_abund_mat)

sample_bray <- vegdist(sample_relabund_mat, method = "bray")
saveRDS(sample_bray, file.path(stats_dir, "sample_bray.rds"))

permanova_result_bray <- adonis2(
  sample_bray ~ canonical_site,
  data = sample_meta,
  permutations = N_PERM,
  by = NULL
)
print(permanova_result_bray)
saveRDS(permanova_result_bray, file.path(stats_dir, "permanova_result_bray.rds"))
capture.output(permanova_result_bray, file = file.path(stats_dir, "permanova_result_bray.txt"))

# Classical PCoA on a non-Euclidean distance produces negative eigenvalues.
# No correction (e.g., Cailliez) is applied. ape's Relative_eig divides by the
# sum of ALL eigenvalues, negative ones included, which overstates % variance,
# so % variance is computed from the positive eigenvalues only. The number
# and sum of negative eigenvalues are printed below.
sample_pcoa_fit_bray <- pcoa(sample_bray)

eig_bray     <- sample_pcoa_fit_bray$values$Eigenvalues
pos_eig_bray <- eig_bray[eig_bray > 0]
neg_eig_bray <- eig_bray[eig_bray < 0]
cat(sprintf("Bray-Curtis PCoA: %d negative eigenvalues (sum = %.1f) vs positive sum = %.1f. %% variance from positive eigenvalues only.\n",
            length(neg_eig_bray), sum(neg_eig_bray), sum(pos_eig_bray)))

sample_pct_var_bray <- round(eig_bray[1:2] / sum(pos_eig_bray) * 100, 1)

# 2D fit error: how well Euclidean distances between the plotted 2D
# coordinates match the original distances. See section 4 for the formula.
fitted_2d_dist_bray <- dist(as.matrix(sample_pcoa_fit_bray$vectors[, 1:2]))
pcoa_stress_bray <- sqrt(sum((as.vector(sample_bray) - as.vector(fitted_2d_dist_bray))^2) /
                            sum(as.vector(sample_bray)^2))
cat("Sample-level Bray-Curtis PCoA 2D fit error:", round(pcoa_stress_bray, 4), "\n")
saveRDS(pcoa_stress_bray, file.path(stats_dir, "pcoa_stress_bray.rds"))

sample_scores_bray <- as.data.frame(sample_pcoa_fit_bray$vectors[, 1:2]) %>%
  rename(PCoA1_bray = Axis.1, PCoA2_bray = Axis.2) %>%
  rownames_to_column("sample_id") %>%
  left_join(sample_meta, by = "sample_id") %>%
  left_join(site_state_lookup, by = "canonical_site") %>%
  mutate(pct_var1_bray = sample_pct_var_bray[1], pct_var2_bray = sample_pct_var_bray[2])

save_both(sample_scores_bray, "sample_pcoa_scores_bray")

# Relative-abundance matrix, used downstream to test which taxa's
# proportions track PCoA1_bray/PCoA2_bray
saveRDS(sample_relabund_mat, file.path(stats_dir, "sample_relabund_mat.rds"))

cat(sprintf("\nBray-Curtis PERMANOVA: pseudo-F = %.2f, R\u00b2 = %.3f, p = %.3f\n",
            permanova_result_bray$F[1], permanova_result_bray$R2[1],
            permanova_result_bray$`Pr(>F)`[1]))

# =============================================================================
# 1d. Dispersion check (betadisper), Jaccard and Bray-Curtis
# =============================================================================
# PERMANOVA cannot separate differences in site centroids from differences
# in within-site spread. betadisper tests spread alone, on the same two
# matrices, using vegan defaults (spatial median, no small-group bias
# adjustment). Both distances are non-Euclidean, so betadisper warns that
# some squared distances were negative and set to zero; this is expected.
# The Spearman correlation between samples per site and mean dispersion
# shows which way unequal group sizes push PERMANOVA: if larger sites are
# more dispersed, PERMANOVA is conservative; if smaller sites are more
# dispersed, it is liberal (Anderson and Walsh 2013).
# Numbered 1d because it depends on both 1 and 1b; 1c is below.

run_betadisper <- function(dist_obj, label) {
  grp <- factor(sample_meta$canonical_site)
  bd  <- betadisper(dist_obj, grp)
  pt  <- permutest(bd, permutations = N_PERM)

  per_site <- tibble(
    distance            = label,
    canonical_site      = levels(grp),
    site_label          = unname(shorthand_lookup[levels(grp)]),
    n_samples           = as.integer(table(grp)),
    mean_dist_to_median = as.numeric(tapply(bd$distances, grp, mean))
  ) %>% arrange(desc(mean_dist_to_median))

  size_check <- cor.test(per_site$n_samples, per_site$mean_dist_to_median,
                         method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

  overall <- tibble(
    distance = label,
    F = pt$tab$F[1], df1 = pt$tab$Df[1], df2 = pt$tab$Df[2],
    p = pt$tab$`Pr(>F)`[1],
    size_vs_dispersion_rho = unname(size_check$estimate),
    size_vs_dispersion_p   = size_check$p.value
  )
  list(overall = overall, per_site = per_site)
}

betadisper_jaccard <- run_betadisper(sample_jaccard, "jaccard")
betadisper_bray    <- run_betadisper(sample_bray, "bray")

betadisper_overall  <- bind_rows(betadisper_jaccard$overall, betadisper_bray$overall)
betadisper_per_site <- bind_rows(betadisper_jaccard$per_site, betadisper_bray$per_site)
save_both(betadisper_overall, "betadisper_overall")
save_both(betadisper_per_site, "betadisper_per_site")

# =============================================================================
# 2. Pooled site-level similarity + hierarchical clustering order
# =============================================================================
# UPGMA (average linkage) on pooled site-level Jaccard distance.

site_long_for_heatmap <- df %>%
  distinct(canonical_site, resolved_name) %>%
  mutate(present = 1)

site_mat <- site_long_for_heatmap %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = resolved_name, values_from = present, values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("canonical_site") %>%
  as.matrix()

site_jaccard <- vegdist(site_mat, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE)
site_sim <- 1 - as.matrix(site_jaccard)
hc <- hclust(site_jaccard, method = "average")
site_cluster_order <- hc$labels[hc$order]

site_similarity_long <- as.data.frame(site_sim) %>%
  rownames_to_column("site_a") %>%
  pivot_longer(-site_a, names_to = "site_b", values_to = "similarity")

save_both(site_similarity_long, "site_similarity_long")
saveRDS(site_cluster_order, file.path(stats_dir, "site_cluster_order.rds"))
write_csv(tibble(canonical_site = site_cluster_order, cluster_rank = seq_along(site_cluster_order)),
          file.path(stats_dir, "site_cluster_order.csv"))

# =============================================================================
# 3. Per-site distinctiveness (taxa binned by how many sites detected them)
# =============================================================================
# n_sites counts every site where a taxon was detected, including the site
# being plotted. Bins are set by bin_occurrence_fig3a() and DIST_LEVELS in
# post-parse-filters: 1, 2, 3-5, 6-13, 14-26, and all N_SITES_TOTAL sites.

site_long <- site_long_for_heatmap
occurrence <- site_long %>%
  count(resolved_name, name = "n_sites") %>%
  mutate(bin = bin_occurrence_fig3a(n_sites))
stopifnot(!any(is.na(occurrence$bin)))

distinctiveness_data <- site_long %>%
  left_join(occurrence %>% select(resolved_name, bin), by = "resolved_name") %>%
  count(canonical_site, bin)
# bin is saved as character for a clean csv round-trip; the figures chunk
# applies DIST_LEVELS as the factor order.

save_both(distinctiveness_data, "distinctiveness_data")

# Full (non-aggregated) site x taxon x bin table. Underlies the counts in
# distinctiveness_data and is the source of the supplemental taxa table.
taxon_taxonomy <- df %>% distinct(resolved_name, genus, family, class)

distinctiveness_data_full <- site_long %>%
  left_join(occurrence %>% select(resolved_name, bin, n_sites), by = "resolved_name") %>%
  left_join(taxon_taxonomy, by = "resolved_name")

save_both(distinctiveness_data_full, "distinctiveness_data_full")

# =============================================================================
# 1c. Sensitivity check: PERMANOVA with taxa detected at every site removed
# =============================================================================
# Numbered 1c for narrative order (it belongs with the other PERMANOVA
# checks), but placed after section 3 because it uses the occurrence bins.
# Tests whether taxa detected at all sites (the last bin in DIST_LEVELS)
# drive site separation or dilute it.
#
# Samples whose only taxa were all in that bin become empty once those taxa
# are removed and drop out, since a zero-taxon row has no Jaccard distance.
# To keep the comparison matched, the full-taxon PERMANOVA is rerun on the
# same reduced set of samples, so the only difference between the two
# results is the removed taxa.

all_site_taxa <- occurrence %>%
  filter(bin == DIST_LEVELS[length(DIST_LEVELS)]) %>%
  pull(resolved_name)

cat("Taxa detected at all", N_SITES_TOTAL, "sites:", length(all_site_taxa), "\n")
print(all_site_taxa)

sample_long_no_ubiq <- sample_long %>%
  filter(!resolved_name %in% all_site_taxa)

samples_before <- n_distinct(sample_long$sample_id)
samples_after  <- n_distinct(sample_long_no_ubiq$sample_id)
cat(sprintf("Samples with at least one remaining taxon: %d of %d (%d dropped)\n",
            samples_after, samples_before, samples_before - samples_after))

sample_mat_no_ubiq <- sample_long_no_ubiq %>%
  select(-canonical_site) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = resolved_name, values_from = present, values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample_id") %>%
  as.matrix()

sample_meta_no_ubiq <- sample_meta %>%
  filter(sample_id %in% rownames(sample_mat_no_ubiq))
sample_meta_no_ubiq <- sample_meta_no_ubiq[match(rownames(sample_mat_no_ubiq), sample_meta_no_ubiq$sample_id), ]
stopifnot(all(sample_meta_no_ubiq$sample_id == rownames(sample_mat_no_ubiq)))

sample_jaccard_no_ubiq <- vegdist(sample_mat_no_ubiq, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE)

permanova_result_no_ubiq <- adonis2(
  sample_jaccard_no_ubiq ~ canonical_site,
  data = sample_meta_no_ubiq,
  permutations = N_PERM,
  by = NULL
)
print(permanova_result_no_ubiq)
saveRDS(permanova_result_no_ubiq, file.path(stats_dir, "permanova_result_no_ubiquitous.rds"))
capture.output(permanova_result_no_ubiq, file = file.path(stats_dir, "permanova_result_no_ubiquitous.txt"))

# Matched comparison: all taxa, same samples as above
matched_ids <- sample_meta_no_ubiq$sample_id
sample_jaccard_matched <- as.dist(as.matrix(sample_jaccard)[matched_ids, matched_ids])

permanova_result_matched <- adonis2(
  sample_jaccard_matched ~ canonical_site,
  data = sample_meta_no_ubiq,
  permutations = N_PERM,
  by = NULL
)
print(permanova_result_matched)
saveRDS(permanova_result_matched, file.path(stats_dir, "permanova_result_matched_all_taxa.rds"))
capture.output(permanova_result_matched, file = file.path(stats_dir, "permanova_result_matched_all_taxa.txt"))

# =============================================================================
# 4. Sample-level PCoA, Jaccard
# =============================================================================
# Every point is one site-date sample. Any site position drawn later (e.g.,
# a centroid) is the mean of that site's sample positions, not a separately
# pooled profile. % variance is computed from positive eigenvalues only,
# for the same reason as the Bray-Curtis PCoA in 1b.

sample_pcoa_fit <- pcoa(sample_jaccard)

eig_j     <- sample_pcoa_fit$values$Eigenvalues
pos_eig_j <- eig_j[eig_j > 0]
neg_eig_j <- eig_j[eig_j < 0]
cat(sprintf("Jaccard PCoA: %d negative eigenvalues (sum = %.1f) vs positive sum = %.1f. %% variance from positive eigenvalues only.\n",
            length(neg_eig_j), sum(neg_eig_j), sum(pos_eig_j)))

sample_pct_var <- round(eig_j[1:2] / sum(pos_eig_j) * 100, 1)

# 2D fit error: sqrt( sum((d - d')^2) / sum(d^2) ), where d is the original
# sample-to-sample distance (the same one PERMANOVA uses) and d' is the
# Euclidean distance between the plotted 2D coordinates, summed over all
# sample pairs. 0 means the 2D plot reproduces the distances exactly.
fitted_2d_dist <- dist(as.matrix(sample_pcoa_fit$vectors[, 1:2]))
pcoa_stress <- sqrt(sum((as.vector(sample_jaccard) - as.vector(fitted_2d_dist))^2) /
                       sum(as.vector(sample_jaccard)^2))
cat("Sample-level Jaccard PCoA 2D fit error:", round(pcoa_stress, 4), "\n")
saveRDS(pcoa_stress, file.path(stats_dir, "pcoa_stress.rds"))
write_csv(tibble(metric = "sample_pcoa_2d_fit_error", value = pcoa_stress),
          file.path(stats_dir, "pcoa_stress.csv"))

sample_scores <- as.data.frame(sample_pcoa_fit$vectors[, 1:2]) %>%
  rename(PCoA1 = Axis.1, PCoA2 = Axis.2) %>%
  rownames_to_column("sample_id") %>%
  left_join(sample_meta, by = "sample_id") %>%
  left_join(site_state_lookup, by = "canonical_site") %>%
  mutate(pct_var1 = sample_pct_var[1], pct_var2 = sample_pct_var[2])

save_both(sample_scores, "sample_pcoa_scores")

cat("\nSite fingerprint stats written to", stats_dir, "\n")

# ---- Summary ------------------------------------------------------------------
# The same numbers are in the .csv files in stats_dir and are printed again
# by manuscript-stats.

site_richness <- site_long_for_heatmap %>% count(canonical_site, name = "n_taxa") %>% arrange(n_taxa)
site_richness_labeled <- site_richness %>% mutate(site_label = unname(shorthand_lookup[canonical_site]))

# Two denominators. samples_in_data counts the samples that survive the
# standard filter with at least one non-human taxon, which is what this
# script works from. samples_in_table_s1 is the collection count published in
# Table S1. They differ because a few samples have no non-human detection, so
# a reader recomputing this correlation from Table S1 gets a different rho.
# Both are reported. The manuscript quotes the filtered-sample version (rho = 0.33).
site_n_samples <- df %>% distinct(canonical_site, sample_id) %>%
  count(canonical_site, name = "n_samples")
site_n_samples_s1 <- site_table %>%
  transmute(canonical_site, n_samples_s1 = `n samples`)

rich_vs_n <- site_richness %>%
  left_join(site_n_samples, by = "canonical_site") %>%
  left_join(site_n_samples_s1, by = "canonical_site")
rich_vs_n_test_s1 <- cor.test(rich_vs_n$n_samples_s1, rich_vs_n$n_taxa,
                              method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
save_both(tibble(rho = unname(rich_vs_n_test_s1$estimate), p = rich_vs_n_test_s1$p.value,
                 n_sites = nrow(rich_vs_n)), "richness_vs_samples_test_table_s1")
rich_vs_n_test <- cor.test(rich_vs_n$n_samples, rich_vs_n$n_taxa,
                           method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
save_both(tibble(rho = unname(rich_vs_n_test$estimate), p = rich_vs_n_test$p.value,
                 n_sites = nrow(rich_vs_n)), "richness_vs_samples_test")
save_both(rich_vs_n %>% mutate(site_label = unname(shorthand_lookup[canonical_site])), "richness_by_site")
save_both(occurrence, "taxon_occurrence")

cat("\n===================================================================\n")
cat(" SITE FINGERPRINT STATS: SUMMARY\n")
cat("===================================================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Sites: %d | Site-date samples: %d | Non-human taxa (family/genus/species, filtered, TAXON_MERGES applied): %d\n",
            n_distinct(df$canonical_site), n_distinct(df$sample_id), n_distinct(df$resolved_name)))

cat(sprintf("\nPERMANOVA (sample-level Jaccard ~ canonical_site, %d permutations):\n", N_PERM))
cat(sprintf("  pseudo-F = %.2f, R\u00b2 = %.3f, p = %.3f\n",
            permanova_result$F[1], permanova_result$R2[1], permanova_result$`Pr(>F)`[1]))

cat("\nPERMANOVA, Bray-Curtis on relative abundance:\n")
cat(sprintf("  pseudo-F = %.2f, R\u00b2 = %.3f, p = %.3f\n",
            permanova_result_bray$F[1], permanova_result_bray$R2[1], permanova_result_bray$`Pr(>F)`[1]))

cat("\nbetadisper (within-site dispersion):\n")
print(as.data.frame(betadisper_overall %>%
                      select(distance, F, p, size_vs_dispersion_rho, size_vs_dispersion_p)),
      digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)

cat(sprintf("\nPERMANOVA, taxa at all sites removed vs all taxa, matched on %d samples:\n",
            length(matched_ids)))
cat(sprintf("  all taxa: R\u00b2 = %.3f, p = %.3f | removed: R\u00b2 = %.3f, p = %.3f\n",
            permanova_result_matched$R2[1], permanova_result_matched$`Pr(>F)`[1],
            permanova_result_no_ubiq$R2[1], permanova_result_no_ubiq$`Pr(>F)`[1]))

cat("\nSample-level PCoA:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Jaccard: PCoA1 = %.1f%%, PCoA2 = %.1f%%, 2D fit error = %.3f\n",
            sample_pct_var[1], sample_pct_var[2], pcoa_stress))
cat(sprintf("  Bray-Curtis: PCoA1 = %.1f%%, PCoA2 = %.1f%%, 2D fit error = %.3f\n",
            sample_pct_var_bray[1], sample_pct_var_bray[2], pcoa_stress_bray))

cat("\nPer-site taxon richness (pooled, post-filter):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Range: %d taxa (%s) to %d taxa (%s)\n",
            min(site_richness$n_taxa), site_richness_labeled$site_label[1],
            max(site_richness$n_taxa), site_richness_labeled$site_label[nrow(site_richness_labeled)]))
cat(sprintf("  vs samples per site: Spearman rho = %.2f, p = %.3f\n",
            rich_vs_n_test$estimate, rich_vs_n_test$p.value))
cat(sprintf("  vs samples per site (Table S1 collection counts): Spearman rho = %.2f, p = %.3f\n",
            rich_vs_n_test_s1$estimate, rich_vs_n_test_s1$p.value))
cat("  Lowest 3:\n")
print(head(site_richness_labeled %>% select(site_label, n_taxa), 3), row.names = FALSE)
cat("  Highest 3:\n")
print(tail(site_richness_labeled %>% select(site_label, n_taxa), 3), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nTaxa per occurrence bin (number of sites detecting each taxon):\n")
print(as.data.frame(occurrence %>%
                      count(bin) %>%
                      mutate(bin = factor(bin, levels = DIST_LEVELS)) %>%
                      arrange(bin)),
      row.names = FALSE)
cat("===================================================================\n")
```


```{r sample-counts}
# =========================================================================
# Samples by what passed the detection filter
# =========================================================================
# Splits every sample (site-date) into three groups, after the standard
# detection filter:
#   No chordate reads   nothing passed the filter
#   Human only          only human (Homo or Hominidae) passed
#   Non-human           at least one non-human taxon passed
# The non-human group is the sample set used by the ordinations,
# PERMANOVA and diversity analyses (fingerprint-stats). The other two
# groups are the samples those analyses leave out.
#
# Samples: every parsed site-date up to STUDY_END_DATE, as in
# per-taxon-glmm. Human and the ambiguous Phasianidae/Bovidae family calls
# are handled as in fingerprint-stats.
# Output: stats_dir/sample_counts_by_group.csv (overall and per site)

if (!exists("all_parsed")) {
  all_parsed <- read_csv(parsed_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(canonical_site = recode_site(canonical_site))
}

count_samples <- all_parsed %>%
  distinct(canonical_site, date) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) %>%
  filter(date <= STUDY_END_DATE)

count_passed <- load_detections(drop_human = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(is_human = is_human(genus, family)) %>%
  group_by(canonical_site, date) %>%
  summarise(any_human = any(is_human), any_nonhuman = any(!is_human), .groups = "drop")

count_groups <- count_samples %>%
  left_join(count_passed, by = c("canonical_site", "date")) %>%
  mutate(group = case_when(
    is.na(any_human) & is.na(any_nonhuman) ~ "No chordate reads",
    any_nonhuman                           ~ "Non-human",
    TRUE                                   ~ "Human only"
  ))

count_overall <- count_groups %>%
  count(group, name = "samples") %>%
  mutate(canonical_site = "All sites")
count_by_site <- count_groups %>%
  count(canonical_site, group, name = "samples")

count_table <- bind_rows(count_overall, count_by_site) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = samples, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(Total = rowSums(across(any_of(c("No chordate reads", "Human only", "Non-human")))))
write_csv(count_table, file.path(stats_dir, "sample_counts_by_group.csv"))

cat("\nSamples by what passed the detection filter:\n")
print(as.data.frame(count_overall %>% select(group, samples)), row.names = FALSE)

# Check against the ordination sample set made in fingerprint-stats
n_nonhuman <- sum(count_groups$group == "Non-human")
n_ord <- n_distinct(sample_meta$sample_id)
if (n_nonhuman != n_ord) {
  warning("Non-human samples here (", n_nonhuman, ") differ from the ordination sample set (",
          n_ord, "). Check that both use the same filter.")
}
```


```{r figure3-figure4-pcoa}
# Figure 3: per-site distinctiveness (a) and pooled Jaccard similarity
# heatmap (b).
# Figure 4: sample-level Jaccard PCoA (a) and what each axis tracks: mean
# richness vs PCoA1 (b) and mean fish fraction vs PCoA2 (c).
# Supplementary Figure (bray_curtis_pcoa): the same for Bray-Curtis: PCoA (a), pig relative
# abundance vs PCoA1 (b), and evenness vs PCoA2 (c).
# Supplementary Figure (pcoa_by_site): the Jaccard PCoA with one panel per site.
# Supplementary Tables 3 and 5: taxa by number of sites detected (Figure
# 3a) and pairwise Jaccard similarity (Figure 3b).
#
# Correlations between PCoA axes and sample properties are Spearman, at the
# sample level and on site means. Samples from one site are repeated over
# time and are not independent, so the site-mean correlations (n = 27) are
# the ones to cite for inference; the sample-level values describe the
# same pattern across all samples.
#
# Reads the .rds files written by fingerprint-stats; run that chunk first
# if the data change.

FIG3_WIDTH_MM  <- 136   # 1.5 column
FIG3_HEIGHT_MM <- 170

FIG4_WIDTH_MM  <- 180
FIG4_HEIGHT_MM <- 95    # Figure 4 and the Bray-Curtis supplementary figure
FIG4_DOT_COLOR <- "black"
FIG4_CA_POINT_SIZE <- 0.7   # California samples in panel a, smaller so Hawaii shows through

# Text and legend sizes shared by every panel in Figures 3 and 4.
SITE_FP_BASE_SIZE    <- 6.5
SITE_FP_AXIS_TEXT    <- 6
SITE_FP_AXIS_TITLE   <- 6.5
SITE_FP_LEGEND_TITLE <- 6.5
SITE_FP_LEGEND_TEXT  <- 6
SITE_FP_LEGEND_KEY   <- unit(3, "mm")

site_fp_compact_legend <- theme(
  legend.title = element_text(size = SITE_FP_LEGEND_TITLE),
  legend.text  = element_text(size = SITE_FP_LEGEND_TEXT),
  legend.key.size = SITE_FP_LEGEND_KEY,
  legend.spacing = unit(2, "mm"),
  legend.background = element_blank(),
  legend.box.background = element_rect(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3, fill = "white"),
  legend.margin = LEGEND_BOX_MARGIN
)

# Occurrence bins, colors, and the rare/common split are DIST_LEVELS,
# DIST_COLORS, DIST_RARE_BINS and DIST_COMMON_BINS (post-parse-filters), the
# same bins fingerprint-stats writes into distinctiveness_data. The legend uses
# the same labels.
DIST_LABELS_SHORT <- DIST_LEVELS

FISH_CLASSES <- c("Actinopteri", "Actinopterygii", "Chondrichthyes", "Cephalaspidomorphi")

# ---- Load stats outputs, recode to shorthand labels ------------------------
read_stat <- function(name) readRDS(file.path(stats_dir, paste0(name, ".rds")))

shorthand_lookup <- read_site_labels() %>%
  select(current_site_label, shorthand_for_figures) %>%
  deframe()
to_shorthand <- function(x) unname(shorthand_lookup[x])

site_order_regional <- to_shorthand(read_stat("site_order_regional"))
site_cluster_order  <- to_shorthand(read_stat("site_cluster_order"))

site_similarity <- read_stat("site_similarity_long") %>%
  mutate(site_a = to_shorthand(site_a), site_b = to_shorthand(site_b))

distinctiveness_data <- read_stat("distinctiveness_data") %>%
  mutate(canonical_site = to_shorthand(canonical_site))

sample_scores_raw <- read_stat("sample_pcoa_scores")   # canonical_site codes kept, needed to join richness below
sample_scores <- sample_scores_raw %>% mutate(canonical_site = to_shorthand(canonical_site))

permanova_result <- read_stat("permanova_result")
pcoa_stress       <- read_stat("pcoa_stress")

# "2D fit error" is a normalized residual: 0 = the 2D plot reproduces the
# distances exactly, higher = worse.
permanova_label <- sprintf(
  "PERMANOVA: R\u00b2 = %.2f, p = %.3f\n2D fit error = %.3f",
  permanova_result$R2[1], permanova_result$`Pr(>F)`[1], pcoa_stress
)

# =========================================================================
# FIGURE 3, Panel a: per-site distinctiveness, diverging bars
# =========================================================================
# Taxa found at few sites (1, 2, or 3-5 sites) extend left of zero; taxa
# found at many sites (6-13, 14-26, or all 27) extend right. The darkest shade is at the outer end of each side. Colors
# do not reuse the vertebrate class colors.

# Site order for panel a:
#   "regional"         = same region/state order as Figures 1, 2 and 5
#   "rare"             = sorted by number of taxa on the rare (pink) side,
#                        most at the top; ties broken by taxa unique to the
#                        site, then by total taxa
#   "unique"           = sorted by number of taxa unique to the site (the
#                        dark pink segment), most at the top
#   "distinctiveness"  = sorted by share of taxa on the rare side, most
#                        distinctive at the top
FIG3A_SORT <- "rare"

dist_counts <- distinctiveness_data %>%
  mutate(bin = factor(bin, levels = DIST_LEVELS)) %>%
  complete(canonical_site, bin, fill = list(n = 0))

# Share of a site's taxa on the rare side (same order as the rare/common
# ratio, but defined even if a side is zero). Saved either way; used for
# ordering only when FIG3A_SORT = "distinctiveness" (ties broken by the
# rare count).
dist_order <- dist_counts %>%
  group_by(canonical_site) %>%
  summarise(n_rare = sum(n[bin %in% DIST_RARE_BINS]),
            n_unique = sum(n[bin == DIST_LEVELS[1]]),
            n_total = sum(n),
            rare_share = n_rare / n_total, .groups = "drop")

# Larger y is drawn higher, so sorting ascending puts the top site last.
dist_order <- if (FIG3A_SORT == "regional") {
  # first site in site_order_regional at the top
  dist_order %>% mutate(y = length(site_order_regional) + 1 -
                          match(canonical_site, site_order_regional))
} else if (FIG3A_SORT == "rare") {
  dist_order %>% arrange(n_rare, n_unique, n_total) %>% mutate(y = row_number())
} else if (FIG3A_SORT == "unique") {
  dist_order %>% arrange(n_unique, n_rare, n_total) %>% mutate(y = row_number())
} else {
  dist_order %>% arrange(rare_share, n_rare) %>% mutate(y = row_number())
}
dist_order <- dist_order %>% arrange(y)

write_csv(dist_order %>% arrange(desc(y)) %>% select(-y),
          file.path(stats_dir, "distinctiveness_rare_share_by_site.csv"))

# Bars stack outward from zero: rare bins left (3-5, 2, 1 site), common bins
# right (6-13, 14-26, all 27).
dist_rects <- dist_counts %>%
  left_join(dist_order %>% select(canonical_site, y), by = "canonical_site") %>%
  mutate(side = if_else(bin %in% DIST_RARE_BINS, "rare", "common"),
         stack_rank = case_when(
           side == "rare"   ~ match(as.character(bin), rev(DIST_RARE_BINS)),
           side == "common" ~ match(as.character(bin), DIST_COMMON_BINS))) %>%
  arrange(canonical_site, side, stack_rank) %>%
  group_by(canonical_site, side) %>%
  mutate(outer = cumsum(n), inner = outer - n) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(sign = if_else(side == "rare", -1, 1),
         xmin = sign * inner, xmax = sign * outer) %>%
  filter(n > 0)

dist_x_max <- max(abs(c(dist_rects$xmin, dist_rects$xmax)))
dist_breaks <- scales::pretty_breaks(n = 4)(c(0, dist_x_max))
dist_breaks <- sort(unique(c(-dist_breaks, dist_breaks)))

p_dist <- ggplot(dist_rects) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = y - 0.38, ymax = y + 0.38, fill = bin),
            color = "black", linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
  annotate("text", x = -dist_x_max * 0.02, y = nrow(dist_order) + 1.1, hjust = 1,
           label = "\u2190 Found at fewer sites", size = SITE_FP_AXIS_TEXT / .pt) +
  annotate("text", x = dist_x_max * 0.02, y = nrow(dist_order) + 1.1, hjust = 0,
           label = "Found at more sites \u2192", size = SITE_FP_AXIS_TEXT / .pt) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = DIST_COLORS, breaks = DIST_LEVELS, labels = DIST_LABELS_SHORT,
                    name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = dist_breaks, labels = abs(dist_breaks),
                     limits = c(-dist_x_max, dist_x_max) * 1.03, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = dist_order$y, labels = dist_order$canonical_site,
                     limits = c(0.4, nrow(dist_order) + 1.6), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)) +
  labs(x = "Number of taxa", y = "Site") +
  theme_bw(base_size = SITE_FP_BASE_SIZE) +
  theme(axis.text   = element_text(size = SITE_FP_AXIS_TEXT, color = "black"),
        axis.title  = element_text(size = SITE_FP_AXIS_TITLE, color = "black"),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.box.spacing = unit(1.5, "mm"),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 5, r = 5, b = 2, l = 5)) +
  site_fp_compact_legend

# =========================================================================
# FIGURE 3, Panel b: pooled site-level Jaccard similarity heatmap
# =========================================================================

build_jaccard_heatmap <- function(order_vec, axis_text_size, force_square = TRUE) {
  sim_long <- site_similarity %>%
    mutate(site_a = factor(site_a, levels = order_vec),
           site_b = factor(site_b, levels = order_vec))

  p <- ggplot(sim_long, aes(site_b, site_a, fill = similarity)) +
    geom_tile(color = HEAT_GRID_COLOR, linewidth = HEAT_GRID_WIDTH) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colors = HEAT_12S_COLORS,
      limits = c(0, 1)
    ) +
    labs(x = "Site", y = "Site", fill = "Jaccard\nsimilarity") +
    theme_bw(base_size = SITE_FP_BASE_SIZE) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = axis_text_size, color = "black"),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = axis_text_size, color = "black"),
          axis.title  = element_text(size = SITE_FP_AXIS_TITLE, color = "black"),
          panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
          panel.grid = element_blank()) +
    site_fp_compact_legend

  if (force_square) p <- p + coord_fixed()
  p
}

p_heatmap_clustered <- build_jaccard_heatmap(site_cluster_order, axis_text_size = SITE_FP_AXIS_TEXT)
# Analysis only (not in the manuscript): the heatmap on its own, larger
save_figure(p_heatmap_clustered, "jaccard_heatmap_clustered", width = 150, height = 140, dir = analysis_dir)

# =========================================================================
# FIGURE 3, combined: a on top, b below
# =========================================================================
# Panel a (horizontal bars) sits above panel b. Panel b is kept square
# (coord_fixed) at the size its row allows.

p_fig3_combined <- cowplot::plot_grid(
  p_dist,
  build_jaccard_heatmap(site_cluster_order, axis_text_size = SITE_FP_AXIS_TEXT - 0.5, force_square = TRUE),
  labels = c("a", "b"), label_size = FIG_PANEL_LABEL_PT, nrow = 2, rel_heights = c(0.85, 1)
)
p_fig3_combined <- cowplot::ggdraw(p_fig3_combined) +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))

save_figure(p_fig3_combined, fig_file("distinctiveness_similarity"), width = FIG3_WIDTH_MM, height = FIG3_HEIGHT_MM)
p_fig3_combined

# =========================================================================
# Figure 4 data (Jaccard): richness and fish fraction per sample, panels b-c
# =========================================================================
# Same exclusions as fingerprint-stats: ambiguous families removed, and
# human removed by genus/family so family-level Hominidae reads do not
# count toward richness.

df_detect <- load_detections() %>%
  mutate(sample_id = paste(canonical_site, date, sep = "_"))

taxon_presence <- df_detect %>% distinct(sample_id, resolved_name, class)

per_sample <- taxon_presence %>%
  group_by(sample_id) %>%
  summarise(
    richness = n_distinct(resolved_name),
    n_fish   = sum(class %in% FISH_CLASSES),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(fish_fraction = n_fish / richness)

combined_scores <- sample_scores_raw %>% left_join(per_sample, by = "sample_id")

if (any(is.na(combined_scores$richness))) {
  warning(sum(is.na(combined_scores$richness)), " samples had no matching richness/fish-fraction ",
          "value. Check that chordate_perfect_match.csv hasn't changed since fingerprint-stats was last run.")
}

pcoa_site_means <- combined_scores %>%
  group_by(canonical_site) %>%
  summarise(
    n_samples          = n(),
    mean_richness      = mean(richness),
    mean_PCoA1         = mean(PCoA1),
    mean_fish_fraction = mean(fish_fraction),
    mean_PCoA2         = mean(PCoA2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(site_label = to_shorthand(canonical_site))

write_csv(pcoa_site_means, file.path(stats_dir, "richness_fishyness_pcoa_by_site.csv"))

# Spearman correlations throughout (several variables are not normally
# distributed). exact = FALSE because richness has ties.
richness_test <- cor.test(combined_scores$richness, combined_scores$PCoA1, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
fishy_test    <- cor.test(combined_scores$fish_fraction, combined_scores$PCoA2, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
richness_test_site <- cor.test(pcoa_site_means$mean_richness, pcoa_site_means$mean_PCoA1, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
fishy_test_site    <- cor.test(pcoa_site_means$mean_fish_fraction, pcoa_site_means$mean_PCoA2, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

saveRDS(list(richness_test = richness_test, fishy_test = fishy_test,
             richness_test_site = richness_test_site, fishy_test_site = fishy_test_site),
        file.path(stats_dir, "richness_fishy_correlation_tests.rds"))

fmt_stat_label <- function(test) {
  p_str <- if (test$p.value < 0.001) "p < 0.001" else sprintf("p = %.3f", test$p.value)
  sprintf("\u03c1 = %.3f, %s", test$estimate, p_str)
}

# =========================================================================
# Bray-Curtis supplementary figure data: pig relative abundance and
# evenness per sample
# =========================================================================
# Pig relative abundance tracks Bray-Curtis PCoA1 and Pielou's evenness
# (J = Shannon H / log(richness)) tracks PCoA2. Samples with one taxon have
# undefined evenness and are left out of the evenness panel only.

sample_scores_bray_raw <- read_stat("sample_pcoa_scores_bray")
sample_scores_bray <- sample_scores_bray_raw %>% mutate(canonical_site = to_shorthand(canonical_site))

permanova_result_bray <- read_stat("permanova_result_bray")
pcoa_stress_bray       <- read_stat("pcoa_stress_bray")

permanova_label_bray <- sprintf(
  "PERMANOVA: R\u00b2 = %.2f, p = %.3f\n2D fit error = %.3f",
  permanova_result_bray$R2[1], permanova_result_bray$`Pr(>F)`[1], pcoa_stress_bray
)

relabund_mat <- read_stat("sample_relabund_mat")
relabund_mat <- relabund_mat[sample_scores_bray_raw$sample_id, , drop = FALSE]

pig_col <- "Sus scrofa"
pig_relabund <- if (pig_col %in% colnames(relabund_mat)) relabund_mat[, pig_col] else 0

shannon_h <- apply(relabund_mat, 1, function(p) {
  p <- p[p > 0]
  -sum(p * log(p))
})
richness_for_evenness <- apply(relabund_mat > 0, 1, sum)
evenness <- ifelse(richness_for_evenness > 1, shannon_h / log(richness_for_evenness), NA_real_)

combined_scores_bray <- sample_scores_bray_raw %>%
  mutate(pig_relabund = pig_relabund, evenness = evenness)

pcoa_site_means_bray <- combined_scores_bray %>%
  group_by(canonical_site) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_PCoA1_bray    = mean(PCoA1_bray),
    mean_PCoA2_bray    = mean(PCoA2_bray),
    mean_pig_relabund  = mean(pig_relabund),
    mean_evenness      = mean(evenness, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(site_label = to_shorthand(canonical_site))

write_csv(pcoa_site_means_bray, file.path(stats_dir, "braycurtis_axis_drivers_by_site.csv"))

pig_test_bray  <- cor.test(pcoa_site_means_bray$mean_pig_relabund, pcoa_site_means_bray$mean_PCoA1_bray, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
even_test_bray <- cor.test(pcoa_site_means_bray$mean_evenness, pcoa_site_means_bray$mean_PCoA2_bray, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

# Leave-one-out check: Ottumwa is a single extreme point (pig ~80% of its
# signal) and could drive the pig correlation on its own.
pig_test_bray_no_ottumwa <- cor.test(
  pcoa_site_means_bray$mean_pig_relabund[pcoa_site_means_bray$canonical_site != "IA_Ottumwa_WPCF"],
  pcoa_site_means_bray$mean_PCoA1_bray[pcoa_site_means_bray$canonical_site != "IA_Ottumwa_WPCF"],
  method = "spearman", exact = FALSE
)
saveRDS(list(pig_test_bray = pig_test_bray, even_test_bray = even_test_bray,
             pig_test_bray_no_ottumwa = pig_test_bray_no_ottumwa),
        file.path(stats_dir, "braycurtis_correlation_tests.rds"))

cat("\n===================================================================\n")
cat(" FIGURE 4: SUMMARY\n")
cat("===================================================================\n")

cat(sprintf("  richness vs PCoA1:      rho = %.3f, p = %.3e\n", richness_test$estimate, richness_test$p.value))
cat(sprintf("  fish_fraction vs PCoA2: rho = %.3f, p = %.3e\n", fishy_test$estimate, fishy_test$p.value))
cat(sprintf("\nSite-level, Jaccard (n = %d site means, Figure 4b-c):\n", nrow(pcoa_site_means)))
cat(sprintf("  mean_richness vs mean_PCoA1:      %s\n", fmt_stat_label(richness_test_site)))
cat(sprintf("  mean_fish_fraction vs mean_PCoA2: %s\n", fmt_stat_label(fishy_test_site)))
cat(sprintf("\nSite-level, Bray-Curtis (n = %d site means, Bray-Curtis supplementary figure):\n", nrow(pcoa_site_means_bray)))
cat(sprintf("  mean_pig_relabund vs mean_PCoA1_bray:            %s\n", fmt_stat_label(pig_test_bray)))
cat(sprintf("  mean_pig_relabund vs mean_PCoA1_bray, no Ottumwa: %s\n", fmt_stat_label(pig_test_bray_no_ottumwa)))
cat(sprintf("  mean_evenness vs mean_PCoA2_bray:                 %s\n", fmt_stat_label(even_test_bray)))
cat("===================================================================\n")

# =========================================================================
# Theil-Sen fit lines with bootstrapped 95% band (axis-driver panels)
# =========================================================================
# Theil-Sen line: the median of the slopes between every pair of sites,
# intercept = median of y - slope * x. Like Spearman's rho it is rank
# based, so one extreme site cannot pull it. The band is a percentile
# bootstrap: sites are resampled FIG4_TS_N_BOOT times, the line is refit
# each time, and the band covers the middle 95% at each x.
FIG4_TS_N_BOOT <- 1000
FIG4_TS_SEED   <- 42

theil_sen_fit <- function(x, y) {
  idx <- combn(length(x), 2)
  slopes <- (y[idx[2, ]] - y[idx[1, ]]) / (x[idx[2, ]] - x[idx[1, ]])
  slope <- median(slopes[is.finite(slopes)])   # pairs with tied x have no slope
  c(intercept = median(y - slope * x), slope = slope)
}

theil_sen_band <- function(x, y, n_boot = FIG4_TS_N_BOOT, level = 0.95,
                           n_grid = 100, seed = FIG4_TS_SEED) {
  ok <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(y)
  x <- x[ok]
  y <- y[ok]
  grid <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = n_grid)
  fit <- theil_sen_fit(x, y)
  set.seed(seed)
  boot_pred <- replicate(n_boot, {
    i <- sample(length(x), replace = TRUE)
    b <- theil_sen_fit(x[i], y[i])
    b[["intercept"]] + b[["slope"]] * grid
  })
  alpha <- (1 - level) / 2
  tibble(
    x   = grid,
    fit = fit[["intercept"]] + fit[["slope"]] * grid,
    lo  = apply(boot_pred, 1, quantile, probs = alpha, na.rm = TRUE),
    hi  = apply(boot_pred, 1, quantile, probs = 1 - alpha, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

# Ribbon and line layers
ts_layers <- function(band) {
  list(
    geom_ribbon(data = band, aes(x = x, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), inherit.aes = FALSE,
                fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.6),
    geom_line(data = band, aes(x = x, y = fit), inherit.aes = FALSE,
              color = "black", linewidth = 0.45)
  )
}

ts_richness <- theil_sen_band(pcoa_site_means$mean_richness,          pcoa_site_means$mean_PCoA1)
ts_fishy    <- theil_sen_band(pcoa_site_means$mean_fish_fraction,     pcoa_site_means$mean_PCoA2)
ts_pig      <- theil_sen_band(pcoa_site_means_bray$mean_pig_relabund, pcoa_site_means_bray$mean_PCoA1_bray)
ts_evenness <- theil_sen_band(pcoa_site_means_bray$mean_evenness,     pcoa_site_means_bray$mean_PCoA2_bray)

# Full-data Theil-Sen slopes (for the text)
ts_slope <- function(x, y) {
  ok <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(y)
  theil_sen_fit(x[ok], y[ok])[["slope"]]
}
ts_slopes <- tibble(
  panel = c("b: richness vs PCoA1", "c: fish fraction vs PCoA2",
            "e: pig vs PCoA1 (Bray-Curtis)", "f: evenness vs PCoA2 (Bray-Curtis)"),
  slope = c(ts_slope(pcoa_site_means$mean_richness,          pcoa_site_means$mean_PCoA1),
            ts_slope(pcoa_site_means$mean_fish_fraction,     pcoa_site_means$mean_PCoA2),
            ts_slope(pcoa_site_means_bray$mean_pig_relabund, pcoa_site_means_bray$mean_PCoA1_bray),
            ts_slope(pcoa_site_means_bray$mean_evenness,     pcoa_site_means_bray$mean_PCoA2_bray))
)
write_csv(ts_slopes, file.path(stats_dir, "figure4_theil_sen_slopes.csv"))

# =========================================================================
# Figure 4, panels b-c: what Jaccard PCoA1 and PCoA2 track

# The y range covers all samples, set with coord_cartesian() so no rows are

shared_y_limits <- range(c(combined_scores$PCoA1, combined_scores$PCoA2,
                            pcoa_site_means$mean_PCoA1, pcoa_site_means$mean_PCoA2))
shared_y_limits <- shared_y_limits + c(-1, 1) * 0.05 * diff(shared_y_limits)

p_richness_pcoa1 <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = combined_scores, aes(richness, PCoA1, color = state),

p_fishy_pcoa2 <- ggplot() +

shared_y_limits_bray <- range(c(combined_scores_bray$PCoA1_bray, combined_scores_bray$PCoA2_bray,

p_pig_pcoa1 <- ggplot() +

# =========================================================================

build_axis_figure <- function(p_ord, p_axis1, p_axis2) {
  drivers <- cowplot::plot_grid(p_axis1, p_axis2, ncol = 1, labels = c("b", "c"), label_size = FIG_PANEL_LABEL_PT,
                                align = "v", axis = "lr")

                            labels = c("a", "", ""), label_size = FIG_PANEL_LABEL_PT)

}

# Figure 4: presence/absence (Jaccard)

# =========================================================================
# Supplementary Figure (pcoa_by_site): Jaccard PCoA small multiples. Each site's samples
# (crimson) against all other samples (gray), the site centroid
# (x), and the site's within-site dispersion (betadisper).
# =========================================================================

# One color for every site's own samples, so each panel reads simply as
# "this site against all others".
PCOA_PANEL_COLOR <- "#DC143C"   # crimson

background <- sample_scores %>%
  select(PCoA1, PCoA2) %>%
  tidyr::crossing(facet_panel = factor(unique(sample_scores$canonical_site), levels = site_order_regional))

foreground <- sample_scores %>%
  rename(facet_panel = canonical_site) %>%
  mutate(facet_panel = factor(facet_panel, levels = site_order_regional))

panel_centroids <- foreground %>%
  group_by(facet_panel) %>%
  summarise(PCoA1 = mean(PCoA1), PCoA2 = mean(PCoA2), .groups = "drop")

# Within-site dispersion from betadisper (fingerprint-stats): mean Jaccard
# distance of the site's samples to the site's spatial median, in the full
# ordination space. Larger = samples less alike. The test of whether
# dispersion differs among sites is reported in the text.
panel_dispersion <- read_stat("betadisper_per_site") %>%
  filter(distance == "jaccard") %>%
  transmute(facet_panel = factor(site_label, levels = site_order_regional),
            label = sprintf("Dispersion = %.2f", mean_dist_to_median))

p_small_multiples <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = background, aes(PCoA1, PCoA2), color = "grey80", size = 0.5, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_point(data = foreground, aes(PCoA1, PCoA2), color = PCOA_PANEL_COLOR, size = 1, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_point(data = panel_centroids, aes(PCoA1, PCoA2), color = "black", shape = 4, size = 2.5, stroke = 0.6) +
  geom_text(data = panel_dispersion, aes(x = -Inf, y = -Inf, label = label),
            hjust = -0.05, vjust = -0.5, size = (SITE_FP_AXIS_TEXT - 0.5) / .pt) +
  facet_wrap(~facet_panel, ncol = 6, labeller = labeller(facet_panel = label_wrap_gen(width = 18))) +
  theme_bw(base_size = SITE_FP_BASE_SIZE) +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        axis.title = element_text(size = SITE_FP_AXIS_TITLE, color = "black"),
        strip.text = element_text(size = SITE_FP_AXIS_TITLE, color = "black", lineheight = 0.85),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90", color = "black", linewidth = 0.3),
        panel.spacing = unit(2, "mm"), legend.position = "none",
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))

save_figure(p_small_multiples, supp_fig_file("pcoa_by_site"), dir = supp_dir, width = 180, height = 165)
p_small_multiples

cat("\nFigure 3, Figure 4 (Jaccard ordination and drivers), the Bray-Curtis\n",
    "supplementary figure, and", supp_fig_ref("pcoa_by_site"), "(small multiples) written.\n")

# =========================================================================
# Supplementary Table (taxa_by_site): taxa by number of sites detected, with the sites
# where each was found.
# =========================================================================

common_names_supp <- read_common_names()

distinctiveness_full <- read_stat("distinctiveness_data_full") %>%
  mutate(canonical_site = to_shorthand(canonical_site))   # raw code -> manuscript label before collapsing to a list

unmatched_common_names <- distinctiveness_full %>%
  filter(!(resolved_name %in% common_names_supp$scientific_name)) %>%
  distinct(resolved_name)
if (nrow(unmatched_common_names) > 0) {
  warning(nrow(unmatched_common_names), " taxa in the distinctiveness table have no entry in ",
          "taxon_common_names_lookup.csv, common name left blank: ",
          paste(unmatched_common_names$resolved_name, collapse = ", "))
}

# Sites in each list follow the region order used in every figure.
site_rank_lookup <- setNames(seq_along(site_order_regional), site_order_regional)

supp_table_taxa_by_site <- distinctiveness_full %>%
  mutate(site_rank = site_rank_lookup[canonical_site]) %>%
  arrange(site_rank) %>%
  group_by(resolved_name, class, n_sites) %>%
  summarise(Sites = paste(canonical_site, collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(common_names_supp, by = c("resolved_name" = "scientific_name")) %>%
  arrange(n_sites, resolved_name) %>%
  transmute(
    Taxon = resolved_name,
    `Common name` = common_name,
    Class = class,
    `Sites detected (of 27)` = n_sites,
    Sites = Sites
  )

add_supp_table("taxa_by_site", supp_table_taxa_by_site,
  paste("One row per non-human taxon (Figure 3a). Taxa are the names each sequence resolved to",
        "(family, genus or species) after the standard filter; human and ambiguous Phasianidae/Bovidae",
        "family calls are excluded. Sites detected = number of the 27 sites where the taxon passed the",
        "filter; Sites lists them in region order. Sorted from taxa found at one site to taxa found at all 27."))

cat("\n", supp_table_ref("taxa_by_site"), "written: taxa by site occurrence,",
    nrow(supp_table_taxa_by_site), "taxa.\n")

# =========================================================================
# Supplementary Table (jaccard_similarity): pairwise site-to-site Jaccard similarity behind
# Figure 3b. Exact similarity values in the text come from this table.
# =========================================================================

supp_table_jaccard_similarity <- site_similarity %>%
  filter(site_a != site_b) %>%
  mutate(
    rank_a = site_rank_lookup[site_a],
    rank_b = site_rank_lookup[site_b]
  ) %>%
  filter(rank_a < rank_b) %>%   # one row per unordered pair, not both A-B and B-A
  arrange(rank_a, rank_b) %>%
  transmute(
    `Site A` = site_a,
    `Site B` = site_b,
    `Jaccard similarity` = round(similarity, 3)
  )

add_supp_table("jaccard_similarity", supp_table_jaccard_similarity,
  paste("One row per pair of sites (Figure 3b). Jaccard similarity = taxa detected at both sites divided",
        "by taxa detected at either, using every non-human taxon detected at each site over the whole",
        "study (presence/absence pooled across samples). 1 = identical taxon lists, 0 = no taxa shared."))

cat("\n", supp_table_ref("jaccard_similarity"), "written: pairwise Jaccard similarity,",
    nrow(supp_table_jaccard_similarity), "site pairs.\n")
```


```{r supp-fig-boston-detections}
# Supplementary Figure (boston_detections): vertebrate detections over time at Boston DITP
# North and Boston DITP South. Also defines the paired-heatmap helpers used
# by Supplementary Figure (hawaii_detections), so this chunk must run first.
#
# Layout. Both sites share one taxon axis: every taxon detected at either
# site, ordered by class and then by total reads across both sites. Each
# site is a panel of one faceted plot, so rows line up across panels and a
# taxon missing from one site shows as an empty row there. Labels and a
# narrow class strip sit left of the first panel. Both legends share one
# box on the right.
#
# Data. All taxa at the rank they resolved to, with no abundance cutoff.
# The standard filter (apply_standard_filter()) is applied per site, as
# everywhere else. Tiles are each taxon's percent of that site's total
# reads that week. Human is included.
#
# A genus or family row is merged into its finer relative only when there
# is exactly one finer relative detected across the two sites (e.g.,
# Hominidae has only resolved to Homo sapiens). The merge is built from
# both sites together, so a taxon is merged the same way in both panels.
# This merge is for display only. The statistics use only the curated
# merges in TAXON_MERGES (post-parse-filters).
#
# PAIRED_BOLD sets which labels are bold: "shared" (detected at both
# sites), "unique" (detected at one site only) or "none".
#
# The class strip is drawn just left of the first panel (outside the
# panel, clip = "off"), in the space the y-axis margin leaves between the
# labels and the panel. PAIRED_STRIP_WEEKS sets its width in week columns
# and PAIRED_STRIP_GAP the gap to the panel. If the strip overlaps the
# labels, raise PAIRED_LABEL_MARGIN_MM.

PAIRED_BOLD            <- "shared"
PAIRED_BASE_SIZE       <- FONT_BASE
PAIRED_AXIS_TEXT       <- FONT_SMALL
PAIRED_STRIP_WEEKS     <- 3
PAIRED_STRIP_GAP       <- 0.6
PAIRED_LABEL_MARGIN_MM <- 3.5
CLASS_STRIP_COLORS     <- CLASS_COLORS  # shared vertebrate class palette (see setup chunk)

common_names <- read_common_names()
build_display_label <- function(taxon_vec) {
  cn <- common_names$common_name[match(taxon_vec, common_names$scientific_name)]
  ifelse(is.na(cn), taxon_vec, cn)
}

# ---- Collapse helper: merge a coarse row into its single finer relative,
# only when unambiguous (see note above) ------------------------------------
build_collapse_map <- function(data) {
  genus_to_species <- data %>%
    filter(resolved_rank == "species", !is.na(genus)) %>%
    distinct(genus, resolved_name) %>%
    add_count(genus, name = "n_species") %>%
    filter(n_species == 1) %>%
    transmute(from = genus, to = resolved_name, to_rank = "species")

  family_to_finer <- data %>%
    filter(resolved_rank %in% c("genus", "species"), !is.na(family)) %>%
    distinct(family, resolved_name, resolved_rank) %>%
    add_count(family, name = "n_finer") %>%
    filter(n_finer == 1) %>%
    transmute(from = family, to = resolved_name, to_rank = resolved_rank)

  bind_rows(genus_to_species, family_to_finer)
}

apply_collapse <- function(data, collapse_map) {
  data %>%
    mutate(collapse_key = case_when(
      resolved_rank == "genus"  ~ genus,
      resolved_rank == "family" ~ family,
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )) %>%
    left_join(collapse_map, by = c("collapse_key" = "from")) %>%
    mutate(
      taxon      = coalesce(to, resolved_name),
      taxon_rank = coalesce(to_rank, resolved_rank)
    ) %>%
    select(-collapse_key, -to, -to_rank)
}

# ---- Paired data: shared taxon axis, weekly percent per site ----------------
build_paired_data <- function(site_codes, site_names) {
  site_lab <- setNames(site_names, site_codes)

  df_pre <- load_detections(drop_human = FALSE) %>%
    filter(canonical_site %in% site_codes) %>%
    mutate(broad_cat = broad_cat(class))

  df <- apply_collapse(df_pre, build_collapse_map(df_pre))

  df <- df %>% mutate(week = study_week(date))

  sampled <- all_parsed %>%
    filter(canonical_site %in% site_codes, as.Date(date) <= STUDY_END_DATE) %>%
    distinct(canonical_site, week = study_week(date))
  week_seq    <- STUDY_WEEKS
  week_levels <- format(week_seq, "%m/%d/%y")

  taxon_order <- df %>%
    group_by(taxon) %>%
    summarise(total_reads = sum(reads), broad_cat = first(broad_cat), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(broad_cat = factor(broad_cat, levels = c("Mammal", "Bird", "Fish", "Other"))) %>%
    arrange(broad_cat, desc(total_reads))
  taxon_levels <- taxon_order$taxon

  n_sites_taxon <- df %>% distinct(taxon, canonical_site) %>% count(taxon, name = "n_sites")
  taxon_order <- taxon_order %>% left_join(n_sites_taxon, by = "taxon")

  cat(paste(site_names, collapse = " + "), ": ", length(taxon_levels), " taxa (",
      sum(taxon_order$n_sites == length(site_codes)), " shared)\n", sep = "")
  unmatched_names <- setdiff(taxon_levels, common_names$scientific_name)
  if (length(unmatched_names) > 0) {
    warning(length(unmatched_names), " taxa have no entry in taxon_common_names_lookup.csv, ",
            "shown as the scientific name instead: ", paste(unmatched_names, collapse = ", "))
  }

  week_totals <- df %>%
    group_by(canonical_site, week) %>%
    summarise(week_total_reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop")

  weekly <- df %>%
    group_by(canonical_site, week, taxon) %>%
    summarise(reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
    left_join(week_totals, by = c("canonical_site", "week")) %>%
    mutate(pct = reads / week_total_reads * 100)

  # Full grid: every site x week x taxon. Sampled weeks get a tile (white when
  # the taxon was not detected); unsampled weeks are gap tiles.
  grid <- expand_grid(canonical_site = site_codes, week = week_seq, taxon = taxon_levels) %>%
    left_join(sampled %>% mutate(sampled = TRUE), by = c("canonical_site", "week")) %>%
    mutate(sampled = replace_na(sampled, FALSE)) %>%
    left_join(weekly %>% select(canonical_site, week, taxon, pct),
              by = c("canonical_site", "week", "taxon")) %>%
    mutate(site       = factor(site_lab[canonical_site], levels = site_names),
           week_label = factor(format(week, "%m/%d/%y"), levels = week_levels),
           taxon      = factor(taxon, levels = rev(taxon_levels)))

  # Labels, bolded by PAIRED_BOLD
  labels <- build_display_label(taxon_order$taxon)
  bold <- switch(PAIRED_BOLD,
                 shared = taxon_order$n_sites == length(site_codes),
                 unique = taxon_order$n_sites == 1,
                 none   = rep(FALSE, nrow(taxon_order)))
  label_map <- setNames(labels, taxon_levels)
  bold_map  <- setNames(bold, taxon_levels)

  # Horizontal lines between classes (y positions on the reversed taxon axis)
  class_counts <- as.vector(table(taxon_order$broad_cat)[levels(taxon_order$broad_cat)])
  class_counts <- class_counts[class_counts > 0]
  class_breaks <- length(taxon_levels) - head(cumsum(class_counts), -1) + 0.5

  # Week tick labels: the first week starting in January, April, July and
  # October, as "%m-%Y", matching the Figure 9 heatmap
  first_month   <- floor_date(week_seq, "month")
  quarter_start <- !duplicated(first_month) & as.integer(format(first_month, "%m")) %in% c(1, 4, 7, 10)
  week_tick_labels <- setNames(ifelse(quarter_start, format(first_month, "%m-%Y"), ""), week_levels)

  list(grid = grid, taxon_order = taxon_order, taxon_levels = taxon_levels,
       week_levels = week_levels, week_tick_labels = week_tick_labels,
       label_map = label_map, bold_map = bold_map, class_breaks = class_breaks)
}

# ---- Paired plot: one faceted heatmap with the class strip and labels -------
build_paired_plot <- function(pd) {
  y_limits    <- rev(pd$taxon_levels)
  n_weeks     <- length(pd$week_levels)
  first_site  <- levels(pd$grid$site)[1]

  # One rectangle per taxon, in the first panel only, left of week 1
  strip_data <- pd$taxon_order %>%
    mutate(y    = match(taxon, y_limits),
           site = factor(first_site, levels = levels(pd$grid$site)),
           xmax = 0.5 - PAIRED_STRIP_GAP,
           xmin = 0.5 - PAIRED_STRIP_GAP - PAIRED_STRIP_WEEKS)

  ggplot() +
    geom_tile(data = pd$grid %>% filter(!sampled),
              aes(x = week_label, y = taxon), fill = GAP_FILL,
              color = HEAT_GRID_COLOR, linewidth = HEAT_GRID_WIDTH) +
    geom_tile(data = pd$grid %>% filter(sampled),
              aes(x = week_label, y = taxon, fill = pct), color = HEAT_GRID_COLOR, linewidth = HEAT_GRID_WIDTH) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(colors = HEAT_12S_COLORS, transform = "log10", na.value = "white",
                         breaks = c(0.01, 0.1, 1, 10), labels = c("0.01", "0.1", "1", "10"),
                         name = "% of week's\ntotal reads (log)",
                         guide = guide_colorbar(order = 1)) +
    new_scale_fill() +
    geom_rect(data = strip_data,
              aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = y - 0.5, ymax = y + 0.5, fill = broad_cat),
              color = NA) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = CLASS_STRIP_COLORS, name = "Class", drop = FALSE,
                      guide = guide_legend(order = 2)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = pd$class_breaks, linewidth = 0.3, color = "black") +
    facet_wrap(~ site, nrow = 1) +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = pd$week_levels, labels = pd$week_tick_labels) +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = y_limits, labels = pd$label_map) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.5, n_weeks + 0.5), ylim = c(0.5, length(y_limits) + 0.5),
                    expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
    labs(x = "Week", y = "Taxon") +
    theme_bw(base_size = PAIRED_BASE_SIZE) +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
      panel.spacing.x = unit(3, "mm"),
      strip.background = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(size = PAIRED_BASE_SIZE, face = "bold", hjust = 0,
                                margin = margin(b = 2)),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1,
                                 size = PAIRED_AXIS_TEXT, color = "black"),
      # Bold set per label with plain text: ggtext adds extra space after hyphens
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = PAIRED_AXIS_TEXT, color = "black",
                                 face = ifelse(pd$bold_map[y_limits], "bold", "plain"),
                                 margin = margin(r = PAIRED_LABEL_MARGIN_MM, unit = "mm")),
      axis.ticks.x = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, color = "grey40"),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.length.x = unit(0.6, "mm"),
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.box = "vertical",
      legend.box.just = "left",
      legend.spacing.y = unit(3, "mm"),
      legend.key.size = unit(3, "mm"),
      legend.title = element_text(size = PAIRED_BASE_SIZE),
      legend.text = element_text(size = PAIRED_AXIS_TEXT + 1),
      legend.background = element_blank(),
      legend.box.background = element_rect(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3, fill = "white"),
      legend.box.margin = margin(1, 1, 1, 1),
      legend.margin = LEGEND_BOX_MARGIN,
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2)
    )
}
```
