```{r supp-fig-fish-dominated-samples}
# =========================================================================
# Supplementary Figure (fish_dominated_samples): fish-dominated samples on the Jaccard PCoA
# =========================================================================
# Sample-level Jaccard PCoA (same as Figure 4a) colored by whether fish made
# up at least 20% of the taxa in the sample. The 20% cutoff was chosen by
# eye, as stated in the manuscript.
#
# PERMANOVA. Fish-dominated samples are concentrated at a few sites (Boston,
# Hawaii, coastal California), so comparing them with all other samples
# would mostly repeat the site difference. The model therefore includes
# site, tests the fish-dominated term after site (by = "margin"), and
# permutes samples only within their own site (blocks = site). The result
# asks whether fish-dominated samples differ from other samples at the
# same site. Note that the grouping is defined from the same taxon lists
# the Jaccard distances use, so the test describes how strongly fish taxa
# shape composition rather than an independent cause.
#
# Uses combined_scores from the Figure 3/4 chunk.
# Single column, legend below the square ordination. Fishy uses the fish
# class color; not fishy is neutral grey.
SUPPFIG5_WIDTH_MM  <- 88
SUPPFIG5_HEIGHT_MM <- 100

FISHY_COLORS <- c("Fishy (>=20% of taxa)" = unname(CLASS_COLORS["Fish"]), "Not fishy (<20%)" = "grey65")
fishy_scores <- combined_scores %>%
  mutate(fishy_group = if_else(fish_fraction >= 0.20, "Fishy (>=20% of taxa)", "Not fishy (<20%)"))

# ---- PERMANOVA: does fishy vs. not-fishy explain sample-level community
# structure, on the same Jaccard matrix and framework as Figure 4a -------
sample_jaccard <- read_stat("sample_jaccard")
jaccard_order <- attr(sample_jaccard, "Labels")
fishy_lookup  <- setNames(fishy_scores$fishy_group, fishy_scores$sample_id)
fishy_group_ordered <- unname(fishy_lookup[jaccard_order])
stopifnot(!any(is.na(fishy_group_ordered)))
fishy_meta <- tibble(canonical_site = str_sub(jaccard_order, 1, -12),   # sample_id = <site>_<YYYY-MM-DD>
                     fishy_group    = fishy_group_ordered)
set.seed(42)
permanova_fishy <- adonis2(
  sample_jaccard ~ canonical_site + fishy_group,
  data = fishy_meta,
  permutations = how(nperm = 999, blocks = factor(fishy_meta$canonical_site)),
  by = "margin"
)
fishy_row <- which(rownames(permanova_fishy) == "fishy_group")
fishy_permanova_label <- sprintf(
  "PERMANOVA: R\u00b2 = %.3f, p = %.3f",
  permanova_fishy$R2[fishy_row], permanova_fishy$`Pr(>F)`[fishy_row]
)
cat("\n", supp_fig_ref("fish_dominated_samples"), "PERMANOVA (fish-dominated, after site, permuted within site):\n")
print(permanova_fishy)
saveRDS(permanova_fishy, file.path(stats_dir, "permanova_fish_dominated.rds"))

# ---- Plot -------------------------------------------------------------
p_pcoa_fishy <- ggplot(fishy_scores, aes(PCoA1, PCoA2, color = fishy_group)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(size = 1.3, alpha = 0.4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = FISHY_COLORS, name = NULL) +
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1) +
  labs(x = paste0("PCoA1 (", sample_scores$pct_var1[1], "%)"),
       y = paste0("PCoA2 (", sample_scores$pct_var2[1], "%)")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = SITE_FP_BASE_SIZE) +
  theme(axis.text  = element_text(color = "black", size = SITE_FP_AXIS_TEXT),
        axis.title = element_text(color = "black", size = SITE_FP_BASE_SIZE),
        panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)) +
  site_fp_compact_legend +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2.5, alpha = 1))) +
  annotate("label", x = -Inf, y = -Inf, label = fishy_permanova_label, hjust = 0, vjust = -0.3,
           size = 6.5 / .pt, linewidth = 0, fill = "white", alpha = 0.85)

save_figure(p_pcoa_fishy, supp_fig_file("fish_dominated_samples"), dir = supp_dir,
            width = SUPPFIG5_WIDTH_MM, height = SUPPFIG5_HEIGHT_MM)
p_pcoa_fishy
```


```{r supp-fig-pcoa-site-metadata}
# =========================================================================
# Supplementary Figure (pcoa_site_metadata): site metadata fitted onto the Jaccard PCoA
# =========================================================================
# Do differences in composition between sites line up with where a site is
# (region, latitude, longitude), how many people it serves, or its sewer
# system type? Each variable is fitted onto the existing sample-level
# Jaccard PCoA (Figure 4a) with vegan::envfit(). The ordination itself does
# not change.
#
# Unit of analysis. These variables describe a site, not a sample, so the
# fit uses one point per site: the mean PCoA1 and PCoA2 of that site's
# samples (n = 27). Fitting on ~1,800 samples would treat repeated samples
# from one site as independent evidence about that site.
#
# Each variable is fitted on its own, so the two sites without a reported
# population drop out of the population fit only.
#   Continuous (arrows): latitude, longitude, log10 population served.
#     Arrow direction = direction in which the variable increases. Arrow
#     length is proportional to sqrt(R2); the longest arrow is scaled to 80%
#     of the site range so arrows are readable. Solid black = p < 0.05.
#   Categorical: region and sewer system type. R2 = share of variation in
#     site positions explained by the grouping.
#   999 permutations of sites, so the smallest possible p is 0.001.
#
# Figure: samples (faded) and site means colored by region, ellipses
# covering the middle ELLIPSE_LEVEL of each region's samples, site means
# shaped by sewer system type, arrows for the continuous variables, and the
# fit statistics in a box.
# Output: Supplementary Figure (pcoa_site_metadata), stats_dir/pcoa_envfit.csv

# Region colors. Dark, muted tones so regions are not read as states.
# Region colors: Paul Tol's "vibrant" scheme, distinct under the common
# forms of color blindness.
REGION_COLORS <- c(Northeast = "#0077BB", Midwest = "#EE7733", South = "#009988", West = "#EE3377")

ENVFIT_PERM   <- 999
ENVFIT_ALPHA  <- 0.05
ELLIPSE_LEVEL <- 0.68

envfit_scores <- readRDS(file.path(stats_dir, "sample_pcoa_scores.rds"))

# ---- Site metadata -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Plant coordinates are held back, so the public copy fits region, sewer
# type and population only. The private copy also fits latitude and longitude.
HAS_SITE_COORDS <- "lat_lon" %in% names(read_site_labels())
envfit_sites <- site_table %>%
  transmute(canonical_site,
            region    = factor(as.character(region), levels = REGION_ORDER),
            sewer     = factor(system, levels = c("Sanitary", "Combined")),
            log10_pop = log10(population))
if (HAS_SITE_COORDS) {
  envfit_sites <- envfit_sites %>%
    left_join(read_site_labels() %>%
                select(canonical_site = current_site_label, lat_lon) %>%
                bind_cols(parse_lat_lon(.$lat_lon)) %>%
                select(-lat_lon) %>%
                rows_update(MANUAL_COORDS %>% rename(canonical_site = current_site_label),
                            by = "canonical_site", unmatched = "ignore"),
              by = "canonical_site")
  stopifnot(!any(is.na(envfit_sites$lat)), !any(is.na(envfit_sites$lon)))
} else {
  message("No site coordinates available; latitude and longitude are not fitted. ",
          "They would show where the treatment plants are.")
}
stopifnot(!any(is.na(envfit_sites$region)), !any(is.na(envfit_sites$sewer)))

# ---- Site means of the sample PCoA scores -------------------------------------------
envfit_samples <- envfit_scores %>%
  select(sample_id, canonical_site, PCoA1, PCoA2) %>%
  left_join(envfit_sites %>% select(canonical_site, region), by = "canonical_site")

envfit_cent <- envfit_scores %>%
  dplyr::group_by(canonical_site) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(PCoA1 = mean(PCoA1), PCoA2 = mean(PCoA2), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(envfit_sites, by = "canonical_site")
stopifnot(nrow(envfit_cent) == N_SITES_TOTAL)

# ---- envfit, one variable at a time --------------------------------------------------
ENVFIT_VARS <- c(region = "Region", lat = "Latitude", lon = "Longitude",
                 log10_pop = "Population (log10)", sewer = "Sewer type")
if (!HAS_SITE_COORDS) ENVFIT_VARS <- ENVFIT_VARS[!names(ENVFIT_VARS) %in% c("lat", "lon")]

envfit_stats <- purrr::map_dfr(names(ENVFIT_VARS), function(v) {
  d <- envfit_cent %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[v]]))
  set.seed(42)
  # envfit expects plain data frames; a tibble triggers "Unknown column: weights" warnings
  ef <- vegan::envfit(as.data.frame(d[, c("PCoA1", "PCoA2")]), as.data.frame(d[, v, drop = FALSE]),
                      permutations = ENVFIT_PERM)
  if (is.numeric(d[[v]])) {
    tibble(variable = v, label = ENVFIT_VARS[[v]], type = "continuous", n_sites = nrow(d),
           r2 = unname(ef$vectors$r), p = unname(ef$vectors$pvals),
           dir1 = ef$vectors$arrows[1, 1], dir2 = ef$vectors$arrows[1, 2])
  } else {
    tibble(variable = v, label = ENVFIT_VARS[[v]], type = "categorical", n_sites = nrow(d),
           r2 = unname(ef$factors$r), p = unname(ef$factors$pvals),
           dir1 = NA_real_, dir2 = NA_real_)
  }
})
write_csv(envfit_stats %>% select(variable = label, type, n_sites, r2, p),
          file.path(stats_dir, "pcoa_envfit.csv"))

# ---- Arrows -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
envfit_rng <- max(abs(c(envfit_cent$PCoA1, envfit_cent$PCoA2)))
envfit_arrows <- envfit_stats %>%
  filter(type == "continuous") %>%
  mutate(len = sqrt(r2),
         x = dir1 * len * 0.8 * envfit_rng / max(len),
         y = dir2 * len * 0.8 * envfit_rng / max(len),
         sig = p < ENVFIT_ALPHA)

envfit_label <- envfit_stats %>%
  mutate(line = sprintf("%s: R\u00b2 = %.2f, p = %.3f", label, r2, p)) %>%
  pull(line) %>%
  paste(collapse = "\n")

# ---- Plot ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
p_envfit <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = envfit_samples, aes(PCoA1, PCoA2, color = region), size = 1.2, alpha = 0.22) +
  stat_ellipse(data = envfit_samples, aes(PCoA1, PCoA2, color = region),
               level = ELLIPSE_LEVEL, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_segment(data = envfit_arrows %>% filter(!sig), aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = x, yend = y),
               color = "grey35", linetype = "22", linewidth = 0.7,
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(1.8, "mm"))) +
  geom_segment(data = envfit_arrows %>% filter(sig), aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = x, yend = y),
               color = "black", linewidth = 1,
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(2.2, "mm"))) +
  geom_text(data = envfit_arrows, aes(x * 1.15, y * 1.15, label = label,
                                      fontface = ifelse(sig, "bold", "plain")),
            size = SITE_FP_AXIS_TEXT / .pt, color = "black") +
  geom_point(data = envfit_cent, aes(PCoA1, PCoA2, fill = region, shape = sewer),
             color = "black", size = 2.6, stroke = 0.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = REGION_COLORS, limits = REGION_ORDER, name = "Region") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = REGION_COLORS, limits = REGION_ORDER, name = "Region") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(Sanitary = 21, Combined = 24), name = "Sewer type") +
  labs(x = paste0("PCoA1 (", envfit_scores$pct_var1[1], "%)"),
       y = paste0("PCoA2 (", envfit_scores$pct_var2[1], "%)")) +
  guides(color = "none",
         fill  = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21, size = 2.6)),
         shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(fill = "grey70", size = 2.6))) +
  theme_bw(base_size = SITE_FP_BASE_SIZE) +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1,
        axis.text  = element_text(color = "black", size = SITE_FP_AXIS_TEXT),
        axis.title = element_text(color = "black", size = SITE_FP_AXIS_TITLE),
        panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
        legend.position = "right") +
  site_fp_compact_legend +
  annotate("label", x = -Inf, y = -Inf, label = envfit_label, hjust = 0, vjust = -0.1,
           size = 6 / .pt, linewidth = 0, fill = "white", alpha = 0.85, lineheight = 0.95)

save_figure(p_envfit, supp_fig_file("pcoa_site_metadata"), dir = supp_dir, width = 136, height = 110)
p_envfit

cat("\nenvfit on site means of the Jaccard PCoA (", ENVFIT_PERM, "permutations):\n")
print(as.data.frame(envfit_stats %>% transmute(variable = label, n_sites, r2 = round(r2, 3), p)),
      row.names = FALSE)
```


```{r supp-fig-alpha-diversity}
# =========================================================================
# Supplementary Figure (alpha_diversity) and Supplementary Table (alpha_diversity): alpha diversity by
# site. Shannon and Pielou's evenness, with Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn's post
# hoc tests. Simpson (1 - D) is still
# computed and saved per sample but not tested or plotted; it ranks sites
# the same way Shannon does.
# =========================================================================
# Same filtered dataset as fingerprint-stats (chordate_perfect_match.csv ->
# drop human reads and ambiguous families -> apply_standard_filter ->
# per-sample relative abundance). Each box is one site, colored by state.
#
# Run AFTER figure3-figure4-pcoa: uses site_fp_compact_legend
# from that chunk for the legend styling.
#
# Tests:
# - Kruskal-Wallis per metric: do sites differ overall? Rank-based, since
#   these metrics are not normally distributed. Epsilon-squared
#   (H / (n - 1)) is reported as an effect size, because with ~1,800
#   samples even small differences give very small p-values.
# - Dunn's test per metric: which pairs of sites differ (27 sites = 351
#   pairs). Uses the same ranks as Kruskal-Wallis, with the standard tie
#   correction. p-values adjusted for multiple comparisons within each
#   metric using ALPHA_P_ADJUST.
# - Samples from the same site are repeated over time, so they are not
#   fully independent. Same caveat as the PERMANOVA.

ALPHA_P_ADJUST <- "BH"   # "BH" (false discovery rate) or "holm" (stricter)

if (!exists("site_fp_compact_legend")) {
  stop("Run figure3-figure4-pcoa first (defines site_fp_compact_legend).")
}

df <- load_detections()

df <- df %>% mutate(sample_id = paste(canonical_site, date, sep = "_"))

site_state_lookup <- df %>% distinct(canonical_site, state)

shorthand_lookup <- read_site_labels() %>%
  select(current_site_label, shorthand_for_figures) %>%
  deframe()
to_shorthand <- function(x) unname(shorthand_lookup[x])

site_order_regional <- site_state_lookup %>%
  mutate(region = factor(REGION_MAP[state], levels = REGION_ORDER),
         shorthand = unname(shorthand_lookup[canonical_site])) %>%
  arrange(region, state, shorthand) %>%
  pull(canonical_site)

# ---- Sample x taxon relative abundance matrix ------------------------------
# Multiple sequences resolving to the same name are summed to one abundance
# value per sample first, matching how detection is collapsed to the taxon
# level everywhere else in this script.

sample_abund_long <- df %>%
  group_by(sample_id, canonical_site, resolved_name) %>%
  summarise(reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop")

sample_meta <- sample_abund_long %>% distinct(sample_id, canonical_site)

sample_abund_mat <- sample_abund_long %>%
  select(-canonical_site) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = resolved_name, values_from = reads, values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample_id") %>%
  as.matrix()

sample_meta <- sample_meta[match(rownames(sample_abund_mat), sample_meta$sample_id), ]
stopifnot(all(sample_meta$sample_id == rownames(sample_abund_mat)))

sample_relabund_mat <- sample_abund_mat / rowSums(sample_abund_mat)

# ---- Per-sample diversity ---------------------------------------------------
# Shannon H' = -sum(p * log(p)); Simpson dominance D = sum(p^2), plotted as
# Simpson's diversity 1 - D so higher = more diverse, consistent with H' and
# evenness; Pielou's evenness J = H' / log(richness). Richness-1 samples
# have H' = 0 and 1 - D = 0, and undefined evenness (log(1) = 0), so they
# are dropped from the evenness panel and test only.

richness <- rowSums(sample_relabund_mat > 0)

shannon_h <- apply(sample_relabund_mat, 1, function(p) {
  p <- p[p > 0]
  -sum(p * log(p))
})

simpson_dominance <- apply(sample_relabund_mat, 1, function(p) sum(p^2))
simpson_diversity <- 1 - simpson_dominance

evenness <- ifelse(richness > 1, shannon_h / log(richness), NA_real_)

alpha_div <- tibble(
  sample_id      = rownames(sample_relabund_mat),
  canonical_site = sample_meta$canonical_site,
  richness       = richness,
  shannon        = shannon_h,
  simpson        = simpson_diversity,
  evenness       = evenness
) %>%
  left_join(site_state_lookup, by = "canonical_site") %>%
  mutate(
    site_label = factor(to_shorthand(canonical_site),
                         levels = to_shorthand(site_order_regional))
  )

write_csv(alpha_div, file.path(stats_dir, "alpha_diversity_by_sample.csv"))

cat("Richness-1 samples (evenness undefined):", sum(richness == 1), "\n")

# ---- Kruskal-Wallis + Dunn's test ---------------------------------------------

alpha_metrics <- c(shannon  = "Shannon diversity (H')",
                   evenness = "Pielou's evenness (J)")

# Dunn's test (Dunn 1964) with tie correction, same as FSA::dunnTest
dunn_test <- function(values, groups, p_adjust) {
  groups <- droplevels(factor(groups))
  N  <- length(values)
  r  <- rank(values)
  ni <- vapply(split(r, groups), length, numeric(1))
  Ri <- vapply(split(r, groups), mean, numeric(1))
  ties <- as.vector(table(values))
  tie_term <- sum(ties^3 - ties) / (12 * (N - 1))
  s2 <- N * (N + 1) / 12 - tie_term
  pairs <- combn(levels(groups), 2)
  a <- pairs[1, ]
  b <- pairs[2, ]
  z <- (Ri[a] - Ri[b]) / sqrt(s2 * (1 / ni[a] + 1 / ni[b]))
  p <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(z))
  tibble(site_a = a, site_b = b, n_a = unname(ni[a]), n_b = unname(ni[b]),
         z = unname(z), p = unname(p), p_adj = p.adjust(unname(p), method = p_adjust))
}

kw_results <- list()
dunn_results <- list()

for (m in names(alpha_metrics)) {
  d <- alpha_div %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[m]]))
  # site_label levels are already in regional order, so pairs come out that way
  kw <- kruskal.test(d[[m]] ~ d$site_label)
  n_samples <- nrow(d)

  kw_results[[m]] <- tibble(
    Metric = alpha_metrics[[m]],
    `n samples` = n_samples,
    `n sites` = n_distinct(d$site_label),
    H = unname(kw$statistic),
    df = unname(kw$parameter),
    p = kw$p.value,
    `Epsilon squared` = unname(kw$statistic) / (n_samples - 1)
  )

  site_medians <- d %>% group_by(site_label) %>% summarise(med = median(.data[[m]]), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(site_label = as.character(site_label)) %>% deframe()

  dunn_results[[m]] <- dunn_test(d[[m]], d$site_label, ALPHA_P_ADJUST) %>%
    mutate(Metric = alpha_metrics[[m]],
           median_a = unname(site_medians[site_a]),
           median_b = unname(site_medians[site_b]))
}

kw_table <- bind_rows(kw_results)
dunn_table <- bind_rows(dunn_results)

# ---- Supplementary tables ---------------------------------------------------
fmt_p_tab <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, "< 0.001", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3))

supp_table_alpha_kw <- kw_table %>%
  mutate(H = round(H, 1), `Epsilon squared` = round(`Epsilon squared`, 3), p = fmt_p_tab(p))

supp_table_alpha_dunn <- dunn_table %>%
  transmute(
    Metric,
    `Site A` = site_a, `Site B` = site_b,
    `n A` = n_a, `n B` = n_b,
    `Median A` = round(median_a, 3), `Median B` = round(median_b, 3),
    z = round(z, 2),
    p = fmt_p_tab(p),
    `Adjusted p` = fmt_p_tab(p_adj)
  )

# One table: the Kruskal-Wallis test for each metric first, then every
# Dunn's pairwise comparison for that metric.
supp_table_alpha <- bind_rows(
  kw_table %>%
    transmute(Metric, Test = "Kruskal-Wallis (all sites)",
              `Site A` = NA_character_, `Site B` = NA_character_,
              `n samples` = `n samples`, `Median A` = NA_real_, `Median B` = NA_real_,
              Statistic = round(H, 1), df = df, `Epsilon squared` = round(`Epsilon squared`, 3),
              p = fmt_p_tab(p), `Adjusted p` = NA_character_),
  dunn_table %>%
    transmute(Metric, Test = "Dunn's test (site pair)",
              `Site A` = site_a, `Site B` = site_b,
              `n samples` = n_a + n_b, `Median A` = round(median_a, 3), `Median B` = round(median_b, 3),
              Statistic = round(z, 2), df = NA_real_, `Epsilon squared` = NA_real_,
              p = fmt_p_tab(p), `Adjusted p` = fmt_p_tab(p_adj))
)
add_supp_table("alpha_diversity", supp_table_alpha,
  paste(paste0(supp_fig_ref("alpha_diversity"), "."), "Shannon diversity (H') and Pielou's evenness (J) were calculated per",
        "sample from relative read abundance of non-human taxa. Kruskal-Wallis rows test whether sites differ",
        "overall (Statistic = H; epsilon squared = H / (n - 1), an effect size). Dunn's rows compare one pair",
        "of sites (Statistic = z, positive when Site A ranks higher; medians are per-sample values;",
        "n samples = both sites combined). Adjusted p uses Benjamini-Hochberg across the 351 site pairs",
        "within each metric. Samples from one site are repeated over time and not fully independent,",
        "so p-values describe the size of differences rather than strict inference."))

cat("\nKruskal-Wallis by metric:\n")
print(as.data.frame(supp_table_alpha_kw))

cat(sprintf("\nDunn's test, %s-adjusted p < 0.05 (of %d site pairs per metric):\n",
            ALPHA_P_ADJUST, choose(n_distinct(alpha_div$site_label), 2)))
print(as.data.frame(dunn_table %>% group_by(Metric) %>%
  summarise(significant_pairs = sum(p_adj < 0.05), total_pairs = n(), .groups = "drop")))

# ---- Figure size and text ------------------------------------------------
ALPHADIV_WIDTH_MM  <- 180
ALPHADIV_HEIGHT_MM <- 115
ALPHADIV_BASE_SIZE  <- 6.5
ALPHADIV_AXIS_TEXT  <- 6
ALPHADIV_AXIS_TITLE <- 6.5

kw_label <- function(m) {
  k <- kw_table %>% filter(Metric == alpha_metrics[[m]])
  p_str <- if (k$p < 0.001) "p < 0.001" else sprintf("p = %.3f", k$p)
  sprintf("Kruskal-Wallis: %s", p_str)
}

# ---- Panel builder -----------------------------------------------------
# Every sample as a jittered, semi-transparent point colored by state, with
# a black box-and-whisker plot on top (median, quartiles, whiskers to 1.5 x
# IQR). Outliers are not drawn separately because every sample is already
# shown. show_x: only the bottom panel gets site labels, so the panels stack
# without repeating the same 27 angled labels.
ALPHA_POINT_SIZE  <- 0.8
ALPHA_POINT_ALPHA <- 0.5
ALPHA_JITTER      <- 0.25

build_alpha_panel <- function(data, y_var, y_lab, show_x = FALSE) {
  set.seed(42)   # same jitter on every knit
  p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = site_label, y = .data[[y_var]])) +
    geom_jitter(aes(color = state), width = ALPHA_JITTER, height = 0,
                size = ALPHA_POINT_SIZE, alpha = ALPHA_POINT_ALPHA, stroke = 0, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = 0.3, color = "black", fill = NA, na.rm = TRUE) +
    scale_color_manual(values = STATE_COLORS, limits = names(STATE_COLORS), name = "State") +
    guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha = 1))) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))) +  # headroom for the test label
    labs(x = if (show_x) "Site" else NULL, y = y_lab) +
    theme_bw(base_size = ALPHADIV_BASE_SIZE) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y  = element_text(color = "black", size = ALPHADIV_AXIS_TEXT),
      axis.title.y = element_text(color = "black", size = ALPHADIV_AXIS_TITLE),
      panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
    ) +
    annotate("label", x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = kw_label(y_var),
             hjust = -0.02, vjust = 1.2, size = 6.5 / .pt, linewidth = 0, fill = "white", alpha = 0.85)
  if (show_x) {
   p <- p + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 55, hjust = 1, color = "black",
                                              size = ALPHADIV_AXIS_TEXT),
                  axis.title.x = element_text(color = "black", size = ALPHADIV_AXIS_TITLE),
                  plot.margin = margin(t = 5, r = 5, b = 5, l = 20))
  } else {
    p <- p + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
  }
  p
}

p_shannon  <- build_alpha_panel(alpha_div, "shannon",  alpha_metrics[["shannon"]])
p_evenness <- build_alpha_panel(alpha_div, "evenness", alpha_metrics[["evenness"]], show_x = TRUE)

alpha_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(
  p_shannon + site_fp_compact_legend + theme(legend.position = "right")
)

# The bottom panel also holds the angled site labels, so it gets more
# height; otherwise its plotting area is squeezed.
panel_stack <- cowplot::plot_grid(
  p_shannon  + theme(legend.position = "none"),
  p_evenness + theme(legend.position = "none"),
  ncol = 1, align = "v", axis = "lr", rel_heights = c(1, 1.7),
  labels = c("a", "b"), label_size = FIG_PANEL_LABEL_PT
)

p_alpha_diversity <- cowplot::plot_grid(panel_stack, alpha_legend, nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(1, 0.14))

save_figure(p_alpha_diversity, supp_fig_file("alpha_diversity"), dir = supp_dir,
            width = ALPHADIV_WIDTH_MM, height = ALPHADIV_HEIGHT_MM)
p_alpha_diversity
```


```{r figure5-fish}
# Figure 5: fish diversity by site.
#   a) Composition (% of each site's fish reads) and magnitude (% of each
#      site's non-human reads), colored by category: Aquaculture,
#      Freshwater, Marine, Ambiguous. Every category is drawn at its true
#      width, so segments under ~1% are present but too thin to see.
#   b) Heatmap of the top 40 fish taxa by total reads, one block per
#      category, ordered by abundance within each block, log color scale.
#      Taxa are shown at the rank they resolved to (species, genus, or
#      family). Labels are common names from taxon_common_names_lookup.csv.
#
# Classification uses fish_taxa_classification_by_resolved_name.tsv, one row
# per resolved_name in this dataset (taxon, category, notes, source). It also
# holds genus- and family-level rows (Carangidae, Lutjanus and so on), which
# catch taxa that resolved no further. "Ambiguous" means the taxon spans two
# categories biologically. A taxon that matches nothing stops the knit. The first file is also written out as
# Supplementary Table (fish_classification), and every fish percentage in the figure and text
# is in Supplementary Table (fish_by_site).
#
# Colors: the fish class shades (CLASS_STEPS$Fish) so every category reads
# as fish, as in Figure 2; Ambiguous uses the shared "Other" gray.

FIG5_WIDTH_MM     <- 136   # 1.5 column
FIG5_HEIGHT_MM    <- 170
FIG5_BASE_SIZE    <- 6.5
FIG5_AXIS_TEXT    <- 6
FIG5_AXIS_TITLE   <- 6.5
FIG5_LEGEND_TITLE <- 6.5
FIG5_LEGEND_TEXT  <- 6
TOP_N_TAXA        <- 40

# Site order for panel a:
#   "regional"  = region and state order used in Figures 1-3
#   "magnitude" = sorted by % of non-human reads that are fish, highest first
# Panel b's site columns stay in regional order either way.
FIG5A_SORT <- "magnitude"

FISH_CLASSES <- c("Actinopteri", "Actinopterygii", "Chondrichthyes", "Cephalaspidomorphi")

# ---- Load taxon classification: resolved-name primary, genus/family
# fallback -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Categories are matched to SIMPLE_LEVELS (below) after trimming spaces and
# fixing capitalization, so "aquaculture " and "Aquaculture" are the same.
# A taxon listed twice in one file would duplicate its reads in the join,
# so that stops the knit.
SIMPLE_LEVELS <- c("Aquaculture", "Freshwater", "Marine", "Ambiguous")

read_fish_lookup <- function(path) {
  lookup <- read_tsv(path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    select(taxon, category, notes, source) %>%
    mutate(taxon = str_trim(taxon), category = str_to_title(str_trim(category)))
  dup <- lookup$taxon[duplicated(lookup$taxon)]
  if (length(dup) > 0) {
    stop(basename(path), " lists these taxa more than once: ", paste(unique(dup), collapse = ", "))
  }
  bad <- lookup %>% filter(!is.na(category), !category %in% SIMPLE_LEVELS)
  if (nrow(bad) > 0) {
    stop(basename(path), " has categories other than ", paste(SIMPLE_LEVELS, collapse = "/"), ": ",
         paste0(bad$taxon, " (", bad$category, ")", collapse = ", "))
  }
  lookup
}

fish_lookup_resolved <- read_fish_lookup(fish_taxon_resolved_path)

# ---- Detection data: standard filter, ambiguous families and human
# removed, so the magnitude denominator is "% of non-human reads" as in the
# Results. ------------------------------------------------------------------
df_all <- load_detections() %>%
  mutate(broad_cat = broad_cat(class))

site_totals <- df_all %>%
  group_by(canonical_site) %>%
  summarise(site_total_reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop")

df_fish <- df_all %>%
  filter(broad_cat == "Fish") %>%
  mutate(taxon = resolved_name)  # finest rank the sequence resolved to

# ---- Join to classification: exact resolved_name first, then genus, then
# family ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Every fish taxon must end up in one of SIMPLE_LEVELS. A taxon that matches
# nothing stops the knit with a list of what to add, instead of showing up
# as an "NA" category in the figure and tables.
# Genus and family fallback uses the same file, which carries genus- and
# family-level rows (Carangidae, Lutjanus and so on) alongside the species.
fallback_lookup <- fish_lookup_resolved
fallback_category <- function(key) {
  fallback_lookup$category[match(key, fallback_lookup$taxon)]
}

df_fish <- df_fish %>%
  mutate(
    category = fish_lookup_resolved$category[match(taxon, fish_lookup_resolved$taxon)],
    classification_key = if_else(!is.na(category), taxon, NA_character_),
    genus_category  = fallback_category(genus),
    family_category = fallback_category(family),
    classification_key = case_when(
      !is.na(classification_key) ~ classification_key,
      !is.na(genus_category)     ~ genus,
      !is.na(family_category)    ~ family,
      TRUE                       ~ NA_character_
    ),
    category = coalesce(category, genus_category, family_category)
  ) %>%
  select(-genus_category, -family_category)

lookup_notes <- fallback_lookup %>% select(taxon, notes, source)
df_fish <- df_fish %>% left_join(lookup_notes, by = c("classification_key" = "taxon"))

unmatched <- df_fish %>%
  filter(is.na(category)) %>%
  group_by(taxon, resolved_rank, genus, family) %>%
  summarise(reads = sum(reads), n_sites = n_distinct(canonical_site), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(reads))
if (nrow(unmatched) > 0) {
  print(as.data.frame(unmatched), row.names = FALSE)
  stop(
    nrow(unmatched), " fish taxa have no category (listed above). Add each to ",
    basename(fish_taxon_resolved_path), " by resolved name, genus or family, then re-knit: ",
    paste(unmatched$taxon, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# Prints how each fish taxon was classified: by_resolved_name = the taxon
# itself was listed; by_genus_or_family = it took the category of its genus
# or family row.
fish_coverage <- df_fish %>%
  distinct(taxon, classification_key) %>%
  summarise(
    taxa               = n(),
    by_resolved_name   = sum(classification_key == taxon),
    by_genus_or_family = sum(classification_key != taxon)
  )
cat(sprintf(
  "Fish classification: %d taxa, all categorized (%d by resolved name, %d by genus or family)\n",
  fish_coverage$taxa, fish_coverage$by_resolved_name, fish_coverage$by_genus_or_family))

# ---- Site labels + shared row order (top to bottom = region order) --------
site_labels_df <- read_site_labels()

sort_tbl <- site_labels_df %>%
  mutate(region = factor(region, levels = REGION_ORDER)) %>%
  arrange(region, state, shorthand_for_figures)
site_order_regional <- sort_tbl$current_site_label
LABEL_LOOKUP <- setNames(sort_tbl$shorthand_for_figures, sort_tbl$current_site_label)

SIMPLE_COLORS <- c(
  "Aquaculture"  = CLASS_STEPS$Fish[2],
  "Freshwater"   = CLASS_STEPS$Fish[3],
  "Marine"       = CLASS_STEPS$Fish[1],
  "Ambiguous"    = unname(CLASS_COLORS["Other"])   # shared "Other" gray
)

df_fish <- df_fish %>%
  mutate(simple_category = factor(category, levels = SIMPLE_LEVELS))

# =========================================================================
# Panel a: composition (with site labels) and magnitude, one faceted plot
# =========================================================================

PANEL_A_LEVELS <- c("% of fish reads (composition)", "% of non-human reads (magnitude)")

magnitude_data <- df_fish %>%
  group_by(canonical_site) %>%
  summarise(fish_reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(site_totals, by = "canonical_site") %>%
  mutate(pct = fish_reads / site_total_reads * 100)

# The first factor level is drawn at the bottom, so the order is reversed
# to put the first site at the top.
site_label_levels <- if (FIG5A_SORT == "magnitude") {
  magnitude_data %>% arrange(pct) %>% pull(canonical_site) %>% LABEL_LOOKUP[.] %>% unname()
} else {
  rev(unname(LABEL_LOOKUP[site_order_regional]))
}

magnitude_data <- magnitude_data %>%
  mutate(
    site_label = factor(LABEL_LOOKUP[canonical_site], levels = site_label_levels),
    panel = factor(PANEL_A_LEVELS[2], levels = PANEL_A_LEVELS)
  )

# Every site-category segment is drawn at its true width, so each bar sums
# to 100%. Exact values are in the composition table below.
composition_data <- df_fish %>%
  group_by(canonical_site, simple_category) %>%
  summarise(reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(canonical_site) %>%
  mutate(site_fish_reads = sum(reads)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    pct = reads / site_fish_reads * 100,
    simple_category = factor(simple_category, levels = SIMPLE_LEVELS),
    site_label = factor(LABEL_LOOKUP[canonical_site], levels = site_label_levels),
    panel = factor(PANEL_A_LEVELS[1], levels = PANEL_A_LEVELS)
  )

p_panel_a <- ggplot() +
    geom_col(data = composition_data, aes(y = site_label, x = pct, fill = simple_category),
           width = 0.75, color = "black", linewidth = 0.12, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_col(data = magnitude_data, aes(y = site_label, x = pct),
           fill = "grey35", width = 0.75) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x", axes = "margins") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = SIMPLE_COLORS, name = "Category", drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.03))) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.4)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Site") +   # x is described by each panel's strip
  theme_bw(base_size = FIG5_BASE_SIZE) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = FIG5_AXIS_TEXT, color = "black", hjust = 1),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = FIG5_AXIS_TEXT, color = "black"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = FIG5_AXIS_TITLE, color = "black"),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(size = FIG5_AXIS_TITLE, color = "black", face = "bold"),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = unit(1, "mm"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = FIG5_LEGEND_TITLE),
    legend.text = element_text(size = FIG5_LEGEND_TEXT),
    legend.key.size = unit(3.5, "mm"),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(2, "mm"),
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    legend.box.background = element_rect(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3, fill = "white"),
    legend.margin = LEGEND_BOX_MARGIN,
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1, title.position = "left"))

panel_a_final <- p_panel_a

# =========================================================================
# Panel b: top 40 taxa by total reads, log color scale, one block per
# category (free heights), ordered by abundance within each block.
# =========================================================================

top_taxa <- df_fish %>%
  group_by(taxon) %>%
  summarise(total_reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(total_reads)) %>%
  slice_head(n = TOP_N_TAXA)

taxon_category_lookup <- df_fish %>% distinct(taxon, simple_category)
taxon_rank_lookup     <- df_fish %>% distinct(taxon, resolved_rank)

top_taxa_ordered <- top_taxa %>%
  left_join(taxon_category_lookup, by = "taxon") %>%
  left_join(taxon_rank_lookup, by = "taxon") %>%
  mutate(simple_category = factor(simple_category, levels = SIMPLE_LEVELS)) %>%
  arrange(simple_category, desc(total_reads))

taxon_levels <- top_taxa_ordered$taxon

# ---- Labels: common name only -----------------------------------------------
# The lookup already marks "(genus)" or "(family)" for taxa not resolved to
# species. Taxa missing from the lookup use the scientific name.
common_names <- read_common_names()

build_display_label <- function(taxon_vec) {
  cn <- common_names$common_name[match(taxon_vec, common_names$scientific_name)]
  ifelse(is.na(cn), taxon_vec, cn)
}
label_map <- setNames(build_display_label(top_taxa_ordered$taxon), taxon_levels)

unmatched_names <- setdiff(taxon_levels, common_names$scientific_name)
if (length(unmatched_names) > 0) {
  warning(length(unmatched_names), " Figure 5 fish taxa have no entry in taxon_common_names_lookup.csv, ",
          "shown as the scientific name instead: ", paste(unmatched_names, collapse = ", "))
}

heatmap_data <- df_fish %>%
  filter(taxon %in% taxon_levels) %>%
  group_by(canonical_site, taxon) %>%
  summarise(reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(site_totals, by = "canonical_site") %>%
  mutate(pct = reads / site_total_reads * 100)

heatmap_full <- expand_grid(canonical_site = site_order_regional, taxon = taxon_levels) %>%
  left_join(heatmap_data, by = c("canonical_site", "taxon")) %>%
  left_join(top_taxa_ordered %>% select(taxon, simple_category), by = "taxon") %>%
  mutate(
    pct = replace_na(pct, 0),
    site_label = LABEL_LOOKUP[canonical_site],  # order set by scale_x_discrete(limits) below
    taxon = factor(taxon, levels = rev(taxon_levels))
  )

x_levels <- unname(LABEL_LOOKUP[site_order_regional])

p_panel_b <- ggplot() +
  geom_tile(data = heatmap_full, aes(x = site_label, y = taxon, fill = pct),
            color = HEAT_GRID_COLOR, linewidth = HEAT_GRID_WIDTH) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = HEAT_12S_COLORS,
    # Lowest color is gold rather than near-white so faint detections stay visible
    transform = "log10", na.value = "white",
    breaks = c(0.01, 0.1, 1, 10), labels = c("0.01", "0.1", "1", "10"),
    name = "% of non-human\nreads (log)"
  ) +
  facet_grid(simple_category ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = x_levels) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = label_map) +
  labs(x = "Site", y = "Taxon") +
  theme_bw(base_size = FIG5_BASE_SIZE) +
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = FIG5_AXIS_TITLE, color = "black"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = FIG5_AXIS_TITLE, color = "black"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = FIG5_AXIS_TEXT, color = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = FIG5_AXIS_TEXT, color = "black"),
    axis.ticks.x = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing.y = unit(1.2, "mm"),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text.y.right = element_text(size = FIG5_AXIS_TEXT, color = "black", face = "bold",
                                      angle = 0, hjust = 0),
    legend.title = element_text(size = FIG5_LEGEND_TITLE),
    legend.text = element_text(size = FIG5_LEGEND_TEXT),
    legend.key.size = unit(3.5, "mm"),
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    legend.box.background = element_rect(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3, fill = "white"),
    legend.margin = LEGEND_BOX_MARGIN,
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
  )

panel_b_final <- p_panel_b

# =========================================================================
# Combined Figure 5
# =========================================================================

p_fig5 <- cowplot::plot_grid(
  panel_a_final, panel_b_final,
  labels = c("a", "b"), label_size = FIG_PANEL_LABEL_PT, ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(0.85, 1.35)
)
p_fig5 <- cowplot::ggdraw(p_fig5) + theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))

save_figure(p_fig5, fig_file("fish"), width = FIG5_WIDTH_MM, height = FIG5_HEIGHT_MM)
p_fig5

# =========================================================================
# Full fish taxon x site matrix (all fish taxa, not only the top 40).
# Columns are sites in regional order; values are % of the site's
# non-human reads.
# =========================================================================

taxon_site_pct <- df_fish %>%
  group_by(canonical_site, taxon) %>%
  summarise(reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(site_totals, by = "canonical_site") %>%
  mutate(
    pct_of_nonhuman_reads = reads / site_total_reads * 100,
    site_label = LABEL_LOOKUP[canonical_site]
  )

taxon_site_wide <- taxon_site_pct %>%
  select(taxon, site_label, pct_of_nonhuman_reads) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = site_label, values_from = pct_of_nonhuman_reads, values_fill = 0) %>%
  select(taxon, all_of(unname(LABEL_LOOKUP[site_order_regional])))  # enforce regional column order

# Sort rows by total abundance across all sites, most abundant taxon first
taxon_site_wide <- taxon_site_wide %>%
  mutate(.total = rowSums(select(., -taxon))) %>%
  arrange(desc(.total)) %>%
  select(-.total)

taxon_site_out_path <- file.path(analysis_dir, "fish_taxa_by_site_pct_of_nonhuman_reads.tsv")
write_tsv(taxon_site_wide, taxon_site_out_path)
message("Wrote taxon x site abundance table to: ", taxon_site_out_path)

# =========================================================================
# Fish supplementary tables: every fish percentage reported in the figure
# or text, plus the classification reference.
# =========================================================================

# ---- Supplementary Table (fish_classification): classification reference ------------------------------
common_names_fish <- read_common_names()
supp_table_fish_class <- fish_lookup_resolved %>%
  left_join(common_names_fish %>% select(scientific_name, common_name), by = c("taxon" = "scientific_name")) %>%
  arrange(category, taxon) %>%
  transmute(Taxon = taxon, `Common name` = common_name, Category = category, Notes = notes, Source = source)
add_supp_table("fish_classification", supp_table_fish_class,
  paste("One row per fish taxon detected (Figure 5). Category: Aquaculture = farmed or imported dietary",
        "species; Freshwater = wild or native freshwater species; Marine = wild marine or reef species;",
        "Ambiguous = the taxon spans more than one category. Each taxon was assigned the category that",
        "describes most of its US population or supply. Notes give the reasoning and Source the reference."))

# ---- Supplementary Table (fish_by_site): fish by site -----------------------------------------
# One row per site and fish taxon. The site-level columns (fish share of
# non-human reads, category share of fish reads) repeat on every row of
# that site so each number cited in the text can be read from one table.
site_fish_totals <- df_fish %>% group_by(canonical_site) %>% summarise(site_fish_reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop")
category_share <- df_fish %>%
  group_by(canonical_site, simple_category) %>%
  summarise(cat_reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(site_fish_totals, by = "canonical_site") %>%
  mutate(cat_pct = 100 * cat_reads / site_fish_reads)

supp_table_fish_by_site <- df_fish %>%
  group_by(canonical_site, taxon, simple_category, resolved_rank) %>%
  summarise(reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(site_totals, by = "canonical_site") %>%
  left_join(site_fish_totals, by = "canonical_site") %>%
  left_join(category_share %>% select(canonical_site, simple_category, cat_pct),
            by = c("canonical_site", "simple_category")) %>%
  left_join(common_names_fish %>% select(scientific_name, common_name), by = c("taxon" = "scientific_name")) %>%
  mutate(site_rank = match(canonical_site, site_order_regional),
         cat_rank  = match(as.character(simple_category), SIMPLE_LEVELS)) %>%
  arrange(site_rank, cat_rank, desc(reads)) %>%
  transmute(
    Site = unname(LABEL_LOOKUP[canonical_site]),
    `Fish, % of site's non-human reads` = round(100 * site_fish_reads / site_total_reads, 2),
    Category = as.character(simple_category),
    `Category, % of site's fish reads` = round(cat_pct, 2),
    Taxon = taxon,
    `Common name` = common_name,
    `Resolved rank` = resolved_rank,
    Reads = round(reads),
    `Taxon, % of site's fish reads` = round(100 * reads / site_fish_reads, 2),
    `Taxon, % of site's non-human reads` = round(100 * reads / site_total_reads, 3)
  )
add_supp_table("fish_by_site", supp_table_fish_by_site,
  paste("One row per site and fish taxon (Figure 5). Reads are summed over every sample at the site after",
        "the standard filter, with human reads removed. Fish, % of site's non-human reads is the site total",
        "(Figure 5a bar length); Category, % of site's fish reads is the share of the site's fish reads in",
        "that category (Figure 5a segments). Both repeat on each row of the site. The taxon columns give each",
        "fish taxon's own share. Categories are defined in", paste0(supp_table_ref("fish_classification"), ".")))

cat("\nFish supplementary tables: classification", nrow(supp_table_fish_class), "taxa;",
    "fish by site", nrow(supp_table_fish_by_site), "rows.\n")
```


```{r per-taxon-glmm}
# =========================================================================
# Per-taxon mixed models: site and sampling month
# =========================================================================
# For each taxon, does detection depend on site or on sampling month? One
# binomial generalized linear mixed model per taxon:
#
#   detected ~ month + (1 | site)
#
# Unit: one sample (site-date). detected = 1 if the taxon passed
# apply_standard_filter() in that sample, 0 otherwise. Every sample from all
# 27 sites is used, so a site where the taxon was never detected contributes
# zeros. Human and ambiguous Phasianidae/Bovidae family calls are excluded.
# Taxa are resolved names at family, genus and species level, not merged
# across ranks (same taxon definition as fingerprint-stats).
#
# Predictors
#   month       sampling month as a 17-level factor, 2025-04 to 2026-08.
#               Years are not pooled: April 2025 and April 2026 are separate
#               levels. Samples from Mar 30-31 2025 are counted as 2025-04
#               and samples from Sep 1-5 2026 as 2026-08.
#   (1 | site)  random intercept. Each site has its own baseline detection
#               rate, so repeated samples from one site are not treated as
#               independent.
#
# Tests (likelihood ratio, per taxon)
#   month: full model vs the same model without month.
#   site: full model vs the same model without (1 | site). A variance cannot
#     be negative, so under the null the parameter sits on the boundary and
#     the chi-square(1) p-value is halved (Self and Liang 1987).
#   p-values are adjusted across taxa with Benjamini-Hochberg, separately
#   for each term.
#
# Estimates
#   site        SD of the site random intercept (log-odds scale). Larger
#               values mean detection is concentrated at fewer sites; used to
#               rank site-restricted taxa.
#   month       no single estimate (16 coefficients); the LRT chi-square
#               measures the strength of the month effect and is used to
#               rank taxa.
#
# Fit problems. Taxa detected at one or two sites, or in few samples, can
# give extreme estimates (separation) or fail to fit. Every test is kept and
# flagged: "Fit failed" (no p-value) or "Convergence warning" (the optimizer
# did not report convergence or the Hessian was not positive definite).
#
# Run time: three model fits per taxon for ~260 taxa. Results are cached in
# stats_dir; set GLMM_REFIT <- TRUE after the data change.
# Output: Supplementary Table (per_taxon_glmm). da_samples, da_det and da_results are used
# by figure8-temporal-variation.

GLMM_ALPHA <- 0.05
GLMM_REFIT <- FALSE
GLMM_CACHE <- file.path(stats_dir, "per_taxon_glmm.rds")

DA_FIRST_MONTH  <- as.Date("2025-04-01")
DA_LAST_MONTH   <- as.Date("2026-08-01")
DA_MONTH_LEVELS <- format(seq(DA_FIRST_MONTH, DA_LAST_MONTH, by = "1 month"), "%Y-%m")

# ---- Samples: every parsed site-date, whether or not anything was detected ----------
if (!exists("all_parsed")) all_parsed <- read_csv(parsed_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

da_samples <- all_parsed %>%
  distinct(canonical_site, date) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) %>%
  filter(date <= STUDY_END_DATE) %>%
  mutate(month_start = floor_date(date, "month"))

outside_months <- unique(da_samples$month_start[da_samples$month_start < DA_FIRST_MONTH |
                                                  da_samples$month_start > DA_LAST_MONTH])
if (any(!outside_months %in% as.Date(c("2025-03-01", "2026-09-01")))) {
  stop("Samples fall outside March 2025 - September 2026: ", paste(outside_months, collapse = ", "))
}

da_samples <- da_samples %>%
  mutate(month_start = pmin(pmax(month_start, DA_FIRST_MONTH), DA_LAST_MONTH),
         month = factor(format(month_start, "%Y-%m"), levels = DA_MONTH_LEVELS)) %>%
  select(-month_start)
stopifnot(n_distinct(da_samples$canonical_site) == N_SITES_TOTAL)

# ---- Detections ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reads per taxon per sample = sum of the taxon's sequences that passed the
# filter in that sample. Read counts are retained for reuse; the detection
# models use presence and absence only.
da_rows <- load_detections() %>%
  semi_join(da_samples, by = c("canonical_site", "date"))

da_det <- da_rows %>%
  group_by(resolved_rank, resolved_name, canonical_site, date) %>%
  summarise(reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop")

da_class <- da_rows %>%
  filter(!is.na(class)) %>%
  distinct(resolved_name, class) %>%
  distinct(resolved_name, .keep_all = TRUE)

da_taxa <- da_det %>%
  group_by(resolved_rank, resolved_name) %>%
  summarise(n_sites_detected = n_distinct(canonical_site),
            n_positive = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(da_class, by = "resolved_name") %>%
  arrange(resolved_rank, resolved_name)
cat("Samples:", nrow(da_samples), "| Taxa:", nrow(da_taxa), "\n")

# ---- Model helpers --------------------------------------------------------------------
fit_glmm <- function(formula, data) {
  tryCatch(suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(glmmTMB(formula, data = data, family = binomial))),
           error = function(e) NULL)
}
fit_ok <- function(m) !is.null(m) && isTRUE(m$fit$convergence == 0) && isTRUE(m$sdr$pdHess)
loglik_df <- function(m) {
  ll <- if (is.null(m)) NA else tryCatch(logLik(m), error = function(e) NA)
  if (length(ll) != 1 || is.na(ll)) return(c(ll = NA_real_, df = NA_real_))
  c(ll = as.numeric(ll), df = as.numeric(attr(ll, "df")))
}
lrt <- function(full, reduced, boundary = FALSE) {
  a <- loglik_df(full); b <- loglik_df(reduced)
  if (anyNA(c(a, b))) return(c(chisq = NA_real_, df = NA_real_, p = NA_real_))
  chisq <- max(0, 2 * (a[["ll"]] - b[["ll"]]))
  df <- a[["df"]] - b[["df"]]
  p <- pchisq(chisq, df = df, lower.tail = FALSE)
  if (boundary) p <- if (chisq > 0) p / 2 else 1
  c(chisq = chisq, df = df, p = p)
}

run_taxon <- function(rank, name) {
  d <- da_samples %>%
    left_join(da_det %>% filter(resolved_rank == rank, resolved_name == name) %>%
                transmute(canonical_site, date, detected = 1L),
              by = c("canonical_site", "date")) %>%
    mutate(detected = replace_na(detected, 0L))

  m_full     <- fit_glmm(detected ~ month + (1 | canonical_site), d)
  m_no_month <- fit_glmm(detected ~ 1 + (1 | canonical_site), d)
  m_no_site  <- fit_glmm(detected ~ month, d)

  est_site <- tryCatch(unname(attr(VarCorr(m_full)$cond$canonical_site, "stddev")), error = function(e) NA_real_)

  tests <- list(
    month = list(reduced = m_no_month, boundary = FALSE, estimate = NA_real_),
    site  = list(reduced = m_no_site,  boundary = TRUE,  estimate = est_site)
  )
  purrr::imap_dfr(tests, function(tt, term) {
    r <- lrt(m_full, tt$reduced, tt$boundary)
    ok <- fit_ok(m_full) && fit_ok(tt$reduced)
    tibble(resolved_rank = rank, resolved_name = name, term = term,
           estimate = tt$estimate, chisq = r[["chisq"]], df = r[["df"]], p = r[["p"]],
           note = case_when(is.na(r[["p"]]) ~ "Fit failed",
                            !ok             ~ "Convergence warning",
                            TRUE            ~ NA_character_))
  })
}

# ---- Fit every taxon ----------------------------------------------------------------------
GLMM_TERMS <- c("month", "site")
glmm_cache_ok <- !GLMM_REFIT && file.exists(GLMM_CACHE)
if (glmm_cache_ok) {
  glmm_raw <- readRDS(GLMM_CACHE)
  if (!setequal(unique(glmm_raw$term), GLMM_TERMS) ||
      !setequal(unique(glmm_raw$resolved_name), da_taxa$resolved_name)) {
    cat("Cached fits do not match the current model or taxa; refitting.\n")
    glmm_cache_ok <- FALSE
  }
}
if (glmm_cache_ok) {
  cat("Using cached", basename(GLMM_CACHE), "(set GLMM_REFIT <- TRUE to refit)\n")
} else {
  glmm_raw <- purrr::map2_dfr(da_taxa$resolved_rank, da_taxa$resolved_name, run_taxon, .progress = TRUE)
  saveRDS(glmm_raw, GLMM_CACHE)
}

da_results <- glmm_raw %>%
  group_by(term) %>%
  mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(da_taxa, by = c("resolved_rank", "resolved_name"))

# ---- Supplementary Table (per_taxon_glmm): one row per taxon -----------------------------------------------
common_names_glmm <- read_common_names()
fmt_tab_p <- function(p) signif(p, 3)

glmm_wide <- da_results %>%
  select(resolved_rank, resolved_name, term, estimate, chisq, p, p_adj, note) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = c(estimate, chisq, p, p_adj, note))

supp_table_glmm <- da_taxa %>%
  left_join(glmm_wide, by = c("resolved_rank", "resolved_name")) %>%
  left_join(common_names_glmm %>% select(scientific_name, common_name),
            by = c("resolved_name" = "scientific_name")) %>%
  mutate(fit_note = pmap_chr(list(note_site, note_month), function(...) {
    x <- unique(na.omit(c(...)))
    if (length(x) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(x, collapse = "; ")
  })) %>%
  arrange(desc(estimate_site)) %>%
  transmute(
    Taxon = resolved_name,
    `Common name` = common_name,
    Rank = resolved_rank,
    `Class` = broad_cat(class),
    `Sites detected (of 27)` = n_sites_detected,
    `Positive samples` = n_positive,
    `Site: random intercept SD` = round(estimate_site, 2),
    `Site: LRT chi-square` = round(chisq_site, 2),
    `Site: p` = fmt_tab_p(p_site),
    `Site: adjusted p` = fmt_tab_p(p_adj_site),
    `Month: LRT chi-square (16 df)` = round(chisq_month, 2),
    `Month: p` = fmt_tab_p(p_month),
    `Month: adjusted p` = fmt_tab_p(p_adj_month),
    `Fit note` = fit_note
  )

add_supp_table("per_taxon_glmm", supp_table_glmm,
  paste("One row per non-human taxon. Each taxon was modeled as detected (1) or not (0) in every sample from",
        "all 27 sites: detected ~ sampling month + (1 | site), binomial GLMM (glmmTMB).",
        "Each term was tested by likelihood ratio test against the model without it; the site test compares",
        "the model with and without the site random intercept, with the p-value halved because a variance",
        "is tested at its boundary of zero. Adjusted p = Benjamini-Hochberg across taxa, separately per term.",
        "Site: random intercept SD is on the log-odds scale; larger values mean detection is concentrated at",
        "fewer sites. Month is a 17-level factor (2025-04 to 2026-08, years not pooled). Rows are sorted by the",
        "site SD. Fit note flags models that failed to fit or did not converge cleanly, mostly taxa found at",
        "one or two sites; interpret those rows with care."))

# ---- Summary --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
glmm_summary <- da_results %>%
  group_by(term) %>%
  summarise(taxa_tested = sum(!is.na(p)),
            significant = sum(p_adj < GLMM_ALPHA, na.rm = TRUE),
            not_fit = sum(is.na(p)),
            convergence_warning = sum(note %in% "Convergence warning"),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(pct_significant = round(100 * significant / taxa_tested, 1))
save_both(glmm_summary, "per_taxon_glmm_summary")

cat("\nPer-taxon GLMM, BH-adjusted p <", GLMM_ALPHA, ":\n")
print(as.data.frame(glmm_summary), row.names = FALSE)
```


```{r figure6-distinctive-detections}
# Figure 6: vertebrate detections that distinguish individual sites. Ten
# taxa chosen as clear examples (not an exhaustive list), each linked to a
# facility (zoo, equine facility, caviar farm) or to regional presence
# (native, invasive, or otherwise notable). 5 x 2 grid in facet order.
#
# Every panel shows all 27 sites in region order, so an empty row means
# "not detected here." One dot per site and date with a detection, fixed
# size, colored by state. A grey line under each row spans that site's
# first to last sampling date: a line with no dots means sampled but not
# detected, and no line means not yet sampled. The line does not show gaps
# within that range.
#
# Panel titles show a PhyloPic silhouette (phylopic.org) above the common
# name. Silhouettes are downloaded once with rphylopic into
# working_dir/silhouettes and reused. A PNG with the same file name placed
# in that folder replaces the download. Contributor and license for each
# image are written to silhouettes/silhouette_attributions.csv for the
# acknowledgments.
#
# Taxa (facet order):
#   1-3  Hippopotamus, giraffe, gentoo penguin: zoo animals.
#   4    Scarlet ibis (Eudocimus ruber), Palo Alto: kept at the Palo Alto Zoo.
#   5    Sturgeon (Acipenseridae, family rank). White and Amur sturgeon share
#        this 12S region and cannot be separated by this assay. Mostly at
#        Sacramento (near white sturgeon caviar farms) and Palo Alto (San
#        Francisco Bay estuary, native range of white sturgeon).
#   6    Mongoose (Urva), Hawaii County, HI: invasive.
#   7    Cattle egret (Bubulcus ibis), Kauai County, HI.
#   8    Horse (Equus caballus), Columbia, MO: 15 dates. Other sites show
#        only single, low-read traces that do not pass the filter.
#   9    Bluefish (Pomatomus saltator, the name in the reference taxonomy;
#        also written P. saltatrix), Boston (both plants).
#   10   Gray snapper (Lutjanus griseus), Miami: within its native range.
#
# axes = "margins": only the left column shows site labels and only the
# bottom row shows dates. Date breaks start at the first full calendar
# month of the study. The legend lists only states present in the data.


FIG6_WIDTH_MM    <- 180
FIG6_HEIGHT_MM   <- 150
FIG6_BASE_SIZE   <- 6.5
FIG6_AXIS_TEXT   <- 5.5
FIG6_SITE_TEXT   <- 5
FIG6_ICON_HEIGHT <- 11      # silhouette height in the panel title (px at 96 dpi)
FIG6_RANGE_COLOR <- SAMPLING_RANGE_COLOR
FIG6_RANGE_WIDTH <- SAMPLING_RANGE_WIDTH

# phylopic_name = the name searched on PhyloPic. Where no image exists for
# the taxon, a close relative is used.
FIGURE6_TAXA <- tribble(
  ~taxon,                       ~common_name,           ~facet_order, ~phylopic_name,
  "Hippopotamus amphibius",     "Hippopotamus",          1,           "Hippopotamus amphibius",
  "Giraffa",                    "Giraffe",               2,           "Giraffa camelopardalis",
  "Pygoscelis papua",           "Gentoo penguin",        3,           "Pygoscelis papua",
  "Eudocimus ruber",            "Scarlet ibis",          4,           "Eudocimus ruber",
  "Acipenseridae",              "Amur/White sturgeon",   5,           "Acipenser transmontanus",
  "Urva",                       "Mongoose",              6,           "Urva auropunctata",
  "Bubulcus ibis",              "Cattle egret",          7,           "Bubulcus ibis",
  "Equus caballus",             "Horse",                 8,           "Equus caballus",
  "Pomatomus saltator",         "Bluefish",              9,           "Pomatomus saltatrix",
  "Lutjanus griseus",           "Gray snapper",         10,           "Lutjanus griseus"
)

# ---- Silhouettes: download once, then reuse ---------------------------------
# For each taxon, tries the phylopic_name, then its genus (via rphylopic's
# name search). A failed download only drops that one silhouette. The
# figure still builds, with a warning naming the taxon.
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a

SILHOUETTE_DIR <- file.path(working_dir, "silhouettes")
dir_create(SILHOUETTE_DIR)

silhouette_file <- function(common_name) {
  file.path(SILHOUETTE_DIR, paste0(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", tolower(common_name)), ".png"))
}

fetch_silhouette <- function(search_name, path) {
  if (!requireNamespace("rphylopic", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("rphylopic is not installed. Run install.packages(\"rphylopic\").")
  }
  candidates <- unique(c(search_name, word(search_name, 1)))
  for (nm in candidates) {
    uuid <- tryCatch(rphylopic::get_uuid(name = nm, n = 1), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(uuid) || length(uuid) == 0 || is.na(uuid[1])) next
    img <- tryCatch(rphylopic::get_phylopic(uuid = uuid[1], format = "raster", height = 256),
                    error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(img)) next
    png::writePNG(img, path)
    attr_info <- tryCatch(rphylopic::get_attribution(uuid = uuid[1]), error = function(e) list())
    return(tibble(search_name = search_name, matched_name = nm, uuid = uuid[1],
                  contributor = attr_info$contributor %||% NA_character_,
                  license = attr_info$license %||% NA_character_))
  }
  NULL
}

attribution_path <- file.path(SILHOUETTE_DIR, "silhouette_attributions.csv")
attributions <- if (file.exists(attribution_path)) {
  read_csv(attribution_path, show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = cols(.default = "c"))
} else {
  tibble(search_name = character(), matched_name = character(), uuid = character(),
         contributor = character(), license = character())
}

for (i in seq_len(nrow(FIGURE6_TAXA))) {
  path <- silhouette_file(FIGURE6_TAXA$common_name[i])
  if (file.exists(path)) next   # already downloaded, or replaced by hand
  got <- tryCatch(fetch_silhouette(FIGURE6_TAXA$phylopic_name[i], path),
                  error = function(e) { warning(conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
  if (is.null(got)) {
    warning("No silhouette for ", FIGURE6_TAXA$common_name[i],
            ". Add a PNG by hand at ", path)
  } else {
    attributions <- bind_rows(attributions %>% filter(search_name != got$search_name), got)
  }
}
if (nrow(attributions) > 0) write_csv(attributions, attribution_path)

# Panel titles: silhouette above the common name (markdown, rendered by
# ggtext::element_markdown). Taxa without a silhouette file get the name only.
FIGURE6_TAXA <- FIGURE6_TAXA %>%
  mutate(
    icon_path   = silhouette_file(common_name),
    strip_label = if_else(file.exists(icon_path),
                          sprintf("<img src='%s' height='%s'/><br>%s",
                                  normalizePath(icon_path, winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE),
                                  FIG6_ICON_HEIGHT, common_name),
                          common_name),
    facet_label = factor(common_name, levels = common_name[order(facet_order)])
  )
strip_labeller <- as_labeller(setNames(FIGURE6_TAXA$strip_label, FIGURE6_TAXA$common_name))

# ---- Detection data: standard filter -----------------------------------
df <- load_detections(drop_human = FALSE) %>% mutate(taxon = resolved_name)

# ---- Site order: ALL 27 sites, region-ordered (not just sites with a
# detection) ------------------------------------------------------------------
site_labels_df <- read_site_labels()

sort_tbl <- site_labels_df %>%
  mutate(region = factor(region, levels = REGION_ORDER)) %>%
  arrange(region, state, shorthand_for_figures)
site_order_master <- sort_tbl$current_site_label
LABEL_LOOKUP <- setNames(sort_tbl$shorthand_for_figures, sort_tbl$current_site_label)

detections <- df %>%
  filter(taxon %in% FIGURE6_TAXA$taxon) %>%
  distinct(canonical_site, date, taxon, state) %>%
  left_join(FIGURE6_TAXA %>% select(taxon, common_name, facet_label), by = "taxon")

supp_table_notable_wildlife <- detections %>%
  transmute(Taxon = taxon, `Common name` = common_name, Site = LABEL_LOOKUP[canonical_site],
            State = state, Date = date) %>%
  arrange(Taxon, Date)
add_supp_table("notable_detections", supp_table_notable_wildlife,
  paste("One row per detection of a Figure 6 taxon: the taxon passed the standard filter at that site on",
        "that collection date. Taxa were chosen as clear examples of site-specific signals (zoo animals,",
        "farmed or captive species, and native or invasive wildlife with a restricted range), not as an",
        "exhaustive list. Statistical support for site restriction across all taxa is in",
        paste0(supp_table_ref("per_taxon_glmm"), ".")))

# Gulls are not a Figure 6 panel, but the Discussion cites gull detections at
# Palo Alto by month, so their dates need to be in the supplement too. Added
# as extra rows of the same table rather than an eleventh panel, which would
# break the 5 x 2 grid.
gull_detections <- df %>%
  filter(genus %in% "Larus" | resolved_name %in% "Larus" |
           str_starts(resolved_name, "Larus ")) %>%
  distinct(canonical_site, date, taxon = resolved_name, state) %>%
  transmute(Taxon = taxon, `Common name` = "Gull", Site = LABEL_LOOKUP[canonical_site],
            State = state, Date = date)

supp_table_notable_wildlife <- bind_rows(supp_table_notable_wildlife, gull_detections) %>%
  arrange(Taxon, Date)
add_supp_table("notable_detections", supp_table_notable_wildlife,
  paste("One row per detection of a Figure 6 taxon, plus every gull (Larus) detection: the taxon passed",
        "the standard filter at that site on that collection date. Taxa were chosen as clear examples of",
        "site-specific signals (zoo animals, farmed or captive species, and native or invasive wildlife",
        "with a restricted range), not as an exhaustive list. Gulls are included because they are cited in",
        "the Discussion but are not a Figure 6 panel. Statistical support for site restriction across all",
        "taxa is in", paste0(supp_table_ref("per_taxon_glmm"), ".")))

cat("Gull (Larus) detections added to the notable-detections table:",
    nrow(gull_detections), "site-dates at", n_distinct(gull_detections$Site), "sites\n")

missing_taxa <- setdiff(FIGURE6_TAXA$taxon, unique(detections$taxon))
if (length(missing_taxa) > 0) {
  warning("Expected taxa not found in current data: ", paste(missing_taxa, collapse = ", "),
          ". Check that the apply_standard_filter() rules have not changed.")
}

detections <- detections %>% mutate(site_f = factor(canonical_site, levels = rev(site_order_master)))

# ---- Sampling range per site (every collected sample, not just detections),
# repeated in every panel ----------------------------------------------------
sampling_range <- all_parsed %>%
  distinct(canonical_site, date) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) %>%
  group_by(canonical_site) %>%
  summarise(start = min(date), end = max(date), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(canonical_site %in% site_order_master) %>%
  mutate(site_f = factor(canonical_site, levels = rev(site_order_master))) %>%
  tidyr::crossing(FIGURE6_TAXA %>% select(facet_label))

# x-axis spans the full study window
plot_max_date <- STUDY_END_DATE
axis_min_date <- STUDY_START_DATE

break_start <- as.Date(format(axis_min_date, "%Y-%m-01"))
if (break_start < axis_min_date) break_start <- break_start %m+% months(1)
x_breaks <- seq(break_start, plot_max_date, by = "3 months")

p_fig6 <- ggplot() +
  geom_segment(data = sampling_range,
               aes(x = start, xend = end, y = site_f, yend = site_f),
               color = FIG6_RANGE_COLOR, linewidth = FIG6_RANGE_WIDTH, alpha = SAMPLING_RANGE_ALPHA) +
  geom_point(data = detections, aes(x = date, y = site_f, color = state),
             size = 1.2, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_color_manual(values = STATE_COLORS, limits = names(STATE_COLORS),
                      breaks = names(STATE_COLORS)[names(STATE_COLORS) %in% unique(detections$state)],
                      name = "State") +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = LABEL_LOOKUP, limits = rev(site_order_master)) +
  scale_x_date(limits = c(axis_min_date, plot_max_date), breaks = x_breaks, date_labels = "%m-%Y",
               expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
  facet_wrap(~facet_label, ncol = 5, axes = "margins", labeller = strip_labeller) +
  labs(x = "Collection date", y = "Site") +
  theme_bw(base_size = FIG6_BASE_SIZE) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = ggtext::element_markdown(size = FIG6_BASE_SIZE, lineheight = 1.1, halign = 0.5),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = FIG6_SITE_TEXT, color = "black"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = FIG6_AXIS_TEXT, color = "black"),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),   # the range lines take the place of row gridlines
    panel.spacing = unit(1.5, "mm"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.key.size = unit(3, "mm"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = FIG6_BASE_SIZE),
    legend.text = element_text(size = FIG6_AXIS_TEXT),
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    legend.box.background = element_rect(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3, fill = "white"),
    legend.margin = LEGEND_BOX_MARGIN
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 1, override.aes = list(size = 2)))

save_figure(p_fig6, fig_file("distinctive_detections"), width = FIG6_WIDTH_MM, height = FIG6_HEIGHT_MM)
p_fig6
```
