```{r figure7-rats}
# Figure 7: Rattus species by site.
#   a) Map with one pie per site or metro area (Kansas City, St. Louis,
#      Boston, Chicago combined). Slices are the share of rat detection
#      dates by species. A site or metro area is shown only if any rat was
#      detected on at least RAT_MAP_THRESHOLD_PCT of its sampling dates
#      (Columbia, Milan, and Monett fall below this). Ontario and Riverside,
#      CA are offset to avoid overlap, with leader lines to their true
#      locations. Hawaii is an inset.
#   b) One dot per site and date with a rat detection, sized by read count,
#      one panel per species. All 27 sites are shown, including sites with
#      no detections. As in Figure 6, a grey line shows each site's
#      sampling period and the x-axis spans the full study. A strip left
#      of the panels shows each site's sewer system type (combined or
#      sanitary, Table S1).
#      Sewer system type is shown here only; it is not tested.
#
# Requires the scatterpie and maps packages.

FIG7_WIDTH_MM     <- 180
FIG7_HEIGHT_MM    <- 170             # Nature Communications maximum
FIG7_REL_HEIGHTS  <- c(92, 78)       # rows: map (a), dot panels (b), in mm
FIG7_BASE_SIZE    <- 6.5
FIG7_AXIS_TEXT    <- 6
FIG7_SITE_TEXT    <- 5
FIG7_AXIS_TITLE   <- 6.5
FIG7_LABEL_SIZE   <- 8   # cowplot panel letters, matches NComms 8pt spec


# Sewer system type and region per site, from Table S1. The strip left of
# panel b shows system type; it is shown here only and is not tested.
site_sewer  <- setNames(as.character(site_table$system), site_table$canonical_site)
stopifnot(!anyNA(site_sewer), all(site_sewer %in% c("Combined", "Sanitary")))
site_region <- setNames(as.character(site_table$region), site_table$canonical_site)

RAT_SPECIES <- c("Rattus norvegicus" = "Norway rat", "Rattus rattus" = "Black rat", "Rattus exulans" = "Pacific rat")
# Okabe-Ito colors (Okabe and Ito 2008): blue, orange and reddish purple stay
# distinct under the common forms of color blindness. Used by the map pies
# and the dot panels.
RAT_COLORS  <- c("Norway rat" = "#0072B2", "Black rat" = "#CC79A7", "Pacific rat" = "#E69F00")
RAT_LEVELS  <- unname(RAT_SPECIES)

RAT_MAP_THRESHOLD_PCT <- 15  # a SITE (or combined metro area) needs ANY Rattus species detected
                              # on >=15% of its total sampling dates to appear on the map at all.


# Plotting positions for markers that overlap. map_group is the site ID for
# sites outside METRO_GROUPS. Leader lines run back to the true location.
MAP_OFFSETS <- tribble(
  ~map_group,             ~plot_lat, ~plot_lon,
  "CA_Ontario_RP1",        34.9,     -116.8,
  "CA_Riverside_RWQCP",    33.0,     -116.8
)

METRO_GROUPS <- list(
  "Kansas City, MO" = c("MO_KC_BlueRiver", "MO_KC_Westside"),
  "St. Louis, MO"   = c("MO_STL_Bissell", "MO_STL_Lemay", "MO_STL_Coldwater_Florissant", "MO_STL_MORiver"),
  "Boston, MA"      = c("MA_Boston_DITPN", "MA_Boston_DITPS"),
  "Chicago, IL"     = c("IL_Chicago_A", "IL_Chicago_B", "IL_Chicago_C", "IL_Chicago_D1", "IL_Chicago_D2")
)
grouped_sites <- unlist(METRO_GROUPS)
group_lookup  <- setNames(rep(names(METRO_GROUPS), lengths(METRO_GROUPS)), grouped_sites)

# ---- Detection data: standard filter, Rattus only --------------------------
df <- load_detections() %>% filter(genus == "Rattus", resolved_rank == "species")

n_dates_by_species <- df %>%
  distinct(canonical_site, species, date) %>%
  count(canonical_site, species, name = "n_dates")

sites_no_rats <- setdiff(unique(all_parsed$canonical_site), unique(n_dates_by_species$canonical_site))
if (length(sites_no_rats) > 0) {
  cat("Site(s) with no qualifying Rattus detections at all (still shown as an empty row in Panel b):",
      paste(sites_no_rats, collapse = ", "), "\n")
}

occurrence_composition <- n_dates_by_species %>%
  group_by(canonical_site) %>%
  mutate(total_dates = sum(n_dates), pct = n_dates / total_dates * 100) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(species_label = factor(unname(RAT_SPECIES[species]), levels = RAT_LEVELS))

# ---- Site coordinates -------------------------------------------------------
site_labels_df <- read_site_labels()

# parse_lat_lon() and MANUAL_COORDS are defined in the setup chunk.
# Plant coordinates are not released, so a clone has none and the map in
# panel a cannot be drawn. Panel b and everything else run either way.
HAS_COORDS <- "lat_lon" %in% names(site_labels_df) && any(!is.na(site_labels_df$lat_lon))
if (!HAS_COORDS) {
  message("No site coordinates available; Figure 7 is drawn as panel b only. ",
          "Panel a is a map of the treatment plants and cannot be made from ",
          "released data without disclosing their locations.")
}

site_coords <- if (HAS_COORDS) {
  site_labels_df %>%
    select(current_site_label, shorthand_for_figures, state, region, lat_lon) %>%
    bind_cols(parse_lat_lon(.$lat_lon)) %>%
    select(-lat_lon) %>%
    rows_update(MANUAL_COORDS, by = "current_site_label")
} else {
  site_labels_df %>%
    transmute(current_site_label, shorthand_for_figures, state, region,
              lat = NA_real_, lon = NA_real_)
}

if (HAS_COORDS) {   # everything to p_panel_a draws the map

# ---- Map-only: "any rat" overall gate, evaluated at the metro-combined level
# Samples = site-dates, as everywhere else. The manifest has one row per raw
# file, so replicate files on the same date are counted once.
# One row per sample. sample_metadata.csv is not released, so when it is
# absent the same sample list is taken from the parsed data, which was built
# from those files and gives the same site and date pairs.
site_total_samples <- (if (file.exists(metadata_path)) {
  read_csv(metadata_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    filter(category == "main") %>%
    mutate(date = as.Date(date), canonical_site = recode_site(canonical_site))
} else {
  all_parsed %>% mutate(date = as.Date(date))
}) %>%
  filter(date <= STUDY_END_DATE) %>%
  distinct(canonical_site, date) %>%
  count(canonical_site, name = "total_samples")

any_rat_dates <- df %>%
  mutate(map_group = coalesce(group_lookup[canonical_site], canonical_site)) %>%
  distinct(map_group, date) %>%
  count(map_group, name = "any_rat_dates")

map_total_samples <- site_total_samples %>%
  mutate(map_group = coalesce(group_lookup[canonical_site], canonical_site)) %>%
  group_by(map_group) %>%
  summarise(total_samples = sum(total_samples), .groups = "drop")

map_gate <- any_rat_dates %>%
  left_join(map_total_samples, by = "map_group") %>%
  mutate(pct_any_rat = any_rat_dates / total_samples * 100)

sites_excluded <- map_gate %>% filter(pct_any_rat < RAT_MAP_THRESHOLD_PCT)
if (nrow(sites_excluded) > 0) {
  cat("Site(s)/metro area(s) excluded from Figure 7 map (any-rat detection below",
      RAT_MAP_THRESHOLD_PCT, "% of total sampling dates):\n")
  print(sites_excluded %>% arrange(pct_any_rat))
}

included_groups <- map_gate %>% filter(pct_any_rat >= RAT_MAP_THRESHOLD_PCT) %>% pull(map_group)

occurrence_for_map <- occurrence_composition %>%
  mutate(map_group = coalesce(group_lookup[canonical_site], canonical_site)) %>%
  filter(map_group %in% included_groups) %>%
  group_by(map_group, species, species_label) %>%
  summarise(n_dates = sum(n_dates), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(map_group) %>%
  mutate(pct = n_dates / sum(n_dates) * 100) %>%
  ungroup()

write_csv(map_gate, file.path(stats_dir, "rat_map_gate.csv"))
write_csv(occurrence_for_map %>% mutate(map_group_label = map_group),
          file.path(stats_dir, "rat_occurrence_for_map.csv"))

map_coords <- site_coords %>%
  mutate(map_group = coalesce(group_lookup[current_site_label], current_site_label)) %>%
  group_by(map_group) %>%
  summarise(lat = mean(lat), lon = mean(lon), state = first(state), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(MAP_OFFSETS, by = "map_group") %>%
  mutate(
    is_offset = !is.na(plot_lat),
    plot_lat  = coalesce(plot_lat, lat),
    plot_lon  = coalesce(plot_lon, lon)
  )

pie_wide <- occurrence_for_map %>%
  select(map_group, species_label, n_dates) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = species_label, values_from = n_dates, values_fill = 0) %>%
  left_join(map_coords, by = "map_group") %>%
  mutate(radius = 0.7)

for (sp in RAT_LEVELS) if (!sp %in% names(pie_wide)) pie_wide[[sp]] <- 0
pie_cols <- RAT_LEVELS

continental_pies <- pie_wide %>% filter(state != "HI")
hawaii_pies      <- pie_wide %>% filter(state == "HI")
leader_lines     <- continental_pies %>% filter(is_offset)

# ---- Main continental US map ------------------------------------------------
us_states <- map_data("state")

p_map_main <- ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = us_states, aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
               fill = "grey95", color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.2) +
  { if (nrow(leader_lines) > 0)
      geom_segment(data = leader_lines, aes(x = lon, y = lat, xend = plot_lon, yend = plot_lat),
                   color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dashed") } +
  geom_scatterpie(data = continental_pies, aes(x = plot_lon, y = plot_lat, r = radius),
                   cols = pie_cols, color = "black", linewidth = 0.2, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = RAT_COLORS, name = NULL, drop = FALSE, limits = RAT_LEVELS) +
  coord_fixed(1.3, xlim = c(-125, -66), ylim = c(24, 49.5)) +
  theme_void(base_size = FIG7_BASE_SIZE) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
        plot.margin = margin(6, 0, 0, 0))

# ---- Hawaii inset ------------------------------------------------------------
hi_islands <- map_data("world", region = "USA:Hawaii")

p_map_hi <- ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = hi_islands, aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
               fill = "grey95", color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_scatterpie(data = hawaii_pies, aes(x = plot_lon, y = plot_lat, r = radius * 0.6),
                   cols = pie_cols, color = "black", linewidth = 0.2, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = RAT_COLORS, guide = "none", drop = FALSE, limits = RAT_LEVELS) +
  coord_fixed(1.1, xlim = c(-160.5, -154.5), ylim = c(18.5, 22.5)) +
  theme_void(base_size = FIG7_BASE_SIZE) +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
  )

# The species legend is drawn inside the map, over the empty ocean east of
# Florida, so the map can use the full width of the figure.
FIG7_LEGEND_X <- 0.85   # legend position and size, as fractions of the map
FIG7_LEGEND_Y <- 0.24
FIG7_LEGEND_W <- 0.14
FIG7_LEGEND_H <- 0.22

legend_dummy <- tibble(species_label = factor(RAT_LEVELS, levels = RAT_LEVELS), x = 1, y = 1)
legend_src <- ggplot(legend_dummy, aes(x, y, fill = species_label)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = RAT_COLORS, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.key.size = unit(3.5, "mm"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = FIG7_AXIS_TEXT),
        legend.background = element_blank(),
        legend.box.background = element_rect(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3, fill = "white"),
        legend.margin = LEGEND_BOX_MARGIN)
map_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(legend_src)

p_map_combined <- cowplot::ggdraw(p_map_main) +
  cowplot::draw_plot(p_map_hi, x = 0.02, y = 0.02, width = 0.28, height = 0.28) +
  cowplot::draw_grob(map_legend, x = FIG7_LEGEND_X, y = FIG7_LEGEND_Y,
                     width = FIG7_LEGEND_W, height = FIG7_LEGEND_H)

# The map is drawn at a fixed aspect ratio. It gets the full height of its
# row and is centered, so the Hawaii inset sits at the map's lower left.
FIG7_MAP_ASPECT <- (125 - 66) / ((49.5 - 24) * 1.3)   # width / height, from coord_fixed above
fig7_map_h <- FIG7_HEIGHT_MM * FIG7_REL_HEIGHTS[1] / sum(FIG7_REL_HEIGHTS)
fig7_map_w <- min(FIG7_WIDTH_MM, fig7_map_h * FIG7_MAP_ASPECT)
fig7_side  <- (FIG7_WIDTH_MM - fig7_map_w) / 2
p_panel_a <- cowplot::plot_grid(NULL, p_map_combined, NULL, nrow = 1,
                                rel_widths = c(fig7_side, fig7_map_w, fig7_side))

}   # end if (HAS_COORDS)

# =========================================================================
# Panel b: all 27 sites, one dot per detection date
# =========================================================================

rat_detections <- df %>%
  group_by(canonical_site, date, species) %>%
  summarise(reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(species_label = factor(unname(RAT_SPECIES[species]), levels = RAT_LEVELS))

# Rows come from every site in the labels file, so sites with no rat
# detections still appear as empty rows.
sort_tbl <- site_labels_df %>%
  mutate(region = factor(region, levels = REGION_ORDER)) %>%
  arrange(region, state, shorthand_for_figures)
site_order <- rev(sort_tbl$current_site_label)
LABEL_LOOKUP <- setNames(sort_tbl$shorthand_for_figures, sort_tbl$current_site_label)

rat_detections <- rat_detections %>% mutate(site_f = factor(canonical_site, levels = site_order))

# Each site's sampling period, drawn as a grey line in every species panel
sampling_range_rat <- all_parsed %>%
  distinct(canonical_site, date) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) %>%
  filter(date <= STUDY_END_DATE) %>%
  group_by(canonical_site) %>%
  summarise(start = min(date), end = max(date), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(canonical_site %in% site_order) %>%
  mutate(site_f = factor(canonical_site, levels = site_order)) %>%
  tidyr::crossing(species_label = factor(RAT_LEVELS, levels = RAT_LEVELS))

# x-axis spans the full sampling period, with quarterly breaks starting at
# the first full calendar month (same as Figure 6)
plot_max_date <- STUDY_END_DATE
axis_min_date <- STUDY_START_DATE

break_start <- as.Date(format(axis_min_date, "%Y-%m-01"))
if (break_start < axis_min_date) break_start <- break_start %m+% months(1)
x_breaks <- seq(break_start, plot_max_date, by = "3 months")

p_rat_dots <- ggplot() +
  geom_segment(data = sampling_range_rat,
               aes(x = start, xend = end, y = site_f, yend = site_f),
               color = SAMPLING_RANGE_COLOR, linewidth = SAMPLING_RANGE_WIDTH, alpha = SAMPLING_RANGE_ALPHA) +
    geom_point(data = rat_detections,
             aes(x = date, y = site_f, size = reads, color = species_label), alpha = 0.85) +
  # Minimum dot size 0.9 so low-read detections (most Pacific rat weeks) stay visible
  scale_size(range = c(0.9, 4.5), name = "Read count") +
  scale_color_manual(values = RAT_COLORS, name = NULL) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = LABEL_LOOKUP, drop = FALSE, limits = site_order, expand = expansion(add = 0.4)) +
  scale_x_date(limits = c(axis_min_date, plot_max_date), breaks = x_breaks, date_labels = "%m-%Y",
               expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
  facet_wrap(~species_label, nrow = 1, axes = "margins") +
  labs(x = "Collection date", y = "Site") +
  theme_bw(base_size = FIG7_BASE_SIZE) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = FIG7_AXIS_TITLE),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = FIG7_SITE_TEXT, color = "black"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = FIG7_AXIS_TEXT, color = "black"),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),   # the sampling lines replace row gridlines
    panel.spacing = unit(1.5, "mm"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.key.size = unit(3, "mm"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = FIG7_AXIS_TEXT),
    legend.text = element_text(size = FIG7_AXIS_TEXT),
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    legend.box.background = element_rect(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3, fill = "white"),
    legend.margin = LEGEND_BOX_MARGIN,
    plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2)
  ) +
  guides(color = "none")

# ---- Panel b: sewer system type strip ------------------------------------------
# One tile per site, on the same rows as the dot panels. The strip carries
# the site names, so the dot panels drop theirs. The facet gives the strip
# a blank title row the same height as the species titles, so rows line
# up. The column is too narrow for a title; the legend names it.
SEWER_STRIP_COLORS <- c(Combined = "grey30", Sanitary = "grey80")
FIG7_STRIP_WIDTH   <- 0.24   # strip + site names, relative to the dot panels (1). The site names take most of this, so small changes resize the strip a lot.

sewer_strip_df <- tibble(canonical_site = site_order) %>%
  mutate(sewer  = factor(unname(site_sewer[canonical_site]), levels = names(SEWER_STRIP_COLORS)),
         site_f = factor(canonical_site, levels = site_order),
         strip  = " ")   # blank title keeps the rows aligned with the species panels
stopifnot(!anyNA(sewer_strip_df$sewer))

p_sewer_strip <- ggplot(sewer_strip_df, aes(x = 1, y = site_f, fill = sewer)) +
  geom_tile(width = 1, height = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~ strip) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = SEWER_STRIP_COLORS, name = "Sewer system") +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = LABEL_LOOKUP, drop = FALSE, limits = site_order, expand = expansion(add = 0.4)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), breaks = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Site") +
  theme_bw(base_size = FIG7_BASE_SIZE) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = FIG7_AXIS_TITLE),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = FIG7_SITE_TEXT, color = "black"),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.size = unit(3, "mm"),
        legend.title = element_text(size = FIG7_AXIS_TEXT),
        legend.text = element_text(size = FIG7_AXIS_TEXT),
        legend.background = element_blank(),
        legend.box.background = element_rect(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3, fill = "white"),
        legend.margin = LEGEND_BOX_MARGIN,
        plot.margin = margin(2, 0, 2, 2))

# Both legends go in one row under panel b, so the strip and dot panels
# keep the same height and their rows line up.
fig7_size_legend  <- cowplot::get_legend(p_rat_dots)
fig7_sewer_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(p_sewer_strip)
p_rat_dots_nolab  <- p_rat_dots +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none", plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 1))
p_panel_b_body <- cowplot::plot_grid(p_sewer_strip + theme(legend.position = "none"), p_rat_dots_nolab,
                                     nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(FIG7_STRIP_WIDTH, 1),
                                     align = "h", axis = "tb")
p_panel_b <- cowplot::plot_grid(p_panel_b_body,
                                cowplot::plot_grid(fig7_sewer_legend, fig7_size_legend, nrow = 1),
                                ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(1, 0.12))

# =========================================================================
# Combined Figure 7. The map gets the larger share of the height.
# =========================================================================

# Without coordinates there is no map, so the figure is panel b alone and
# keeps no letters: see the message in the site coordinates section above.
p_fig7 <- if (HAS_COORDS) {
  cowplot::plot_grid(p_panel_a, p_panel_b, ncol = 1, labels = c("a", "b"),
                     label_size = FIG7_LABEL_SIZE, rel_heights = FIG7_REL_HEIGHTS)
} else {
  p_panel_b
}
p_fig7 <- cowplot::ggdraw(p_fig7) + theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))

save_figure(p_fig7, fig_file("rats"), width = FIG7_WIDTH_MM,
            height = if (HAS_COORDS) FIG7_HEIGHT_MM else FIG7_REL_HEIGHTS[2])
p_fig7

# ---- Supplementary Table (rats_by_site): Rattus species by site and metro area ----------------
# Every site, not limited by the map threshold. Sites with no rat
# detections get explicit zero rows. Each row is one site and species; the
# metro-area columns pool the sites of a metro area the same way the map
# does (Boston, Chicago, Kansas City, St. Louis) and repeat on each of
# that metro area's rows. For single-site areas the two sets of columns
# are the same.
rat_species_grid <- tidyr::crossing(
  canonical_site = site_labels_df$current_site_label,
  species = names(RAT_SPECIES)
)

rat_site_counts <- rat_species_grid %>%
  left_join(n_dates_by_species, by = c("canonical_site", "species")) %>%
  mutate(n_dates = replace_na(n_dates, 0),
         map_group = coalesce(unname(group_lookup[canonical_site]), canonical_site)) %>%
  group_by(canonical_site) %>%
  mutate(site_total = sum(n_dates)) %>%
  group_by(map_group, species) %>%
  mutate(metro_species = sum(n_dates)) %>%
  group_by(map_group) %>%
  mutate(metro_total = sum(n_dates)) %>%
  ungroup()

supp_table_rats <- rat_site_counts %>%
  mutate(site_rank = match(canonical_site, sort_tbl$current_site_label)) %>%
    arrange(site_rank, match(unname(RAT_SPECIES[species]), RAT_LEVELS)) %>%   # figure order: Norway, black, Pacific
  transmute(
    `Metro area` = coalesce(unname(LABEL_LOOKUP[map_group]), map_group),
    Site = unname(LABEL_LOOKUP[canonical_site]),
    Species = unname(RAT_SPECIES[species]),
    `Dates detected (site)` = n_dates,
    `Rattus dates, all species (site)` = site_total,
    `% of site's Rattus detections` = if_else(site_total > 0, round(100 * n_dates / site_total, 1), NA_real_),
    `Dates detected (metro area)` = metro_species,
    `Rattus dates, all species (metro area)` = metro_total,
    `% of metro area's Rattus detections` = if_else(metro_total > 0, round(100 * metro_species / metro_total, 1), NA_real_)
  )
add_supp_table("rats_by_site", supp_table_rats,
  paste("One row per site and Rattus species (Figure 7). Dates detected = collection dates on which the",
        "species passed the standard filter at the site. % of Rattus detections = that species' share of all",
        "Rattus detection dates at the site (Figure 7b) or in the metro area (Figure 7a pies). Metro areas pool",
        "the plants of one city; other sites are their own area. All 27 sites are listed, including sites",
        "without rat detections, regardless of the map threshold."))
```


```{r figure8-temporal-variation}
# =========================================================================
# Figure 8: temporal variation in detection of wild taxa
# =========================================================================
# Shows when detection of selected wild taxa rose during the study, and
# which months were significantly elevated.
#
# Taxa shown. Selected by hand from the taxa with a significant month
# effect in the per-taxon GLMM (BH-adjusted p < 0.05) that are wild (not
# livestock, poultry, pets, commensal rodents or pigeons, or farmed and
# dietary fish) and detected at 3 or more sites. Every taxon tested is in
# the per-taxon GLMM supplementary table.
#
# Curve. Smoothed detection rate: for each day, the share of samples with a
# detection, weighting each sample by a Gaussian kernel on its collection
# date (SD = SEAS_BW_DAYS). Positive and total samples are weighted the same
# way, so periods with more samples do not create peaks. Samples are from
# the taxon's detecting sites. Ticks below the curve are positive samples.
#
# Elevated months (grey). For each sampling month, positive ~ this_month +
# (1 | site) is compared with positive ~ (1 | site) by likelihood ratio
# test (1 df), using the same samples as the curve. p-values are adjusted
# across the 17 months of each taxon (Benjamini-Hochberg). A month is
# shaded when its estimate is positive and adjusted p <= SEAS_SHADE_ALPHA:
# detection that month was higher than in the rest of the study.
#
# Strip p-value: BH-adjusted month p from the per-taxon GLMM.
#
# Sampling covered 17 months and only April to August were sampled in both
# years, so these results describe change over the study period, not a
# confirmed annual cycle.
# Output: Figure 8, Supplementary Table (elevated_months),
#         stats_dir/temporal_elevated_months_by_month.csv

FIG8_WIDTH_MM    <- 136   # 1.5 column, wide enough for a one-row legend
FIG8_HEIGHT_MM   <- 150
FIG8_BASE_SIZE   <- FONT_BASE
FIG8_AXIS_TEXT   <- FONT_AXIS
FIG8_AXIS_TITLE  <- FONT_TITLE
FIG8_TAXON_SIZE  <- FONT_TITLE   # bold taxon name in each strip
FIG8_STAT_TEXT   <- FONT_AXIS    # (n sites, p) after the taxon name
ELEVATED_BAND    <- "grey85"
SEAS_BW_DAYS     <- 21
SEAS_SHADE_ALPHA <- 0.05

SEAS_TAXA <- tribble(
  ~resolved_rank, ~resolved_name,          ~label,            ~class,
  "genus",        "Odocoileus",            "Deer",            "Mammal",
  "family",       "Turdidae",              "Thrushes",        "Bird",
  "family",       "Sturnidae",             "Starlings",       "Bird",
  "species",      "Aplodinotus grunniens", "Freshwater drum", "Fish",
  "genus",        "Pomoxis",               "Crappie",         "Fish",
  "genus",        "Lepomis",               "Sunfish",         "Fish",
  "species",      "Morone chrysops",       "White bass",      "Fish"
)
SEAS_LEVELS <- SEAS_TAXA$label

# ---- Month p from the per-taxon GLMM --------------------------------------------------
SEAS_TAXA <- SEAS_TAXA %>%
  left_join(da_results %>% filter(term == "month") %>%
              select(resolved_rank, resolved_name, p_adj, n_sites_detected, n_positive),
            by = c("resolved_rank", "resolved_name"))
if (any(is.na(SEAS_TAXA$p_adj))) {
  stop("No month p-value for: ", paste(SEAS_TAXA$label[is.na(SEAS_TAXA$p_adj)], collapse = ", "))
}

# ---- Samples per taxon (detecting sites only) ---------------------------------------------
seas_samples <- purrr::pmap_dfr(SEAS_TAXA, function(resolved_rank, resolved_name, label, class, ...) {
  pos <- da_det %>%
    filter(resolved_rank == !!resolved_rank, resolved_name == !!resolved_name) %>%
    distinct(canonical_site, date) %>%
    mutate(positive = 1L)
  da_samples %>%
    filter(canonical_site %in% pos$canonical_site) %>%
    select(canonical_site, date, month) %>%
    left_join(pos, by = c("canonical_site", "date")) %>%
    mutate(positive = replace_na(positive, 0L), label = label, class = class)
})

# ---- Elevated months: each month vs all other months -----------------------------------------
month_vs_rest <- function(d) {
  m0 <- glmmTMB(positive ~ 1 + (1 | canonical_site), data = d, family = binomial)
  purrr::map_dfr(levels(d$month), function(mo) {
    d$this_month <- as.integer(d$month == mo)
    n_month <- sum(d$this_month)
    pos_month <- sum(d$positive[d$this_month == 1])
    if (n_month == 0 || pos_month == 0) {
      return(tibble(month = mo, samples = n_month, positives = pos_month, estimate = -Inf, p = 1))
    }
    m1 <- glmmTMB(positive ~ this_month + (1 | canonical_site), data = d, family = binomial)
    chisq <- max(0, 2 * (as.numeric(logLik(m1)) - as.numeric(logLik(m0))))
    tibble(month = mo, samples = n_month, positives = pos_month,
           estimate = fixef(m1)$cond[["this_month"]],
           p = pchisq(chisq, df = 1, lower.tail = FALSE))
  })
}

seas_months <- seas_samples %>%
  group_by(label) %>%
  group_modify(~ month_vs_rest(.x)) %>%
  mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(elevated = estimate > 0 & p_adj <= SEAS_SHADE_ALPHA)

write_csv(seas_months %>%
            transmute(Taxon = label, Month = month, Samples = samples, `Positive samples` = positives,
                      `Detection rate (%)` = round(100 * positives / samples, 1),
                      `Odds ratio vs other months` = signif(exp(estimate), 3),
                      p = signif(p, 3), `Adjusted p` = signif(p_adj, 3), Elevated = elevated),
          file.path(stats_dir, "temporal_elevated_months_by_month.csv"))

# ---- Supplementary Table (elevated_months): one row per taxon ------------------------------------------------
seas_rates <- seas_samples %>%
  left_join(seas_months %>% select(label, month, elevated), by = c("label", "month")) %>%
  group_by(label) %>%
  summarise(samples_elev  = sum(elevated), rate_elev  = 100 * mean(positive[elevated]),
            samples_other = sum(!elevated), rate_other = 100 * mean(positive[!elevated]),
            .groups = "drop")

supp_table_elevated <- SEAS_TAXA %>%
  left_join(seas_months %>% filter(elevated) %>% group_by(label) %>%
              summarise(months = paste(month, collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop"), by = "label") %>%
  left_join(seas_rates, by = "label") %>%
  transmute(Taxon = resolved_name, `Common name` = label, Class = class,
            `Sites detected (of 27)` = n_sites_detected, `Positive samples` = n_positive,
            !!paste0("Month effect, adjusted p (", supp_table_ref("per_taxon_glmm"), ")") := signif(p_adj, 3),
            `Elevated months` = months,
            `Samples in elevated months` = samples_elev,
            `Detection rate, elevated months (%)` = round(rate_elev, 1),
            `Samples in other months` = samples_other,
            `Detection rate, other months (%)` = round(rate_other, 1))

add_supp_table("elevated_months", supp_table_elevated,
  paste("One row per taxon in Figure 8. Elevated months are sampling months in which detection was higher",
        "than in all other months combined: positive ~ this month + (1 | site) vs positive ~ (1 | site),",
        "likelihood ratio test, Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted across the 17 months of each taxon, adjusted p <= 0.05.",
        "Detection rate = positive samples / samples collected, using samples from the sites where the taxon",
        "was detected. Only April to August were sampled in both years, so elevated months describe change",
        "over the study period, not a confirmed annual cycle. Month-by-month results are in",
        "stats/temporal_elevated_months_by_month.csv."))

# ---- Shading: whole sampling months --------------------------------------------------------------
# The first month starts on STUDY_START_DATE (Mar 30-31 count as April) and
# the last month ends on STUDY_END_DATE (Sep 1-5 count as August).
first_date <- STUDY_START_DATE
last_date  <- STUDY_END_DATE

seas_bands <- seas_months %>%
  filter(elevated) %>%
  mutate(xmin = as.Date(paste0(month, "-01")),
         xmax = xmin %m+% months(1),
         xmin = if_else(month == DA_MONTH_LEVELS[1], first_date, xmin),
         xmax = if_else(month == tail(DA_MONTH_LEVELS, 1), last_date, xmax),
         label = factor(label, levels = SEAS_LEVELS))

# ---- Smoothed detection rate -----------------------------------------------------------------------
seas_grid <- seq(first_date, last_date, by = "1 day")
smooth_rate <- function(dates, positive) {
  w <- outer(as.numeric(seas_grid), as.numeric(dates), function(a, b) dnorm(a - b, sd = SEAS_BW_DAYS))
  as.vector(w %*% positive) / rowSums(w)
}

seas_curves <- seas_samples %>%
  group_by(label, class) %>%
  summarise(y = list(100 * smooth_rate(date, positive)), date = list(seas_grid), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::unnest(c(date, y)) %>%
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = SEAS_LEVELS))

seas_rug <- seas_samples %>%
  filter(positive == 1L) %>%
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = SEAS_LEVELS))

y_top   <- ceiling(max(seas_curves$y) / 10) * 10
RUG_TOP <- -0.06 * y_top
RUG_BOT <- -0.26 * y_top

# ---- Strips: name (n sites, p) ------------------------------------------------------------------
fmt_p_glmm <- function(p) if_else(p < 0.001, "p < 0.001", sprintf("p = %.3f", p))
strip_seas <- setNames(
  sprintf("<span style='font-size:%spt'>**%s**</span> <span style='font-size:%spt'>(%d %s, %s)</span>",
          FIG8_TAXON_SIZE, SEAS_TAXA$label, FIG8_STAT_TEXT,
          SEAS_TAXA$n_sites_detected, if_else(SEAS_TAXA$n_sites_detected == 1, "site", "sites"),
          fmt_p_glmm(SEAS_TAXA$p_adj)),
  SEAS_TAXA$label
)

# ---- Colors: one CLASS_STEPS shade per class ------------------------------------------------------
seas_class_present <- intersect(names(CLASS_COLORS), unique(SEAS_TAXA$class))
seas_fill <- vapply(seas_class_present, function(cl) {
  steps <- CLASS_STEPS[[cl]]
  steps[min(3, length(steps))]
}, character(1))

# ---- Plot -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Legend keys: elevated month (alpha), positive sample (linetype, drawn as a
# vertical tick) and class (fill). The alpha and linetype scales only create
# legend entries; they do not change how the shading or ticks are drawn.
p_temporal <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = seas_bands, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
                                   alpha = "Elevated month(s)"),
            fill = ELEVATED_BAND, color = NA) +
  geom_area(data = seas_curves, aes(x = date, y = y, fill = class, color = class),
            linewidth = 0.3, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_segment(data = seas_rug, aes(x = date, xend = date, y = RUG_BOT, yend = RUG_TOP,
                                    color = class, linetype = "Positive sample"),
               linewidth = 0.25, key_glyph = "vpath") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = seas_fill, breaks = seas_class_present, name = "Class") +
  scale_color_manual(values = CLASS_COLORS[seas_class_present], guide = "none") +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c("Elevated month(s)" = 1), name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Positive sample" = "solid"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%m-%Y", expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(RUG_BOT * 1.08, y_top), breaks = seq(0, y_top, by = y_top / 2),
                     labels = function(v) paste0(v, "%"), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  facet_wrap(~ label, ncol = 1, labeller = as_labeller(strip_seas)) +
  labs(x = "Collection date", y = "Samples with detection (%)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = FIG8_BASE_SIZE) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(color = "black", size = FIG8_BASE_SIZE),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = FIG8_AXIS_TEXT),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "black", size = FIG8_AXIS_TITLE),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.ticks.y = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.2),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey85", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.spacing = unit(1.5, "mm"),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = ggtext::element_markdown(hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 2, b = 1)),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box = "horizontal",        # all keys on one row
    legend.spacing.x = unit(1.5, "mm"),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(1.5, "mm"),
    legend.key.size = unit(3, "mm"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = FIG8_AXIS_TEXT),
    legend.text = element_text(size = FIG8_AXIS_TEXT),
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    legend.box.background = element_rect(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3, fill = "white"),
    legend.margin = LEGEND_BOX_MARGIN,
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2)
  ) +
  guides(alpha    = guide_legend(order = 1),
         linetype = guide_legend(order = 2, override.aes = list(color = "black", linewidth = 0.4)),
         fill     = guide_legend(order = 3, nrow = 1, override.aes = list(color = NA)))

save_figure(p_temporal, fig_file("temporal_variation"), width = FIG8_WIDTH_MM, height = FIG8_HEIGHT_MM)
p_temporal

cat("\nFigure 8 taxa:\n")
print(as.data.frame(supp_table_elevated %>%
                      select(`Common name`, `Elevated months`, `Detection rate, elevated months (%)`,
                             `Detection rate, other months (%)`)), row.names = FALSE)
```


```{r figure9-virus-host}
# =========================================================================
# Figure 9: virus detections and host nucleic acid
# =========================================================================
# Does a virus turn up in wastewater where and when its host's nucleic acid
# does? Each pair links one virus (metagenomic reads) to the host it
# infects, identified in the 12S data:
#   Luchacovirus (Lucheng Rn rat coronavirus)    -> rat (any Rattus species);
#                                                   "Rn" in the name = Rattus
#                                                   norvegicus, tested below
#   Rat hepatitis E virus (Rocahepevirus ratti)  -> rat (any Rattus species);
#                                                   zoonotic
#   Passerivirus A1 (formerly turdivirus 1)      -> thrushes (Turdidae); first
#                                                   described from dead wild
#                                                   thrushes
#   Micropterus salmoides rhabdovirus            -> largemouth bass
#                                                   (Micropterus salmoides)
#
# Virus data: the Public Health Dashboard export (data through
#   2026-09-30), one value per metagenomic sample. Virus abundance is reads
#   per 10 million tobamovirus reads (RPMT), the dashboard's normalization
#   for sequencing depth and fecal strength. Tobamoviruses (such as pepper
#   mild mottle virus) come from diet and are shed in human feces, so they
#   scale with how much sewage, and how deep the sequencing, a sample has.
#   Raw read counts are arbitrary because samples are sequenced to
#   different depths. Each sample's total reads are recovered from the
#   dashboard's reads-per-billion values and used as a depth covariate in
#   the detection models below. Samples are binned to the Sunday study
#   weeks, like the 12S data. Two samples in one week: reads and depth are
#   summed, and RPMT is pooled (summed virus reads / summed tobamovirus
#   reads). Passerivirus A1 weeks are then restricted to those with a
#   BLAST-verified read (see the Passerivirus block below).
#
# Host 12S: standard filter, human removed. Every 12S sample counts,
#   including samples where nothing non-human passed the filter (host not
#   detected). Two 12S samples in one week: host detected if either had it;
#   % of non-human reads is the mean of the two.
#
# Unit: a paired week = a site-week with both a 12S and a metagenomic
#   sample. Sites with only one of the two data sets are dropped.
#
# Per virus:
#   - share of virus-positive weeks that also had host nucleic acid, and
#     share of the virus abundance (summed RPMT) that fell in those weeks
#   - virus detection rate in weeks with vs without host nucleic acid
#   - binomial GLMM: virus detected ~ host detected + log10 sequencing depth
#     + (1 | site). The random intercept compares weeks within a site, so the
#     odds ratio is not just "sites with more rats have more rat virus". The
#     depth term accounts for deeper samples finding a virus more often. LRT
#     against the same model without host.
#   - site level: Spearman correlation between the share of a site's
#     paired weeks with the virus and with host nucleic acid
#   - Each pair is tested separately, so LRT p-values are also adjusted
#     across all pairs (Benjamini-Hochberg).
#
# Follow-up (both rat viruses): the main tests pair each rat virus with
#   rat nucleic acid (any Rattus). Each rat virus is also tested against each
#   rat species alone, and in one GLMM with Norway rat and black rat nucleic
#   acid as joint predictors, to see which species it tracks. Reported
#   separately, not in the Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. A supplementary
#   figure shows which rat species were present in the weeks each rat virus
#   was found.
#
# Analysis only (not in the manuscript): Passerivirus A1 tested against
#   other candidate hosts (starlings, thrushes or starlings, wild
#   passerines). Virus-positive weeks without host nucleic acid are listed
#   by date in stats/virus_weeks_without_host.csv.
#
# Figures:
#   Figure 9a: site x week heatmap, drawn compact, with four panels:
#     Norway rat nucleic acid, black rat nucleic acid, then each rat virus.
#     The two host panels share one color scale, so each virus can be read
#     against each species directly. Pacific rat (Kauai County only) has no
#     panel; Figure 7 shows all three species. Legends are drawn under the
#     panels so four panels fit at 180 mm without shrinking the weekly
#     tiles. The numbers are in the table.
#   Figure 9b-c: thrush (b) and largemouth bass (c). Each panel is the
#     share of paired sites with a host and with a virus detection each
#     week, smoothed with a centered 5-week moving average (as in Justen
#     et al. 2026), drawn as a strip above a dot plot of every
#     virus-positive paired week by site and week. Point size is virus
#     RPMT and point color is whether host nucleic acid was detected that
#     week, so the strip gives the summary and the dots give the evidence
#     behind it. Rats are not drawn as dots: panel a already shows their
#     timing, and 513 and 861 virus-positive weeks are too dense for points.
#
# Output: Supplementary Table (virus_host), one table with a summary row per
#   pair, then one row per site.

FIG9_WIDTH_MM    <- 180
FIG9_HEIGHT_MM   <- 168   # Nature Communications maximum is 170 mm
FIG9_A_HEIGHT    <- 68    # relative heights of the rows: a, then b-c.
FIG9_BC_HEIGHT   <- 70    #   a carries four panels and a legend row below them
TS_STRIP_HEIGHT  <- 23    # b-c: height of the smoothed series row
DOT_PANEL_HEIGHT <- 77    # b-c: height of the dot plot row
VH_DOT_RANGE     <- c(0.25, 1.9)        # point size range in the dot plots, mm
VH_DOT_BREAKS    <- c(0.1, 1, 10, 100)  # size legend breaks, RPMT
VH_LEGEND_WIDTH  <- 0.14                # shared legend column, as a share of b-c.
                                        # Panel a draws its legends underneath its
                                        # panels and runs the full figure width, so
                                        # b-c end short of a's right edge by this
                                        # much. Set to 0 and move these legends below
                                        # as well if the two blocks must end level.
TS_WINDOW_WEEKS  <- 5     # centered moving-average window
TS_MIN_WEEKS     <- 3     # weeks with data needed inside the window
VIRUS_BAR_BREAKS <- c(1, 100, 10000)  # ticks on the virus color bar. Every
                                       # decade crowds 100 against 1,000 at this
                                       # bar length, so every other decade is used

# Panel titles are drawn as markdown so they can be bolded without the
# strip theme forcing a face. Wrapped titles arrive with newlines, which
# markdown needs as <br>.
md_bold <- function(x) paste0("**", str_replace_all(x, "\n", "**<br>**"), "**")

# Panel letters are drawn on the assembled figure, not inside the strips:
# both &nbsp; entities and literal non-breaking spaces are collapsed by
# gridtext, which leaves the letter jammed against its title.
# x = left edge of each letter, in figure widths. a and b share a position
# because the first heatmap panel and the b panel start at the same place;
# c sits the same distance left of the c panel. Nudge if a letter clips a
# title or drifts into the panel beside it.
VH_LABEL_X <- c(a = 0.157, b = 0.157, c = 0.5155)

RAT_HEAT_COLORS   <- HEAT_12S_COLORS          # same as every 12S heatmap
VIRUS_HEAT_COLORS <- HEAT_VIRUS_COLORS[-1]    # palest shade dropped so low counts are distinct from GAP_FILL

# Virus counts come from one of two places. The dashboard export is the
# original source but is not public, so when it is absent this chunk reads
# the per-week table written out below, which holds only what the analysis
# uses: site code, week, virus, virus reads, and the two denominators.
# Both routes produce the same virus_weekly table and the same figures.
DASHBOARD_FILE     <- "Public Health Dashboard 20261004.html"
VIRUS_WEEKLY_FILE  <- "virus_weekly_reads.csv"
USE_DASHBOARD      <- !PUBLIC_RELEASE && file.exists(file.path(working_dir, DASHBOARD_FILE))
VIRUS_HOST_PAIRS <- tribble(
  ~virus_id, ~virus_label,                        ~taxid,     ~host_id,
  "luch",    "Lucheng Rn rat coronavirus",        "1508224",  "rat",
  "rhev",    "Rat hepatitis E virus",             "1678145",  "rat",
  "pasv",    "Passerivirus A1",                   "871699",   "thrush",
  "msrv",    "Micropterus salmoides rhabdovirus", "2527734",  "lmb"
)
VH_DEPTH_COVARIATE <- TRUE   # FALSE drops the sequencing depth term from the detection models
HOST_LABELS <- c(rat = "Rat", nrat = "Norway rat", brat = "Black rat", thrush = "Thrush",
                 lmb = "Largemouth bass", starling = "Starling",
                 thrush_starling = "Thrush or starling", passerine = "Wild passerine")
# Text between the panel letter and the panel title in the heatmaps
VH_PANEL_SEP <- "  "
VH_TITLE_WRAP  <- 24            # characters per line in heatmap panel titles
                                # (titles are top-aligned, so one- and two-line
                                # titles start at the same height)
VH_LEGEND_BAR  <- unit(14, "mm") # color bar length in the heatmap legends

# Which bird detections count as wild, used only by the Passerivirus host
# check below. A bird is wild unless it is a food bird, a farmed, kept or
# zoo bird, a family-level Anatidae call (which cannot be told apart from
# food ducks), or a pigeon or dove (Columbidae calls cannot separate feral
# or kept pigeons from wild doves).
FOOD_BIRD_GENERA        <- c("Gallus", "Meleagris", "Anas", "Anser", "Numida", "Coturnix")
KEPT_BIRD_GENERA        <- c("Cairina",  # muscovy duck: farmed or kept
                             "Cygnus")   # black-necked swan: zoo or kept
EXCLUDE_ANATIDAE_FAMILY <- TRUE
INCLUDE_PIGEONS         <- FALSE
PIGEON_FAMILY           <- "Columbidae"

is_wild_bird <- function(class, family, genus, rank) {
  class %in% "Aves" &
    !(genus %in% c(FOOD_BIRD_GENERA, KEPT_BIRD_GENERA)) &
    !(EXCLUDE_ANATIDAE_FAMILY & rank %in% "family" & family %in% "Anatidae") &
    (INCLUDE_PIGEONS | !(family %in% PIGEON_FAMILY))
}

# Rows of the filtered 12S data that belong to a host. The starling and
# passerine hosts are used only in the Passerivirus host check. Wild
# passerines use the wild bird definition above
# (is_wild_bird), limited to order Passeriformes.
host_rows <- function(d, host_id) {
  switch(host_id,
    rat      = !is.na(d$genus) & d$genus == "Rattus" & d$resolved_rank == "species",
    nrat     = d$resolved_name %in% "Rattus norvegicus",
    brat     = d$resolved_name %in% "Rattus rattus",
    thrush   = !is.na(d$family) & d$family == "Turdidae",
    lmb      = d$resolved_name %in% "Micropterus salmoides",
    starling = !is.na(d$family) & d$family == "Sturnidae",
    thrush_starling = !is.na(d$family) & d$family %in% c("Turdidae", "Sturnidae"),
    passerine = d$order %in% "Passeriformes" &
                is_wild_bird(d$class, d$family, d$genus, d$resolved_rank),
    stop("No host definition for ", host_id))
}

# Site codes in the dashboard -> canonical site labels. Dashboard-only
# sites are ignored.
META_SITE_MAP <- if (has_private_file(DASHBOARD_SITE_MAP_FILE)) {
  k <- read_csv(file.path(working_dir, DASHBOARD_SITE_MAP_FILE), show_col_types = FALSE)
  setNames(recode_site(k$canonical_site), k$dashboard_code)
} else {
  character(0)   # public release: sites come from virus_weekly_reads.csv
}

site_labels_df <- read_site_labels()
site_label_map <- setNames(site_labels_df$shorthand_for_figures, site_labels_df$current_site_label)
site_state_map <- setNames(site_labels_df$state, site_labels_df$current_site_label)

# ---- Virus counts ------------------------------------------------------------------
if (USE_DASHBOARD) {

  # The dashboard HTML holds its data as one JSON object on the line that
  # starts "const DATA = ". For each site and sample date it gives raw reads,
  # reads per billion total reads (RPB) and RPMT for every detected virus.
  # Viruses not listed for a sample date had zero reads.
  dash_line <- grep("^\\s*const DATA = ", readLines(file.path(working_dir, DASHBOARD_FILE), warn = FALSE,
                                                   encoding = "UTF-8"), value = TRUE)
  stopifnot(length(dash_line) == 1)
  dash <- jsonlite::fromJSON(sub(";\\s*$", "", sub("^\\s*const DATA = ", "", dash_line)),
                             simplifyVector = FALSE)$sewersheds
  dash <- dash[intersect(names(dash), names(META_SITE_MAP))]
  rm(dash_line)

  # Values of one dashboard field for all sample dates of one site, long format
  dash_values <- function(site, field) {
    purrr::imap_dfr(dash[[site]][[field]], function(by_date, taxid) {
      tibble(taxid = taxid, date = names(by_date), value = as.numeric(unlist(by_date)))
    })
  }

  # Per sample: total reads and tobamovirus reads, recovered from any
  # detected virus (reads / RPB * 1e9 and reads / RPMT * 1e7; every virus in
  # a sample shares the same denominators, so the median is taken)
  dash_depth <- purrr::map_dfr(names(dash), function(site) {
    raw <- dash_values(site, "viruses")
    rpb <- dash_values(site, "viruses_rpb")
    rpmt <- dash_values(site, "viruses_rpmt")
    raw %>%
      rename(reads = value) %>%
      left_join(rpb %>% rename(rpb = value), by = c("taxid", "date")) %>%
      left_join(rpmt %>% rename(rpmt = value), by = c("taxid", "date")) %>%
      filter(reads > 0) %>%
      group_by(date) %>%
      summarise(total_reads = median(reads / rpb * 1e9, na.rm = TRUE),
                tobamo_reads = median(reads / rpmt * 1e7, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
      mutate(meta_site = site)
  }) %>%
    mutate(across(c(total_reads, tobamo_reads), ~ if_else(is.finite(.x), .x, NA_real_)))

  # One row per site, week and virus, for the four viruses in the manuscript
  virus_weekly <- purrr::map_dfr(VIRUS_HOST_PAIRS$taxid, function(taxid) {
    purrr::map_dfr(names(dash), function(site) {
      dates <- unlist(dash[[site]]$dates)
      v <- dash[[site]]$viruses[[taxid]]
      tibble(meta_site = site, date = dates,
             virus_reads = if (is.null(v)) 0 else coalesce(as.numeric(unlist(v)[dates]), 0))
    }) %>%
      left_join(dash_depth, by = c("meta_site", "date")) %>%
      mutate(canonical_site = unname(META_SITE_MAP[meta_site]),
             date = as.Date(date)) %>%
      filter(date >= STUDY_START_DATE) %>%
      mutate(week = study_week(date), taxid = taxid) %>%
      group_by(taxid, canonical_site, week) %>%
      summarise(virus_reads  = sum(virus_reads),
                total_reads  = sum(total_reads),
                tobamo_reads = sum(tobamo_reads), .groups = "drop")
  })

  # Written out so the chunk can run without the dashboard export
  write_csv(virus_weekly, file.path(working_dir, VIRUS_WEEKLY_FILE))

} else {

  message("No ", DASHBOARD_FILE, " in working_dir; reading ", VIRUS_WEEKLY_FILE, " instead.")
  virus_weekly <- read_csv(file.path(working_dir, VIRUS_WEEKLY_FILE), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(taxid = as.character(taxid), week = as.Date(week),
           canonical_site = recode_site(canonical_site))
  stopifnot(all(VIRUS_HOST_PAIRS$taxid %in% virus_weekly$taxid))

}

# Weekly reads, depth and RPMT for one virus at every paired site
read_virus_weekly <- function(taxid) {
  virus_weekly %>%
    filter(taxid == !!taxid) %>%
    select(canonical_site, week, virus_reads, total_reads, tobamo_reads) %>%
    mutate(virus_rpmt = if_else(tobamo_reads > 0, 1e7 * virus_reads / tobamo_reads, NA_real_))
}

cat("Site-weeks without a recovered sequencing depth:",
    sum(is.na(virus_weekly$total_reads[virus_weekly$taxid == VIRUS_HOST_PAIRS$taxid[1]])), "\n")

# ---- Host 12S per site per week ---------------------------------------------------
# Sites with virus data. The public release has no dashboard map, so it
# takes the sites from virus_weekly_reads.csv.
VH_SITES <- if (length(META_SITE_MAP) > 0) unname(META_SITE_MAP) else unique(virus_weekly$canonical_site)

samples_12s <- all_parsed %>%
  distinct(canonical_site, date) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) %>%
  filter(canonical_site %in% VH_SITES, date <= STUDY_END_DATE)

df_12s <- load_detections() %>%
  filter(canonical_site %in% VH_SITES)

host_week <- function(host_id) {
  d <- df_12s
  d$is_host <- host_rows(d, host_id)
  per_sample <- d %>%
    group_by(canonical_site, date) %>%
    summarise(host_reads = sum(reads[is_host]), nonhuman_reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop")
  samples_12s %>%
    left_join(per_sample, by = c("canonical_site", "date")) %>%
    mutate(host_reads     = replace_na(host_reads, 0),
           nonhuman_reads = replace_na(nonhuman_reads, 0),
           host_pct       = if_else(nonhuman_reads > 0, 100 * host_reads / nonhuman_reads, 0),
           week           = study_week(date)) %>%
    group_by(canonical_site, week) %>%
    summarise(host = any(host_reads > 0), host_pct = mean(host_pct), .groups = "drop")
}

# Virus weeks after the last 12S sample have nothing to pair with
last_12s_week <- study_week(max(samples_12s$date))

build_pair <- function(virus_id, virus_label, taxid, host_id) {
  hw <- host_week(host_id)
  vw <- read_virus_weekly(taxid) %>% filter(week <= last_12s_week)
  list(virus_id = virus_id, virus_label = virus_label, host_id = host_id,
       host_label = unname(HOST_LABELS[host_id]), host_week = hw, virus_week = vw,
       paired = inner_join(hw, vw, by = c("canonical_site", "week")) %>%
         filter(!is.na(total_reads)) %>%
         mutate(virus = virus_reads > 0, log_depth = as.numeric(scale(log10(total_reads)))))
}

pair_data <- purrr::pmap(VIRUS_HOST_PAIRS, build_pair) %>% setNames(VIRUS_HOST_PAIRS$virus_id)

# ---- Passerivirus A1: keep only BLAST-verified weeks --------------------------------
# Reads the dashboard assigned to Passerivirus A1 were checked by BLAST
# against the NCBI nucleotide database. A read pair counts as verified if
# either mate's best hit was Turdivirus 1 (Passerivirus A1 itself). A
# site-week keeps its Passerivirus detection only if at least one verified
# pair came from that site and date; weeks with no verified pair are set to
# zero, exactly as if the virus had not been detected. Read counts in the
# weeks that are kept are left as the dashboard reported them. Site labels
# in the BLAST file are raw sample labels and are mapped back to canonical
# sites here; reads whose site or date is "unknown", and reads from sites
# outside this study, are dropped.
PASV_BLAST_FILE       <- "passerivirus_a1_blast_results.tsv"
PASV_VERIFIED_SUBJECT <- "Turdivirus 1"   # Passerivirus A1's own reference sequence

# The released BLAST file already carries canonical_site. The internal copy
# carries each utility's own sample label instead, which the alias file maps.
PASV_SITE_ALIASES <- if (has_private_file(PASV_SITE_ALIAS_FILE)) {
  k <- read_csv(file.path(working_dir, PASV_SITE_ALIAS_FILE), show_col_types = FALSE)
  setNames(recode_site(k$canonical_site), k$blast_site_label)
} else {
  character(0)
}

pasv_verified_weeks <- read_tsv(file.path(working_dir, PASV_BLAST_FILE), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(canonical_site = if ("canonical_site" %in% names(.)) recode_site(canonical_site)
                          else unname(PASV_SITE_ALIASES[Site]),
         date     = suppressWarnings(mdy(Collection_Date)),
         verified = str_detect(coalesce(BLAST_Primary_Name, ""), fixed(PASV_VERIFIED_SUBJECT))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(canonical_site), !is.na(date)) %>%
  group_by(canonical_site, date, Pair_ID) %>%          # either mate verifies the pair
  summarise(verified = any(verified), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(verified) %>%
  transmute(canonical_site, week = study_week(date)) %>%
  distinct()

# Zero out every Passerivirus week with no verified read
drop_unverified <- function(d) {
  d %>%
    left_join(pasv_verified_weeks %>% mutate(keep = TRUE), by = c("canonical_site", "week")) %>%
    mutate(keep = coalesce(keep, FALSE),
           across(any_of(c("virus_reads", "virus_rpmt")), ~ if_else(keep, .x, 0)),
           across(any_of("virus"), ~ .x & keep)) %>%
    select(-keep)
}
pasv_weeks_before <- sum(pair_data$pasv$paired$virus)
pair_data$pasv$paired     <- drop_unverified(pair_data$pasv$paired)
pair_data$pasv$virus_week <- drop_unverified(pair_data$pasv$virus_week)
cat(sprintf("\nPasserivirus A1: %d of %d virus-positive paired weeks had a BLAST-verified read (%d removed).\n",
            sum(pair_data$pasv$paired$virus), pasv_weeks_before,
            pasv_weeks_before - sum(pair_data$pasv$paired$virus)))

# ---- Statistics ------------------------------------------------------------------
VH_GLMM_CTRL <- glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))

# Model formula with the site random intercept and, if VH_DEPTH_COVARIATE,
# the scaled log10 sequencing depth
vh_formula <- function(fixed) {
  as.formula(paste(fixed, if (VH_DEPTH_COVARIATE) "+ log_depth" else "", "+ (1 | canonical_site)"))
}

virus_host_stats <- function(p) {
  d  <- p$paired
  m1 <- glmer(vh_formula("virus ~ host"), data = d, family = binomial, control = VH_GLMM_CTRL)
  m0 <- glmer(vh_formula("virus ~ 1"),    data = d, family = binomial, control = VH_GLMM_CTRL)
  b  <- fixef(m1)[["hostTRUE"]]
  se <- sqrt(vcov(m1)["hostTRUE", "hostTRUE"])
  chisq <- max(0, as.numeric(2 * (logLik(m1) - logLik(m0))))

  by_site <- d %>%
    group_by(canonical_site) %>%
    summarise(host_pct_weeks = 100 * mean(host), virus_pct_weeks = 100 * mean(virus), .groups = "drop")
  sp <- cor.test(by_site$host_pct_weeks, by_site$virus_pct_weeks, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

  tibble(
    Virus = p$virus_label,
    Host  = p$host_label,
    `Sites (n)`        = n_distinct(d$canonical_site),
    `Paired weeks (n)`  = nrow(d),
    `Weeks with virus (n)` = sum(d$virus),
    `Virus weeks with host nucleic acid (%)`          = round(100 * mean(d$host[d$virus]), 1),
    `Virus abundance (RPMT) in weeks with host nucleic acid (%)` =
      round(100 * sum(d$virus_rpmt[d$host & d$virus], na.rm = TRUE) / sum(d$virus_rpmt[d$virus], na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    `Virus detected, weeks with host nucleic acid (%)`    = round(100 * mean(d$virus[d$host]), 1),
    `Virus detected, weeks without host nucleic acid (%)` = round(100 * mean(d$virus[!d$host]), 1),
    `Odds ratio, within site (GLMM)` = round(exp(b), 2),
    `95% CI`         = sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", exp(b - 1.96 * se), exp(b + 1.96 * se)),
    `LRT chi-square` = round(chisq, 2),
    `p (LRT)`        = signif(pchisq(chisq, df = 1, lower.tail = FALSE), 3),
    `Site-level Spearman rho` = round(unname(sp$estimate), 2),
    `Site-level p`            = signif(sp$p.value, 3),
    `Singular fit`   = isSingular(m1)
  )
}

virus_host_summary <- purrr::map_dfr(pair_data, virus_host_stats) %>%
  mutate(`Adjusted p (BH)` = signif(p.adjust(`p (LRT)`, method = "BH"), 3), .after = `p (LRT)`)
write_csv(virus_host_summary, file.path(stats_dir, "virus_host_summary.csv"))


# ---- Follow-up: both rat viruses, Norway rat vs black rat ---------------------------
# The main pairs test each rat virus against any rat nucleic acid. Here each rat
# virus is also tested against each rat species:
#   1. Each species alone: the same summary as the main pairs
#      (virus_host_stats), with that species as the host.
#   2. Both species in one binomial GLMM on the same paired site-weeks:
#        virus ~ Norway rat + black rat + depth + (1 | site)
#      Each species is tested while holding the other constant (LRT
#      dropping that species from the full model).
# These are reported separately and are not part of the Benjamini-Hochberg
# adjustment of the main pairs.
#
# Site level (descriptive): Spearman correlation between the share of a
# site's paired weeks with the virus and the Norway rat share of its
# rat-positive weeks. Sites with no rat-positive weeks are dropped.

RAT_VIRUS_IDS <- c("luch", "rhev")

rat_species_followup <- function(virus_id) {
  row <- VIRUS_HOST_PAIRS[VIRUS_HOST_PAIRS$virus_id == virus_id, ]

  # 1. Each species alone
  single <- purrr::map_dfr(c("nrat", "brat"), function(h) {
    virus_host_stats(build_pair(virus_id, row$virus_label, row$taxid, h))
  })

  # 2. Both species together
  d <- pair_data[[virus_id]]$paired %>%
    select(canonical_site, week, virus, log_depth) %>%
    left_join(host_week("nrat") %>% select(canonical_site, week, nrat = host),
              by = c("canonical_site", "week")) %>%
    left_join(host_week("brat") %>% select(canonical_site, week, brat = host),
              by = c("canonical_site", "week"))
  stopifnot(!anyNA(d$nrat), !anyNA(d$brat))   # same 12S samples, so every week matches

  m_both <- glmer(vh_formula("virus ~ nrat + brat"), data = d, family = binomial, control = VH_GLMM_CTRL)
  m_no_n <- glmer(vh_formula("virus ~ brat"),        data = d, family = binomial, control = VH_GLMM_CTRL)
  m_no_b <- glmer(vh_formula("virus ~ nrat"),        data = d, family = binomial, control = VH_GLMM_CTRL)

  joint_row <- function(term, label, m_reduced) {
    b  <- fixef(m_both)[[term]]
    se <- sqrt(vcov(m_both)[term, term])
    chisq <- max(0, as.numeric(2 * (logLik(m_both) - logLik(m_reduced))))
    host_col <- sub("TRUE$", "", term)
    tibble(
      Virus = row$virus_label,
      Host  = label,
      `Sites with this host (n)`  = n_distinct(d$canonical_site[d[[host_col]]]),
      `Weeks with host nucleic acid (n)`   = sum(d[[host_col]]),
      `Virus weeks with host nucleic acid (%)`              = round(100 * mean(d[[host_col]][d$virus]), 1),
      `Virus detected, weeks with host nucleic acid (%)`    = round(100 * mean(d$virus[d[[host_col]]]), 1),
      `Virus detected, weeks without host nucleic acid (%)` = round(100 * mean(d$virus[!d[[host_col]]]), 1),
      `Odds ratio, adjusted for other species (GLMM)` = round(exp(b), 2),
      `95% CI`         = sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", exp(b - 1.96 * se), exp(b + 1.96 * se)),
      `LRT chi-square` = round(chisq, 2),
      `p (LRT)`        = signif(pchisq(chisq, df = 1, lower.tail = FALSE), 3),
      `Singular fit`   = isSingular(m_both)
    )
  }
  joint <- bind_rows(joint_row("nratTRUE", "Norway rat", m_no_n),
                     joint_row("bratTRUE", "Black rat",  m_no_b))

  # Virus detection by which rat species was detected that week
  cells <- d %>%
    mutate(rats = case_when(nrat & brat ~ "Both",
                            nrat        ~ "Norway rat only",
                            brat        ~ "Black rat only",
                            TRUE        ~ "Neither")) %>%
    group_by(rats) %>%
    summarise(paired_weeks = n(), virus_weeks = sum(virus),
              virus_pct = round(100 * mean(virus), 1), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(Virus = row$virus_label, .before = 1)

  # Site level: Norway rat share of rat-positive weeks vs virus detection
  by_site <- d %>%
    group_by(canonical_site) %>%
    summarise(virus_pct_weeks = 100 * mean(virus),
              rat_weeks       = sum(nrat | brat),
              nrat_share      = if_else(rat_weeks > 0, 100 * sum(nrat) / rat_weeks, NA_real_),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(!is.na(nrat_share))
  sp <- cor.test(by_site$nrat_share, by_site$virus_pct_weeks, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
  site_level <- tibble(Virus = row$virus_label, `Sites (n)` = nrow(by_site),
                       `Spearman rho` = round(unname(sp$estimate), 2), p = signif(sp$p.value, 3))

  list(single = single, joint = joint, cells = cells, site_level = site_level)
}

rat_followup <- purrr::map(RAT_VIRUS_IDS, rat_species_followup) %>% setNames(RAT_VIRUS_IDS)
rat_species_single <- purrr::map_dfr(rat_followup, "single")
rat_species_joint  <- purrr::map_dfr(rat_followup, "joint")
rat_species_cells  <- purrr::map_dfr(rat_followup, "cells")
rat_species_site   <- purrr::map_dfr(rat_followup, "site_level")

write_csv(rat_species_single, file.path(stats_dir, "rat_virus_by_species_single.csv"))
write_csv(rat_species_joint,  file.path(stats_dir, "rat_virus_by_species_joint.csv"))
write_csv(rat_species_cells,  file.path(stats_dir, "rat_virus_by_species_cells.csv"))

cat("\n===================================================================\n")
cat(" RAT VIRUSES: NORWAY RAT VS BLACK RAT\n")
cat("===================================================================\n")
cat("\nEach species alone:\n")
print(as.data.frame(rat_species_single %>%
        select(Virus, Host, `Weeks with virus (n)`, `Virus weeks with host nucleic acid (%)`,
               `Virus abundance (RPMT) in weeks with host nucleic acid (%)`, `Odds ratio, within site (GLMM)`,
               `95% CI`, `p (LRT)`)), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nBoth species in one model:\n")
print(as.data.frame(rat_species_joint), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nVirus detection by rat species detected that week:\n")
print(as.data.frame(rat_species_cells), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nSite level: Norway rat share of rat weeks vs % weeks with virus:\n")
print(as.data.frame(rat_species_site), row.names = FALSE)
cat("===================================================================\n")

# ---- Supplementary Figure (rat_species_virus_weeks) ---------------------------------
# How often each rat virus was detected, by which rat species' nucleic acid
# was detected that week: Norway rat only, both, black rat only, or
# neither. A virus that infects only Norway rats should be rare in weeks
# with only black rat, no more common than in weeks with no rat at all.
# n above each bar = paired weeks in that group. Descriptive; the test is
# the joint GLMM above (rat_species_joint).
RAT_WEEK_LEVELS <- c("Norway rat only", "Both", "Black rat only", "Neither")
RAT_WEEK_COLORS <- c(`Norway rat only` = RAT_COLORS[["Norway rat"]],
                     Both              = "#8E6FB0",              # between the two rat colors
                     `Black rat only`  = RAT_COLORS[["Black rat"]],
                     Neither           = "grey70")
RATWK_WIDTH_MM  <- 110
RATWK_HEIGHT_MM <- 50

rat_week_rates <- rat_species_cells %>%
  mutate(rats  = factor(rats, levels = RAT_WEEK_LEVELS),
         Virus = factor(Virus, levels = VIRUS_HOST_PAIRS$virus_label[VIRUS_HOST_PAIRS$virus_id %in% RAT_VIRUS_IDS]))

p_rat_weeks <- ggplot(rat_week_rates, aes(rats, virus_pct, fill = rats)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0("n = ", paired_weeks)), vjust = -0.5, size = FONT_SMALL / .pt) +
  facet_wrap(~ Virus, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = RAT_WEEK_COLORS, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(x = "Rat nucleic acid detected that week", y = "Weeks with the virus (%)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = FONT_BASE) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = FONT_TITLE, hjust = 0),
        axis.text = element_text(size = FONT_AXIS, color = "black"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
        axis.title = element_text(size = FONT_TITLE, color = "black"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
        panel.spacing = unit(4, "mm"),
        plot.margin = margin(2, 3, 2, 2))

save_figure(p_rat_weeks, supp_fig_file("rat_species_virus_weeks"), dir = supp_dir,
            width = RATWK_WIDTH_MM, height = RATWK_HEIGHT_MM)
p_rat_weeks

# ---- Analysis only (not in the manuscript): Passerivirus A1 host check -------------
# Passerivirus A1 has been found only in thrushes, but a close relative
# (Passerivirus GPS, about 82% amino acid identity to A1) was found in
# starlings and other birds (Grimwood et al. 2024, BMC Ecol Evol). Reads
# assigned to A1 could include related viruses from other passerines.
# Same summary as the main pairs, with each candidate host in turn. Run on
# the verified Passerivirus weeks, like the main pair.
pasv_row   <- VIRUS_HOST_PAIRS[VIRUS_HOST_PAIRS$virus_id == "pasv", ]
pasv_hosts <- c("thrush", "starling", "thrush_starling", "passerine")
pasv_host_check <- purrr::map_dfr(pasv_hosts, function(h) {
  p <- build_pair("pasv", pasv_row$virus_label, pasv_row$taxid, h)
  p$paired     <- drop_unverified(p$paired)
  p$virus_week <- drop_unverified(p$virus_week)
  virus_host_stats(p)
})
write_csv(pasv_host_check, file.path(analysis_dir, "passerivirus_host_check.csv"))

cat("\n===================================================================\n")
cat(" PASSERIVIRUS A1: CANDIDATE HOSTS\n")
cat("===================================================================\n")
print(as.data.frame(pasv_host_check %>%
        select(Host, `Weeks with virus (n)`, `Virus weeks with host nucleic acid (%)`,
               `Virus abundance (RPMT) in weeks with host nucleic acid (%)`,
               `Virus detected, weeks with host nucleic acid (%)`,
               `Virus detected, weeks without host nucleic acid (%)`,
               `Odds ratio, within site (GLMM)`, `p (LRT)`)), row.names = FALSE)
cat("===================================================================\n")

by_site_counts <- function(pairs) purrr::map_dfr(pairs, function(p) {
  p$paired %>%
    group_by(canonical_site) %>%
    summarise(
      paired_weeks       = n(),
      host_weeks         = sum(host),
      virus_weeks        = sum(virus),
      virus_weeks_host   = sum(virus & host),
      virus_weeks_nohost = sum(virus & !host),
      virus_reads_nohost = sum(virus_reads[!host]),  # before virus_reads, which overwrites the column
      virus_reads        = sum(virus_reads),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(Virus = p$virus_label, Host = p$host_label)
})
virus_host_by_site <- by_site_counts(pair_data)

site_rank <- site_labels_df %>%
  mutate(region = factor(region, levels = REGION_ORDER)) %>%
  arrange(region, state, shorthand_for_figures) %>%
  pull(current_site_label)

# ---- Supplementary Table (virus_host) ----------------------------------------------------
# Summary rows ("All paired sites") carry the test results; site rows
# carry the counts behind them. Count columns are filled for both.
vh_site_rows <- virus_host_by_site %>%
  mutate(site_order = match(canonical_site, site_rank)) %>%
  arrange(factor(Virus, levels = VIRUS_HOST_PAIRS$virus_label), site_order) %>%
  transmute(Virus, Host,
            Site = unname(site_label_map[canonical_site]),
            `Paired weeks` = paired_weeks,
            `Weeks with host nucleic acid` = host_weeks,
            `Weeks with virus` = virus_weeks,
            `Virus weeks with host nucleic acid` = virus_weeks_host,
            `Virus weeks without host nucleic acid` = virus_weeks_nohost,
            `Virus reads` = virus_reads,
            `Virus reads in weeks without host nucleic acid` = virus_reads_nohost)

vh_summary_rows <- vh_site_rows %>%
  group_by(Virus, Host) %>%
  summarise(across(c(`Paired weeks`, `Weeks with host nucleic acid`, `Weeks with virus`, `Virus weeks with host nucleic acid`,
                     `Virus weeks without host nucleic acid`, `Virus reads`, `Virus reads in weeks without host nucleic acid`), sum),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Site = "All paired sites") %>%
  left_join(virus_host_summary %>%
              select(Virus, Host, `Sites (n)`,
                     `Virus detected, weeks with host nucleic acid (%)`, `Virus detected, weeks without host nucleic acid (%)`,
                     `Odds ratio, within site (GLMM)`, `95% CI`, `LRT chi-square`, `p (LRT)`,
                     `Adjusted p (BH)`, `Site-level Spearman rho`, `Site-level p`, `Singular fit`),
            by = c("Virus", "Host"))

supp_table_virus_host <- bind_rows(vh_summary_rows, vh_site_rows) %>%
  mutate(pair_order = match(Virus, VIRUS_HOST_PAIRS$virus_label),
         row_order  = if_else(Site == "All paired sites", 0L, 1L)) %>%
  arrange(pair_order, row_order) %>%
  select(-pair_order, -row_order) %>%
  relocate(Virus, Host, Site, `Sites (n)`)

add_supp_table("virus_host", supp_table_virus_host,
  paste(paste0(fig_ref("virus_host"), "."), "Unit = paired site-week: a week (Sunday start) with both a 12S sample",
        "and a metagenomic sample at the site. Host nucleic acid = the host passed the 12S standard filter in",
        "a sample that week. Virus = at least one read of the virus that week. For each virus, the first row",
        "pools all paired sites and gives the tests: odds ratio of virus detection in weeks with vs without host",
        "nucleic acid from a binomial GLMM, virus ~ host + log10 sequencing depth + (1 | site), with a Wald 95% CI",
        "and a likelihood ratio test; adjusted p = Benjamini-Hochberg across all",
        "virus-host pairs; site-level Spearman correlation between the share of weeks with host nucleic acid and with",
        "the virus. Singular fit = TRUE means the site random effect was estimated at zero. Following rows",
        "give the counts for each site."))
```
