```{r figure9-virus-host}
# =========================================================================
# Shared figure style (Nature Communications: 5-7 pt text, 8 pt bold panel
# letters, 0.25-1 pt lines), matching the other figures in this file
# =========================================================================
vh_theme <- function(base = 6.5) {
  theme_bw(base_size = base) +
    theme(text = element_text(color = "black"),
          axis.text  = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
          axis.title = element_text(color = "black", size = 6.5),
          panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          strip.background = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 6.5),
          legend.title = element_text(size = 6.5),
          legend.text  = element_text(size = 6),
          legend.key.size = unit(3, "mm"),
          legend.background = element_blank(),
          legend.box.background = element_rect(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3, fill = "white"),
          legend.margin = LEGEND_BOX_MARGIN,
          plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))
}

# p-value text for figures: exact to 2 significant figures, "< 0.001" below
fmt_p_fig <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste("p =", formatC(p, format = "fg", digits = 2)))

# =========================================================================
# Host nucleic acid and virus heatmap by site and week (Figure 9a). One row
# per site with both data sets, in region order; one column per Sunday study
# week. Host panels = that host's nucleic acid as % of the site's non-human
# 12S reads, all on one color scale; virus panels = virus reads per 10M
# tobamovirus reads. White = sampled, nothing detected. GAP_FILL = no sample
# that week, including weeks before a site's first sample (not yet enrolled)
# and after its last. Styled like Supplementary Figure (boston_detections).
# =========================================================================
# compact = TRUE draws smaller text and legend for use inside Figure 9.
# panel_letters = FALSE drops the letter prefixes when the heatmap is itself
# one lettered panel of a larger figure.
# hosts = named vector, host_id -> panel title. One panel per host, drawn
# left of the virus panels. Several hosts let a virus be read against each
# candidate species in the same row of panels.
# legend_position = "bottom" draws the two color bars in a horizontal row
# under the panels instead of a column at the right, which frees that width
# for the panels themselves. Needed once there are four panels.
build_virus_heatmap <- function(hosts, pairs, compact = FALSE, panel_letters = TRUE,
                                legend_position = "right") {
  ts <- if (compact) list(y = 5, x = 5, strip = 6, legend = 4.5, bar = unit(8, "mm"), wrap = 60)   # 5 pt minimum
        else         list(y = 6, x = 5,   strip = 6.5, legend = 5.5, bar = VH_LEGEND_BAR, wrap = VH_TITLE_WRAP)
  bottom   <- legend_position == "bottom"
  bar_len  <- if (bottom) unit(16, "mm") else ts$bar
  bar_wide <- unit(2, "mm")
  bar_guide <- function(order) {
    # title.hjust centres the title over its own bar; without it the title
    # is left-aligned and a long title leaves its bar sitting off to one side
    if (bottom) guide_colourbar(order = order, title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5,
                                direction = "horizontal", barwidth = bar_len, barheight = bar_wide)
    else        guide_colourbar(order = order, title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5,
                                direction = "vertical", barwidth = bar_wide, barheight = bar_len)
  }
  # The right-hand column is narrow, so those titles wrap; a legend row
  # underneath has the width to run each on one line
  host_legend  <- if (bottom) "Host nucleic acid (% of non-human reads, log)"
                  else        "Host nucleic acid\n(% of non-human\nreads, log)"
  virus_legend <- if (bottom) "Virus reads per 10M tobamovirus reads (log)"
                  else        "Virus reads per\n10M tobamovirus\nreads (log)"

  # Every host comes from the same 12S samples, so one host's week grid and
  # site list cover them all
  host_wks <- setNames(purrr::map(names(hosts), host_week), names(hosts))
  host_wk  <- host_wks[[1]]
  full_week_seq <- seq(min(host_wk$week), max(host_wk$week), by = "7 days")
  sites <- intersect(unique(host_wk$canonical_site),
                      unique(unlist(lapply(pairs, function(p) p$virus_week$canonical_site))))
  site_levels <- site_rank[site_rank %in% sites]

  week_levels <- format(full_week_seq, "%m/%d/%y")
  # Label the week that contains the 1st of January, April, July and
  # October, as "%m-%Y". Monthly labels overlap at this panel width.
  week_end  <- full_week_seq + 6
  has_first <- format(week_end, "%d") < format(full_week_seq, "%d") | format(full_week_seq, "%d") == "01"
  first_month <- if_else(format(full_week_seq, "%d") == "01", full_week_seq, week_end)
  quarter_start <- has_first & as.integer(format(first_month, "%m")) %in% c(1, 4, 7, 10)
  week_tick_labels <- setNames(ifelse(quarter_start, format(first_month, "%m-%Y"), ""), week_levels)

  panel_ids    <- letters[seq_len(length(hosts) + length(pairs))]
  host_slots   <- seq_along(hosts)
  panel_titles <- stringr::str_wrap(c(paste(unname(hosts), "nucleic acid"),
                                      sapply(pairs, `[[`, "virus_label")),
                                    width = ts$wrap)
  # Strip titles are markdown so they can carry bold without the strip theme
  # setting a face. Panel letters are drawn on the assembled figure instead.
  panel_labels <- if (panel_letters) paste0(panel_ids, VH_PANEL_SEP, panel_titles) else panel_titles
  panel_labels <- setNames(md_bold(panel_labels), panel_ids)

  prep_panel <- function(d, value_col, panel_id) {
    # Every site-week in the figure's date range without a sample is a gap,
    # whether it falls before, during or after the site's sampling period
    gaps <- tidyr::expand_grid(canonical_site = sites, week = full_week_seq) %>%
      anti_join(d, by = c("canonical_site", "week"))
    fmt <- function(x) x %>%
      filter(canonical_site %in% sites, week %in% full_week_seq) %>%
      mutate(week_label = factor(format(week, "%m/%d/%y"), levels = week_levels),
             site = factor(canonical_site, levels = rev(site_levels)),
             panel = factor(panel_id, levels = panel_ids))
    list(tiles = fmt(d) %>% mutate(fill_val = if_else(.data[[value_col]] > 0, .data[[value_col]], NA_real_)),
         gaps  = fmt(gaps))
  }
  host_p  <- purrr::map2(host_wks, panel_ids[host_slots], ~ prep_panel(.x, "host_pct", .y))
  virus_p <- purrr::map2(pairs, panel_ids[-host_slots], ~ prep_panel(.x$virus_week, "virus_rpmt", .y))

  ggplot() +
    geom_tile(data = bind_rows(purrr::map_dfr(host_p, "gaps"), purrr::map_dfr(virus_p, "gaps")),
              aes(x = week_label, y = site), fill = GAP_FILL,
              color = HEAT_GRID_COLOR, linewidth = HEAT_GRID_WIDTH) +
    geom_tile(data = purrr::map_dfr(host_p, "tiles"), aes(x = week_label, y = site, fill = fill_val),
              color = HEAT_GRID_COLOR, linewidth = HEAT_GRID_WIDTH) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colors = RAT_HEAT_COLORS, transform = "log10", na.value = "white",
      breaks = c(0.01, 0.1, 1, 10), labels = c("0.01", "0.1", "1", "10"),
      name = host_legend,
      guide = bar_guide(1)
    ) +
    new_scale_fill() +
    geom_tile(data = purrr::map_dfr(virus_p, "tiles"), aes(x = week_label, y = site, fill = fill_val),
              color = HEAT_GRID_COLOR, linewidth = HEAT_GRID_WIDTH) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colors = VIRUS_HEAT_COLORS, transform = "log10", na.value = "white",
      # Explicit breaks, like the host bar: breaks_log() put its lowest tick
      # well inside the bar, so the low end carried no label
      breaks = VIRUS_BAR_BREAKS, labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE, big.mark = ","),
      name = virus_legend,
      guide = bar_guide(2)
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, nrow = 1, labeller = labeller(panel = panel_labels)) +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = week_levels, labels = week_tick_labels, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = site_label_map, drop = FALSE, expand = expansion(add = 0.8)) +
    labs(x = "Week", y = "Site") +
    vh_theme() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = ts$x, color = "black"),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = ts$y, color = "black"),
          axis.ticks.x = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, color = "grey40"),
          axis.ticks.length = unit(0.6, "mm"),
          panel.grid = element_blank(),
          panel.spacing = unit(if (bottom) 1.5 else 2.5, "mm"),
          # Titles sit directly on top of their panel
          strip.text = ggtext::element_markdown(size = ts$strip, hjust = 0, vjust = 0, lineheight = 0.9,
                                                margin = margin(t = 0, b = 1.5)),
          legend.position = legend_position,
          legend.box = if (bottom) "horizontal" else "vertical",
          legend.title = element_text(size = ts$legend, lineheight = 0.9),
          legend.text  = element_text(size = ts$legend),
          legend.spacing.x = unit(4, "mm"),
          legend.spacing.y = unit(2, "mm"),
          legend.margin = LEGEND_BOX_MARGIN,
          legend.box.spacing = unit(if (bottom) 0.5 else 1, "mm"),
          plot.margin = margin(t = 1, r = 1, b = if (bottom) 0 else 1, l = 1))
}

pairs_for_host <- function(ids) pair_data[VIRUS_HOST_PAIRS$virus_id[VIRUS_HOST_PAIRS$host_id %in% ids]]

# =========================================================================
# Groups used by the check below and by the analysis-only chunks: each
# virus-positive paired week, split by whether host nucleic acid was
# detected that week.
# =========================================================================
# Host names as written in titles: common nouns lowercase, proper nouns kept
HOST_LABEL_TEXT <- c(Rat = "rat", `Norway rat` = "Norway rat", `Black rat` = "black rat",
                     Thrush = "thrush", `Largemouth bass` = "largemouth bass")

VH_HOST_GROUPS <- c("Detected", "Not detected")
VH_GROUP_COLORS <- setNames(c(HEAT_12S_COLORS[4], "grey60"), VH_HOST_GROUPS)

virus_week_points <- purrr::map_dfr(pair_data, function(p) {
  p$paired %>%
    filter(virus, !is.na(virus_rpmt)) %>%
    transmute(Virus = p$virus_label, Host = p$host_label, canonical_site, week, virus_reads, virus_rpmt,
              host_group = factor(if_else(host, VH_HOST_GROUPS[1], VH_HOST_GROUPS[2]),
                                  levels = VH_HOST_GROUPS))
})

# Check: when do virus-positive weeks without host nucleic acid happen?
# Listed by date and site, with a count per quarter.
virus_weeks_no_host <- virus_week_points %>%
  filter(host_group == VH_HOST_GROUPS[2]) %>%
  transmute(Virus, Host, Site = unname(site_label_map[canonical_site]), week, virus_reads, virus_rpmt) %>%
  arrange(Virus, week, Site)
write_csv(virus_weeks_no_host, file.path(stats_dir, "virus_weeks_without_host.csv"))
cat("\nVirus-positive weeks without host nucleic acid, by quarter:\n")
print(as.data.frame(virus_weeks_no_host %>%
                      mutate(quarter = paste0(year(week), " Q", quarter(week))) %>%
                      count(Virus, quarter, name = "weeks") %>%
                      pivot_wider(names_from = quarter, values_from = weeks, values_fill = 0)),
      row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nMedian virus RPMT per virus-positive week, with vs without host nucleic acid:\n")
print(as.data.frame(virus_week_points %>%
                      group_by(Virus, host_group) %>%
                      summarise(weeks = n(), median_rpmt = median(virus_rpmt), .groups = "drop")),
      row.names = FALSE)

# =========================================================================
# Figure 9a: Norway rat and black rat nucleic acid, then the two rat
# viruses, by site and week (compact). Both host panels share one color
# scale, so each virus can be read against each species directly. Pacific
# rat (Kauai County only) has no panel here; all three species are in
# Figure 7. Legends are drawn under the panels so four panels fit at
# 180 mm without shrinking the weekly tiles.
# =========================================================================
p_rat_virus <- build_virus_heatmap(c(nrat = "Norway rat", brat = "Black rat"),
                                   pairs_for_host("rat"),
                                   compact = TRUE, panel_letters = FALSE,
                                   legend_position = "bottom")

# =========================================================================
# Figure 9b-c: host nucleic acid and virus detection over time, thrushes (b)
#   and largemouth bass (c). Rats are not repeated here because panel a
#   already shows their timing week by week. For each week, the share of
#   paired sites (12S and metagenomic sample that week) where the host's
#   nucleic acid was detected (12S red) and where each of its viruses was
#   detected (virus purples, from the same palettes as the panel a heatmap).
#   Faint points = weekly values; lines = centered 5-week moving average,
#   the smoothing used by Justen et al. (2026) for wastewater time series.
#   A smoothed week needs at least TS_MIN_WEEKS weeks with data in its
#   window. Both y-axes start at 0; each has its own upper limit because
#   the hosts are detected at different rates. Date ticks fall on the 1st
#   of January, April, July and October, matching panel a.
#
#   Subtitles give the Spearman correlation and p-value between each
#   smoothed virus series and the smoothed host series, computed on weeks
#   where both have a smoothed value, as in Justen et al. (2026). The
#   p-values treat weeks as independent, as Justen et al. do; the
#   within-site test is the GLMM (Supplementary Table (virus_host)). Values
#   are also saved to stats/virus_host_timeseries_spearman.csv.
# =========================================================================
TS_LINE_COLORS <- c(host = HEAT_12S_COLORS[4], virus1 = HEAT_VIRUS_COLORS[5], virus2 = HEAT_VIRUS_COLORS[3])

moving_avg <- function(x, k = TS_WINDOW_WEEKS, min_n = TS_MIN_WEEKS) {
  half <- (k - 1) %/% 2
  vapply(seq_along(x), function(i) {
    w <- x[max(1, i - half):min(length(x), i + half)]
    if (sum(!is.na(w)) >= min_n) mean(w, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_
  }, numeric(1))
}

# Weekly share of paired sites with a detection, smoothed
weekly_share <- function(paired, col) {
  w <- paired %>%
    group_by(week) %>%
    summarise(raw = 100 * mean(.data[[col]]), .groups = "drop")
  tibble(week = seq(min(w$week), max(w$week), by = "7 days")) %>%   # calendar weeks for the window
    left_join(w, by = "week") %>%
    mutate(smooth = moving_avg(raw))
}

# Spearman correlation between the smoothed host and virus series for one
# pair, on weeks where both have a smoothed value (as in Justen et al. 2026)
ts_spearman <- function(id, pairs = pair_data) {
  h <- weekly_share(pairs[[id]]$paired, "host")
  v <- weekly_share(pairs[[id]]$paired, "virus")
  d <- inner_join(h %>% select(week, host = smooth), v %>% select(week, virus = smooth), by = "week") %>%
    filter(!is.na(host), !is.na(virus))
  ct <- cor.test(d$host, d$virus, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
  tibble(Virus = pairs[[id]]$virus_label, Host = pairs[[id]]$host_label,
         weeks = nrow(d), rho = unname(ct$estimate), p = ct$p.value)
}

# One panel's data: the host series plus one series per virus. All viruses
# in a panel share the host they are tested against, so the host line comes
# from the first virus's pairing.
build_ts_panel <- function(host_label, virus_pairs, pairs = pair_data) {
  host <- weekly_share(pairs[[virus_pairs[1]]]$paired, "host") %>%
    mutate(series = paste(host_label, "nucleic acid"), role = "host")
  viruses <- purrr::imap_dfr(virus_pairs, function(id, i) {
    weekly_share(pairs[[id]]$paired, "virus") %>%
      mutate(series = pairs[[id]]$virus_label, role = paste0("virus", i))
  })
  stats <- purrr::map_dfr(virus_pairs, ts_spearman, pairs = pairs)
  lines <- sprintf("%s vs %s nucleic acid: \u03c1 = %.2f, %s",
                   stats$Virus, HOST_LABEL_TEXT[host_label], stats$rho, fmt_p_fig(stats$p))
  list(data = bind_rows(host, viruses) %>% mutate(x = week + 3),   # plot at mid-week
       subtitle = paste(lines, collapse = "\n"),
       stats = stats)
}

# Kept for the Spearman table below; the figure draws its own series from
# weekly_share() so that b and c can share one faceted plot
ts_thrush <- build_ts_panel("Thrush", "pasv")
ts_bass   <- build_ts_panel("Largemouth bass", "msrv")

virus_host_ts_spearman <- bind_rows(ts_thrush$stats, ts_bass$stats) %>%
  mutate(rho = round(rho, 2), p = signif(p, 3))
write_csv(virus_host_ts_spearman, file.path(stats_dir, "virus_host_timeseries_spearman.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(virus_host_ts_spearman), row.names = FALSE)

# =========================================================================
# Figure 9b-c: thrush and largemouth bass
# =========================================================================
# b and c are not two separately built columns. Each row of the block is
# ONE faceted ggplot (facet per pair), so the two columns are guaranteed
# the same width, share one y axis and one x range, and need only one
# legend each. Building them as four plots in a 2 x 2 cowplot grid does
# not work: align = "hv" forces every cell to the same panel size and
# crushes the series row.
#
# Top row: weekly share of paired sites with a host and with a virus
#   detection, smoothed with a centered 5-week moving average. Carries the
#   panel letters and titles in its facet strips (the VH_PANEL_SEP idiom
#   used by build_virus_heatmap).
# Bottom row: one point per virus-positive paired week, sized by virus
#   RPMT and colored by whether host nucleic acid was detected that week.
#   A grey line spans each site's paired weeks.
#
# Colors: red is host and purple is virus throughout, matching the two
# fill scales in panel a; grey is absence.

VH_BC_PAIRS <- c(b = "pasv", c = "msrv")
# Genus abbreviated in c: the full name clips at this panel width
VH_BC_TITLES <- c(b = "Thrush and Passerivirus A1",
                  c = "Largemouth bass and M. salmoides rhabdovirus")
# Titles only; the b and c letters are drawn on the assembled figure below
VH_BC_LABELS <- setNames(md_bold(VH_BC_TITLES), names(VH_BC_TITLES))
VH_SERIES <- c("Host nucleic acid", "Virus")

# Every site in either pair, so both facets show the same rows
vh_bc_sites <- site_rank[site_rank %in% unlist(lapply(VH_BC_PAIRS,
                                                      function(id) pair_data[[id]]$paired$canonical_site))]

# ---- Top row: smoothed series ---------------------------------------------------
vh_bc_series <- purrr::imap_dfr(VH_BC_PAIRS, function(id, panel) {
  bind_rows(weekly_share(pair_data[[id]]$paired, "host")  %>% mutate(series = VH_SERIES[1]),
            weekly_share(pair_data[[id]]$paired, "virus") %>% mutate(series = VH_SERIES[2])) %>%
    mutate(panel = panel)
}) %>%
  mutate(panel  = factor(panel, levels = names(VH_BC_PAIRS)),
         series = factor(series, levels = VH_SERIES),
         x      = week + 3)                               # plot at mid-week

p_bc_series <- ggplot(vh_bc_series, aes(x = x, color = series)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = raw), size = 0.3, alpha = 0.3, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_line(aes(y = smooth), linewidth = 0.4, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, nrow = 1, labeller = labeller(panel = VH_BC_LABELS)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = unname(TS_LINE_COLORS[c("host", "virus1")]),
                     name = "Paired sites with\na detection (%)") +
  scale_x_date(limits = range(vh_bc_series$x), expand = expansion(mult = 0.02)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 25, 50), limits = c(0, NA),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.08, 0.1))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Paired sites with\na detection (%)") +
  vh_theme() +
  theme(axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 5, color = "black"),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 5),
        panel.grid   = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing = unit(3, "mm"),
        strip.text   = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 6, hjust = 0,
                                                margin = margin(t = 0, b = 1.5)),
        legend.position = "none",
        plot.margin  = margin(t = 1, r = 1, b = 0, l = 1))

# ---- Bottom row: virus-positive weeks by site -----------------------------------
vh_bc_weeks <- purrr::imap_dfr(VH_BC_PAIRS, function(id, panel) {
  pair_data[[id]]$paired %>% mutate(panel = panel)
}) %>%
  mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = names(VH_BC_PAIRS)),
         site  = factor(canonical_site, levels = rev(vh_bc_sites)),
         host_group = factor(if_else(host, "Detected", "Not detected"), levels = VH_HOST_GROUPS),
         x = week + 3)

# Sampling period per site and panel, drawn behind the points
vh_bc_spans <- vh_bc_weeks %>%
  group_by(panel, site) %>%
  summarise(xmin = min(x), xmax = max(x), .groups = "drop")

vh_bc_points <- vh_bc_weeks %>% filter(virus, !is.na(virus_rpmt), virus_rpmt > 0)

p_bc_dots <- ggplot() +
  geom_segment(data = vh_bc_spans, aes(x = xmin, xend = xmax, y = site, yend = site),
               color = "grey88", linewidth = 0.25) +
  # Grey drawn first so red points are never hidden underneath
  geom_point(data = vh_bc_points %>% filter(host_group == "Not detected"),
             aes(x = x, y = site, size = virus_rpmt, color = host_group),
             alpha = 0.8, stroke = 0) +
  geom_point(data = vh_bc_points %>% filter(host_group == "Detected"),
             aes(x = x, y = site, size = virus_rpmt, color = host_group),
             alpha = 0.8, stroke = 0) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = VH_GROUP_COLORS, name = "Host nucleic acid", drop = FALSE,
                     guide = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(size = 1.4))) +
  scale_size_continuous(transform = "log10", range = VH_DOT_RANGE,
                        breaks = VH_DOT_BREAKS, limits = range(VH_DOT_BREAKS),
                        labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE),
                        name = "Virus reads per 10M\ntobamovirus reads (log)",
                        guide = guide_legend(order = 2)) +
  scale_x_date(limits = range(vh_bc_series$x),
               breaks = function(lims) seq(floor_date(lims[1], "quarter"), lims[2], by = "3 months"),
               date_labels = "%m-%Y", expand = expansion(mult = 0.02)) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = site_label_map, drop = FALSE, expand = expansion(add = 0.8)) +
  labs(x = "Week", y = "Site") +
  vh_theme() +
  theme(axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 5, color = "black"),
        axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 5, color = "black"),
        axis.ticks.length = unit(0.6, "mm"),
        panel.grid   = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing = unit(3, "mm"),
        strip.text   = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none",
        plot.margin  = margin(t = 1, r = 1, b = 1, l = 1))

# ---- Shared legends, one boxed key centred on each row --------------------------
# Legend text matches panel a: build_virus_heatmap(compact = TRUE) draws
# its color bars at 4.5 pt, so the keys here are 4.5 pt too
vh_legend_theme <- theme(legend.title = element_text(size = 4.5, lineheight = 0.9),
                         legend.text  = element_text(size = 4.5),
                         legend.key.size = unit(2.5, "mm"),
                         legend.spacing.y = unit(0.8, "mm"),
                         legend.margin = LEGEND_BOX_MARGIN,
                         legend.box.background = element_rect(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3,
                                                              fill = "white"))

p_fig9_legend <- cowplot::plot_grid(
  cowplot::get_legend(p_bc_series +
                        theme(legend.position = "right", legend.key.width = unit(4, "mm")) +
                        vh_legend_theme),
  cowplot::get_legend(p_bc_dots +
                        theme(legend.position = "right") + vh_legend_theme),
  ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(TS_STRIP_HEIGHT, DOT_PANEL_HEIGHT))

# ---- Figure 9: a, then the b-c block with its legends ---------------------------
p_fig9_bc_panels <- cowplot::plot_grid(p_bc_series, p_bc_dots, ncol = 1,
                                       rel_heights = c(TS_STRIP_HEIGHT, DOT_PANEL_HEIGHT),
                                       align = "v", axis = "lr")

p_fig9_bc <- cowplot::plot_grid(p_fig9_bc_panels, p_fig9_legend, nrow = 1,
                                rel_widths = c(1, VH_LEGEND_WIDTH))

# No labels here: a, b and c are drawn inside their own panel strips above
p_fig9 <- cowplot::plot_grid(p_rat_virus, p_fig9_bc, ncol = 1,
                             rel_heights = c(FIG9_A_HEIGHT, FIG9_BC_HEIGHT))

# a, b and c drawn at matching offsets from their own panel's left edge, so
# all three sit the same distance left of their titles. VH_BC_TOP is where
# the b-c block starts, measured from the bottom of the figure.
VH_BC_TOP <- FIG9_BC_HEIGHT / (FIG9_A_HEIGHT + FIG9_BC_HEIGHT)

p_fig9 <- cowplot::ggdraw(p_fig9) +
  cowplot::draw_plot_label(names(VH_LABEL_X), x = unname(VH_LABEL_X),
                           y = c(1, VH_BC_TOP, VH_BC_TOP),
                           hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = FIG_PANEL_LABEL_PT) +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))
save_figure(p_fig9, fig_file("virus_host"), width = FIG9_WIDTH_MM, height = FIG9_HEIGHT_MM)
p_fig9
```



```{r permanova-robustness}
# =========================================================================
# PERMANOVA robustness checks (analysis only, not in the manuscript)
# =========================================================================
# The site PERMANOVAs in fingerprint-stats treat every site-date as an
# independent sample, and the detection filter thresholds were set by
# hand. Each check below asks whether the site effect survives once one of
# those is handled. Nothing here changes a figure. Results are written to
# stats_dir and printed by manuscript-stats.
#
# Sequencing depth is not tested. Sites differ in population and sewer
# system type, and raw sequencing depth is not available after the
# pipeline.
#
#   1. Season. Calendar month of collection is entered with site, also
#      marginally, so the site R2 is what site explains over and above
#      month-to-month change shared across the network.
#   2. Repeated sampling. Samples are pooled to one profile per site per
#      calendar month (Jaccard: taxon detected in any sample that month;
#      Bray-Curtis: mean relative abundance over that month's samples).
#      This removes most week-to-week autocorrelation and evens out sites
#      that were sampled more often, at the cost of fewer rows.
#   3. Detection threshold. The standard filter is rerun over a grid of
#      minimum reads x minimum dates and the Jaccard site PERMANOVA refit
#      each time. Thresholds below MIN_READS need all_parsed, because
#      chordate_perfect_match.csv is already cut at MIN_READS. The grid
#      compares R2 and pseudo-F only, which do not need permutations, so
#      they are computed directly from the distances (permanova_fit())
#      instead of with adonis2. The MIN_READS x MIN_DATES cell must
#      reproduce the main adonis2 R2, which checks that shortcut.
#
# Run time: checks 1 and 2 are permutation tests on ~1,800 samples
# (n x n matrix work on every permutation, and by = "margin" tests each
# term separately), so they take several minutes. They run in parallel on
# ROBUST_CORES cores, and the results are cached in stats_dir and reused
# on later knits. Set ROBUST_REFIT = TRUE after the data change.
#
# Run after fingerprint-stats (reads its .rds files).


set.seed(42)
N_PERM       <- 999
ROBUST_REFIT <- FALSE                                    # TRUE = rerun checks 1-3 even if cached
ROBUST_CORES <- max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1)      # passed to adonis2(parallel = )
GRID_MIN_READS <- c(2, 4, 8, 16, 32)
GRID_MIN_DATES <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)

if (!exists("all_parsed")) all_parsed <- read_csv(parsed_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

sample_jaccard      <- readRDS(file.path(stats_dir, "sample_jaccard.rds"))
sample_bray         <- readRDS(file.path(stats_dir, "sample_bray.rds"))
sample_relabund_mat <- readRDS(file.path(stats_dir, "sample_relabund_mat.rds"))
stopifnot(identical(attr(sample_jaccard, "Labels"), attr(sample_bray, "Labels")))

# sample_id is "<canonical_site>_<YYYY-MM-DD>"
sample_id_site <- function(id) str_sub(id, 1, -12)
sample_id_date <- function(id) as.Date(str_sub(id, -10))

robust_meta <- tibble(sample_id = attr(sample_jaccard, "Labels")) %>%
  mutate(canonical_site = sample_id_site(sample_id),
         date           = sample_id_date(sample_id),
         month          = factor(as.integer(format(date, "%m")), levels = 1:12),
         year_month     = format(date, "%Y-%m"))

tidy_adonis <- function(res, check, distance) {
  tab <- as.data.frame(res)
  tibble(check = check, distance = distance, term = rownames(tab),
         df = tab$Df, R2 = tab$R2, F = tab$F, p = tab$`Pr(>F)`) %>%
    filter(!term %in% c("Residual", "Total"))
}

robust_cache <- file.path(stats_dir, "permanova_robustness.rds")
grid_cache   <- file.path(stats_dir, "permanova_threshold_grid.rds")
run_robust   <- ROBUST_REFIT || !file.exists(robust_cache)
run_grid     <- ROBUST_REFIT || !file.exists(grid_cache)

if (run_robust) {
# ---- 1. Month as a covariate ---------------------------------------------------------
robust_results <- bind_rows(
  tidy_adonis(adonis2(sample_jaccard ~ canonical_site + month, data = robust_meta,
                      permutations = N_PERM, by = "margin", parallel = ROBUST_CORES),
              "Site + month", "Jaccard"),
  tidy_adonis(adonis2(sample_bray ~ canonical_site + month, data = robust_meta,
                      permutations = N_PERM, by = "margin", parallel = ROBUST_CORES),
              "Site + month", "Bray-Curtis")
)

# ---- 2. One pooled profile per site per calendar month ---------------------------
site_month   <- paste(robust_meta$canonical_site, robust_meta$year_month, sep = "|")
month_n      <- table(site_month)
month_pa     <- rowsum((sample_relabund_mat[robust_meta$sample_id, ] > 0) * 1, site_month) > 0
month_relab  <- rowsum(sample_relabund_mat[robust_meta$sample_id, ], site_month)
month_relab  <- month_relab / as.vector(month_n[rownames(month_relab)])
stopifnot(identical(rownames(month_pa), rownames(month_relab)))
month_meta   <- tibble(site_month = rownames(month_pa),
                       canonical_site = str_remove(site_month, "\\|.*$"))

robust_results <- bind_rows(
  robust_results,
  tidy_adonis(adonis2(vegdist(month_pa * 1, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE) ~ canonical_site,
                      data = month_meta, permutations = N_PERM, parallel = ROBUST_CORES),
              "Site, pooled to site-months", "Jaccard"),
  tidy_adonis(adonis2(vegdist(month_relab, method = "bray") ~ canonical_site,
                      data = month_meta, permutations = N_PERM, parallel = ROBUST_CORES),
              "Site, pooled to site-months", "Bray-Curtis")
) %>%
  mutate(term = recode(term, Model = "canonical_site"))

save_both(robust_results, "permanova_robustness")
} else {
  robust_results <- readRDS(robust_cache)
  save_both(robust_results, "permanova_robustness")
  cat("Checks 1-2: using cached", basename(robust_cache), "(set ROBUST_REFIT = TRUE to rerun)\n")
}

# ---- 3. Detection-threshold grid -------------------------------------------------
# PERMANOVA R2 and pseudo-F straight from the distances (Anderson 2001):
# SS_total = sum of squared distances over all pairs / N, SS_within = the
# same within each site / that site's n. No permutations needed.
permanova_fit <- function(d, groups) {
  d2 <- as.matrix(d)^2
  g  <- factor(groups)
  N  <- length(g)
  a  <- nlevels(g)
  ss_total  <- sum(d2) / (2 * N)
  ss_within <- sum(vapply(split(seq_len(N), g),
                          function(i) sum(d2[i, i]) / (2 * length(i)), numeric(1)))
  ss_between <- ss_total - ss_within
  c(R2 = ss_between / ss_total, F = (ss_between / (a - 1)) / (ss_within / (N - a)))
}

grid_input <- all_parsed %>%
  filter(chordate %in% TRUE, perfect %in% TRUE) %>%
  filter(!(resolved_rank == "family" & family %in% DROP_AMBIGUOUS_NAMED_FAMILIES)) %>%
  filter(!is_human(genus, family)) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date))

threshold_cell <- function(min_reads, min_dates) {
  pa <- apply_standard_filter(grid_input, min_reads = min_reads, min_dates = min_dates) %>%
    distinct(canonical_site, date, resolved_name) %>%
    mutate(sample_id = paste(canonical_site, date, sep = "_"), present = 1) %>%
    select(sample_id, resolved_name, present) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = resolved_name, values_from = present, values_fill = 0) %>%
    column_to_rownames("sample_id") %>%
    as.matrix()
  cell_site <- sample_id_site(rownames(pa))
  fit <- permanova_fit(vegdist(pa, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE), cell_site)
  tibble(min_reads = min_reads, min_dates = min_dates,
         n_taxa = ncol(pa), n_samples = nrow(pa), n_sites = n_distinct(cell_site),
         mean_richness = mean(rowSums(pa)), R2 = fit[["R2"]], F = fit[["F"]])
}

if (run_grid) {
  threshold_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(min_reads = GRID_MIN_READS, min_dates = GRID_MIN_DATES) %>%
    purrr::pmap_dfr(threshold_cell) %>%
    mutate(standard = min_reads == MIN_READS & min_dates == MIN_DATES)
} else {
  threshold_grid <- readRDS(grid_cache)
  cat("Check 3: using cached", basename(grid_cache), "(set ROBUST_REFIT = TRUE to rerun)\n")
}

main_permanova <- readRDS(file.path(stats_dir, "permanova_result.rds"))
standard_cell  <- threshold_grid %>% filter(standard)
if (nrow(standard_cell) == 1 && abs(standard_cell$R2 - main_permanova$R2[1]) > 1e-8) {
  warning("Threshold grid at MIN_READS/MIN_DATES does not reproduce the main Jaccard PERMANOVA R2 (",
          round(standard_cell$R2, 4), " vs ", round(main_permanova$R2[1], 4),
          "). all_parsed and chordate_perfect_match.csv may be out of sync.")
}
save_both(threshold_grid, "permanova_threshold_grid")

# ---- Summary --------------------------------------------------------------------
cat("\n===================================================================\n")
cat(" PERMANOVA ROBUSTNESS\n")
cat("===================================================================\n")
if (exists("month_meta")) cat(sprintf("Site-months: %d (from %d samples)\n", nrow(month_meta), nrow(robust_meta)))
cat("\n")
print(as.data.frame(robust_results %>% mutate(across(c(R2, F), ~ round(.x, 3)))), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nThreshold grid (Jaccard site PERMANOVA; * = standard filter):\n")
print(as.data.frame(threshold_grid %>%
                      mutate(R2 = round(R2, 3), F = round(F, 2), mean_richness = round(mean_richness, 1),
                             standard = if_else(standard, "*", ""))), row.names = FALSE)
cat("===================================================================\n")
```


```{r publication-text}
# =========================================================================
# Figure legends and supplementary table descriptions
# =========================================================================
# All text that goes into the publication documents lives here, one entry
# per figure or table, keyed by the same IDs as MAIN_FIGURES, SUPP_FIGURES
# and SUPP_TABLES in the setup chunk. Edit the text here, not in Word: the
# Word files are rebuilt on every knit and overwrite any edits made in them.
#
# Formatting inside the text: **bold** and *italic* (for species names).
# Panel letters are bold. Figure and table numbers come from fig_ref(),
# supp_fig_ref() and supp_table_ref(), so they follow any renumbering.
# Nature Communications asks for a brief title and a legend of up to 350
# words for every figure; the publication-documents chunk warns if a
# legend is longer.
#
# This chunk runs before supp-tables-workbook, so the table descriptions
# here are also the ones written into the Excel workbook.

FIGURE_LEGENDS <- list(
  sample_collection = list(
    title = "Sample collection across the CASPER network",
    text  = paste0(
      "Each point is one wastewater sample, plotted by collection date and site (n = 1,867 samples ",
      "from 27 sites in nine states). Sites are grouped by region, and boxes at left mark the sites in",
      " each state, colored by state.")),
  composition = list(
    title = "Vertebrate read composition by site",
    text  = paste0(
      "Percent of each site's chordate reads assigned to each taxon, with human reads included (**a**)",
      " and removed (**b**). Colors show vertebrate class and, within each class, the most abundant ",
      "taxa. Remaining taxa in each class are grouped as Other. Sites are grouped by region.")),
  distinctiveness_similarity = list(
    title = "Taxon distribution and similarity among sites",
    text  = paste0(
      "**a** Number of non-human taxa detected at each site, colored by the number of sites at which ",
      "each taxon was detected. Taxa detected at 1 to 5 sites extend left of zero, and taxa detected ",
      "at 6 to 27 sites extend right. Sites are sorted by the number of taxa detected at 1 to 5 sites.",
      " **b** Pairwise Jaccard similarity between sites, based on presence or absence of non-human ",
      "taxa across all samples. Sites are ordered by hierarchical clustering. n = 27 sites.")),
  pcoa_drivers = list(
    title = "Sample-level ordination of vertebrate composition",
    text  = paste0(
      "**a** Principal coordinates analysis (PCoA) of Jaccard dissimilarity among samples (n = 1,830),",
      " colored by state. Small transparent points are samples, and larger opaque points are site ",
      "centroids. The PERMANOVA result for site and the two-dimensional fit error are shown. **b** ",
      "Site PCoA1 position versus mean taxon richness. **c** Site PCoA2 position versus the fraction ",
      "of detected taxa that are fish. In **b** and **c**, transparent points are samples and black ",
      "points are site means (n = 27). Lines show Theil-Sen fits with bootstrapped 95% confidence ",
      "intervals, and site-level Spearman correlations are shown.")),
  fish = list(
    title = "Fish composition by site",
    text  = paste0(
      "**a** Fish reads in each category as a percent of each site's fish reads and of its non-human ",
      "reads. Each taxon was assigned the category describing most of its U.S. population or supply (",
      supp_table_ref("fish_classification"),
      "). **b** The 40 fish taxa with the most reads, as percent of each site's non-human reads (log ",
      "scale), grouped by category and ranked by reads within category. White tiles indicate no ",
      "detection.")),
  distinctive_detections = list(
    title = "Selected site-specific detections",
    text  = paste0(
      "Detections of ten taxa linked to a nearby facility (zoo, equine facility, or aquaculture ",
      "facility) or to a restricted native or introduced range. Each point is one detection, colored ",
      "by state. All 27 sites are shown for each taxon, and grey lines span each site's sampling ",
      "period. Silhouettes are from PhyloPic.")),
  rats = list(
    title = "Rat species composition by site",
    text  = if (HAS_COORDS) paste0(
      "**a** Percent of rat detection dates belonging to each species, at sites or metro areas where ",
      "rats were detected on at least 15% of sampling dates. Sites in Boston, Chicago, Kansas City, ",
      "and St. Louis are combined by metro area. Ontario and Riverside, CA are offset for visibility, ",
      "and Hawaii is shown as an inset. **b** Rat detections at all 27 sites by species. Each point is",
      " one detection, sized by read count, and grey lines span each site's sampling period. The strip",
      " at left shows each site's sewer system type.") else paste0(
      "Panel **a**, a map of rat species composition, is drawn only from the private data because it ",
      "shows treatment plant locations. **b** Rat detections at all 27 sites by species. Each point is",
      " one detection, sized by read count, and grey lines span each site's sampling period. The strip",
      " at left shows each site's sewer system type.")),
  temporal_variation = list(
    title = "Temporal variation in detection of wild taxa",
    text  = paste0(
      "Percent of samples with a detection over time for seven wild taxa with a significant month ",
      "effect, using samples from the sites where each taxon was detected. Lines are smoothed with a ",
      "Gaussian kernel (21-day standard deviation) and colored by class. Ticks mark positive samples. ",
      "Grey shading marks months with higher detection than all other months combined (likelihood ",
      "ratio test, Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p \u2264 0.05). Strips give the number of detecting sites ",
      "and the adjusted p-value for the month effect.")),
  virus_host = list(
    title = "Virus detections and host nucleic acid",
    text  = paste0(
      "**a** Norway rat (*Rattus norvegicus*) and black rat (*Rattus rattus*) nucleic acid, as percent",
      " of non-human 12S reads, and reads per 10 million tobamovirus reads of Lucheng Rn rat ",
      "coronavirus and rat hepatitis E virus by site and week. The two host panels share one color ",
      "scale. Pacific rat (*Rattus exulans*), detected only at Kauai County, is not shown. Grey tiles ",
      "mark weeks without a sample, and white tiles mark sampled weeks with no detection. **b**, **c**",
      " Thrushes and Passerivirus A1 (**b**) and largemouth bass and Micropterus salmoides rhabdovirus",
      " (**c**). Upper panels show the weekly percent of paired sites with host nucleic acid and with ",
      "the virus. Faint points are weekly values, and lines are centered 5-week moving averages. Lower",
      " panels show each virus-positive paired week by site, sized by virus reads per 10 million ",
      "tobamovirus reads and colored by whether host nucleic acid was detected that week. Grey lines ",
      "span each site's paired weeks. A paired week is a site-week with both a 12S sample and a ",
      "metagenomic sample. Counts and tests are in ",
      supp_table_ref("virus_host"),
      "."))
)

SUPP_FIGURE_LEGENDS <- list(
  composition_with_without_human = list(
    title = "Pooled class composition with and without human reads",
    text  = paste0(
      "Percent of reads belonging to mammals, birds, and fish across all sites, with human reads ",
      "included and removed. Large points show pooled values, and small points show individual sites.")),
  boston_detections = list(
    title = "Detections over time at Boston DITP North and Boston DITP South, MA",

      "strip shows class. Taxa in bold were detected at both sites. Human reads are included. Grey ",

  alpha_diversity = list(
    title = "Alpha diversity by site",
    text  = paste0(
```
