```{r publication-text}
      ".")),
  pcoa_by_site = list(
    title = "Position of each site within the sample-level ordination",
    text  = paste0(
      "The ordination from ",
      fig_ref("pcoa_drivers"),
      "a, shown once per site. Each panel shows that site's samples in red, all other samples in grey,",
      " and the site centroid as a black \u00d7. Dispersion is the mean distance of the site's samples to ",
      "their spatial median.")),
  fish_dominated_samples = list(
    title = "Sample-level ordination by fish dominance",
    text  = paste0(
      "The ordination from ",
      fig_ref("pcoa_drivers"),
      "a, with samples colored by whether fish made up at least 20% of detected taxa. The PERMANOVA ",
      "result, with permutations restricted within sites, is shown.")),
  pcoa_site_metadata = list(
    title = "Site characteristics fitted to the sample-level ordination",
    text  = if (HAS_SITE_COORDS) paste0(
      "The ordination from ",
      fig_ref("pcoa_drivers"),
      "a, with samples and site centroids colored by region and centroids shaped by sewer system type.",
      " Ellipses cover the middle 68% of each region's samples. Arrows show the direction of ",
      "increasing latitude, longitude, and population served, with length proportional to the strength",
      " of fit. Solid arrows are significant (envfit, p < 0.05, n = 27 sites; population served was ",
      "fitted on the 25 sites with a reported population).") else paste0(
      "The ordination from ",
      fig_ref("pcoa_drivers"),
      "a, with samples and site centroids colored by region and centroids shaped by sewer system type.",
      " Ellipses cover the middle 68% of each region's samples. Arrows show the direction of ",
      "increasing population served, with length proportional to the strength of fit. Solid arrows are",
      " significant (envfit, p < 0.05; population served was fitted on the 25 sites with a reported ",
      "population). Latitude and longitude are not fitted here because they would show treatment plant",
      " locations.")),
  bray_curtis_pcoa = list(
    title = "Sample-level Bray-Curtis ordination of vertebrate composition",
    text  = paste0(
      "**a** PCoA of Bray-Curtis dissimilarity on relative read abundance among samples (n = 1,830), ",
      "colored by state. Small points are samples, and outlined points are site centroids. The ",
      "PERMANOVA result for site and the two-dimensional fit error are shown. **b** Site PCoA1 ",
      "position versus mean pig relative abundance. **c** Site PCoA2 position versus mean Pielou's ",
      "evenness. Points, fits, and statistics are as in ",
      fig_ref("pcoa_drivers"),
      "b and c.")),
  rat_species_virus_weeks = list(
    title = "Rat species detected in weeks with each rat virus",
    text  = paste0(
      "Percent of paired weeks with each virus, grouped by which rat species' nucleic acid was ",
      "detected that week. n is the number of paired weeks in each group. A paired week is a site-week",
      " with both a 12S sample and a metagenomic sample."))
)

SUPP_TABLE_DESCRIPTIONS <- list(
  sites = paste(
    "Site names were approved by each utility. Population served is as reported by the utility and is",
    "blank where not reported. Combined sewer systems carry sewage and stormwater, and sanitary systems",
    "carry sewage only. Study start and study end are the first and last collection dates at the site.",
    "Samples are counted once per site and collection date, after technical replicates were merged."),
  composition = paste(
    "Reads are summed across all samples at each site. Percentages give each category's share of the",
    "site's reads with human reads included and removed."),
  taxa_by_site = paste(
    "Taxa are listed at the rank to which they resolved (family, genus, or species). Sites detected is",
    "the number of the 27 sites at which the taxon passed the detection filter."),
  alpha_diversity = paste(
    "Kruskal-Wallis tests compare all sites, with epsilon squared as the effect size. Dunn's tests",
    "compare each pair of sites, with z positive when Site A ranks higher. P-values are",
    "Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted across the 351 site pairs within each metric. Repeated samples from a",
    "site are not fully independent, so p-values indicate the size of differences rather than strict",
    "inference."),
  jaccard_similarity = paste(
    "Similarity is the number of taxa detected at both sites divided by the number detected at either,",
    "from 0 (no taxa shared) to 1 (identical taxon lists)."),
  fish_classification = paste(
    "Aquaculture, farmed or imported food species. Freshwater, wild freshwater species. Marine, wild",
    "marine or reef species. Ambiguous, taxa spanning more than one category. Each taxon was assigned",
    "the category describing most of its U.S. population or supply."),
  fish_by_site = paste0(
    "Reads are summed across all samples at each site, with human reads removed. Site-level columns give ",
    "fish as a percent of the site's non-human reads and each category as a percent of the site's fish ",
    "reads and repeat on each row for that site. Taxon columns give each fish taxon's share. Categories ",
    "are defined in ", supp_table_ref("fish_classification"), "."),
  notable_detections = paste(
    "Each row is a collection date on which the taxon passed the detection filter at that site. Taxa",
    "were selected as examples of site-specific sources and are not an exhaustive list."),
  rats_by_site = paste(
    "Percent of rat detections is each species' share of rat detection dates at the site or metro area.",
    "Metro areas combine the sites within one city. All 27 sites are listed."),
  per_taxon_glmm = paste(
    "Detection in each sample was modeled with a binomial generalized linear mixed model, with sampling",
    "month as a fixed effect and site as a random intercept. Terms were tested by likelihood ratio test,",
    "and p-values were Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted across taxa. The site p-value is halved because a",
    "variance is tested at its boundary of zero. Site standard deviation is on the log-odds scale, and",
    "larger values indicate detection concentrated at fewer sites. Fit notes flag models that did not",
    "converge cleanly, mostly for taxa detected at one or two sites."),
  elevated_months = paste(
    "Elevated months had higher detection than all other months combined (likelihood ratio test,",
    "Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p \u2264 0.05 across the 17 months for each taxon). Detection rates use",
    "samples from the sites where the taxon was detected. Only April through August were sampled in",
    "both years, so elevated months may not reflect an annual cycle."),
    virus_host = paste(
    "A paired site-week had both a 12S sample and a metagenomic sample. A host was detected if it passed",
    "the 12S detection filter that week, and a virus if at least one read was detected. For each virus,",
    "the first row pools all sites and gives the odds ratio of virus detection in weeks with versus",
    "without host nucleic acid (binomial generalized linear mixed model with log10 sequencing depth as a",
    "covariate and site as a random intercept, Wald 95% confidence interval, likelihood ratio test,",
    "Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across pairs) and the site-level Spearman correlation. Singular fit",
    "indicates the site random effect was estimated at zero. Remaining rows give counts for each site."))


# Every figure and table needs text, and every entry needs a figure or table
check_ids <- function(have, need, what) {
  missing <- setdiff(need, have); extra <- setdiff(have, need)
  if (length(missing)) stop(what, " missing for: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
  if (length(extra))   stop(what, " given for unknown IDs: ", paste(extra, collapse = ", "))
}
check_ids(names(FIGURE_LEGENDS),          names(MAIN_FIGURES), "Figure legends")
check_ids(names(SUPP_FIGURE_LEGENDS),     names(SUPP_FIGURES), "Supplementary figure legends")
check_ids(names(SUPP_TABLE_DESCRIPTIONS), names(SUPP_TABLES),  "Supplementary table descriptions")

# The descriptions here replace the ones set where each table is made
for (id in names(SUPP_TABLE_DESCRIPTIONS)) {
  if (!is.null(supp_table_registry[[id]])) supp_table_registry[[id]]$description <- SUPP_TABLE_DESCRIPTIONS[[id]]
}
```


```{r supp-tables-workbook}
# =========================================================================
# Supplementary tables: one Excel workbook
# =========================================================================
# Writes every supplementary table registered with add_supp_table() into
# supp_dir/Supplementary_Tables.xlsx: a Contents sheet listing each table,
# then one sheet per table (Table S1, Table S2, ...). Each sheet starts with
# the table title and a short description of what one row is and how the
# values were calculated, followed by the table with a bold, frozen header.
# Numbering follows SUPP_TABLES in the setup chunk. The same tables are
# also saved as CSV files (supp_table_S<n>_<id>.csv).

missing_tables <- setdiff(names(SUPP_TABLES), names(supp_table_registry))
if (length(missing_tables) > 0) {
  stop("Supplementary tables not created (run the chunks that make them): ",
       paste(missing_tables, collapse = ", "))
}

wb <- createWorkbook()
title_style  <- createStyle(textDecoration = "bold", fontSize = 12)
desc_style   <- createStyle(wrapText = TRUE, valign = "top")
header_style <- createStyle(textDecoration = "bold", border = "Bottom", fgFill = "#F2F2F2",
                            wrapText = TRUE, valign = "top")

contents <- tibble(
  Table       = paste0("Table S", seq_along(SUPP_TABLES)),
  Title       = unname(SUPP_TABLES),
  Rows        = vapply(names(SUPP_TABLES), function(id) nrow(supp_table_registry[[id]]$data), integer(1)),
  Description = vapply(names(SUPP_TABLES), function(id) supp_table_registry[[id]]$description, character(1))
)

addWorksheet(wb, "Contents")
writeData(wb, "Contents", "Supplementary Tables", startRow = 1)
addStyle(wb, "Contents", title_style, rows = 1, cols = 1)
writeData(wb, "Contents", contents, startRow = 3, headerStyle = header_style)
addStyle(wb, "Contents", desc_style, rows = 4:(3 + nrow(contents)), cols = 4, gridExpand = TRUE)
setColWidths(wb, "Contents", cols = 1:4, widths = c(10, 55, 8, 110))

for (i in seq_along(SUPP_TABLES)) {
  id    <- names(SUPP_TABLES)[i]
  sheet <- paste0("Table S", i)
  tab   <- supp_table_registry[[id]]
  # Dates as plain text (YYYY-MM-DD), so Excel shows no time and no locale format
  dat <- tab$data %>% mutate(across(where(~ inherits(.x, c("Date", "POSIXct"))), ~ format(as.Date(.x), "%Y-%m-%d")))
  n_cols <- max(ncol(dat), 1)

  addWorksheet(wb, sheet)
  writeData(wb, sheet, paste0("Table S", i, ". ", SUPP_TABLES[[id]]), startRow = 1)
  addStyle(wb, sheet, title_style, rows = 1, cols = 1)

  # Description: merged across the table width (at least 8 columns), wrapped
  desc_cols <- max(n_cols, 8)
  writeData(wb, sheet, tab$description, startRow = 2)
  mergeCells(wb, sheet, cols = 1:desc_cols, rows = 2)
  addStyle(wb, sheet, desc_style, rows = 2, cols = 1)

  writeData(wb, sheet, dat, startRow = 4, headerStyle = header_style, keepNA = FALSE)
  freezePane(wb, sheet, firstActiveRow = 5)

  # Column widths from the header and data only (not the title or the
  # description), capped so long text such as site lists wraps instead of
  # stretching the column
  col_w <- vapply(seq_len(n_cols), function(j) {
    vals <- c(names(dat)[j], as.character(dat[[j]]))
    min(max(nchar(vals), na.rm = TRUE), 45) + 2
  }, numeric(1))
  setColWidths(wb, sheet, cols = seq_len(n_cols), widths = col_w)
  addStyle(wb, sheet, createStyle(wrapText = TRUE, valign = "top"),
           rows = 5:(nrow(dat) + 4), cols = which(col_w >= 45), gridExpand = TRUE, stack = TRUE)

  # Description row tall enough for its text across the merged width
  merged_w <- sum(c(col_w, rep(10, max(0, desc_cols - n_cols))))
  setRowHeights(wb, sheet, rows = 2, heights = 15 * ceiling(nchar(tab$description) / (merged_w * 1.1)) + 5)
}

workbook_path <- file.path(supp_dir, "Supplementary_Tables.xlsx")
if (file.exists(workbook_path)) file.remove(workbook_path)   # write fresh, never over an old file
saveWorkbook(wb, workbook_path, overwrite = TRUE)
cat("Wrote", workbook_path, "with", length(SUPP_TABLES), "tables:\n")
print(as.data.frame(contents %>% select(Table, Title, Rows)), row.names = FALSE)
```


```{r publication-documents}
# =========================================================================
# Publication documents
# =========================================================================
# Builds two Word files from the saved figures and the text in the
# publication-text chunk:
#   figures/Figures_and_Legends.docx: each main figure on its own page,
#     with its legend below it.
#   figures/supplemental/Supplementary_Information.docx: title page with the
#     manuscript title and authors, each supplementary figure with its
#     legend, then a list of the supplementary tables. The tables
#     themselves are in Supplementary_Tables.xlsx.
# Nature Communications asks for Supplementary Information as one file,
# preferably Word. Both files are rebuilt on every knit, so edit the text
# in publication-text, not in Word.
#
# Requires the officer package.

library(officer)

MANUSCRIPT_TITLE <- paste("Wastewater 12S metabarcoding recovers site-specific vertebrate signatures",
                          "across a multi-state surveillance network")
MANUSCRIPT_AUTHORS <- paste(
  "Emma E. Copen, Devon A. Gregory, Maggie Kester, Clayton Rushford, Alejandro Tovar-Mendez,",
  "Jonathan Naydenov, Clement Bagaza, Ava Barbaro, Rachel Poretsky, Jason A. Rothman, Ayaaz Amirali,",
  "Helena M. Solo-Gabriele, Lauren Stadler, Alessandro Zulli, Shelby L. O\u2019Connor,",
  "David H. O\u2019Connor, Marc C. Johnson")

DOC_FONT        <- "Arial"
DOC_FONT_SIZE   <- 10
DOC_PAGE_W_IN   <- 8.5
DOC_PAGE_H_IN   <- 11
DOC_MARGIN_IN   <- 0.75
DOC_IMG_MAX_H_IN <- 7.5     # leaves room for the legend under the figure
LEGEND_MAX_WORDS <- 350
FIG_LABEL_SEP   <- " | "    # "Fig. 1 | Title."

# Text with **bold** and *italic* marks -> formatted runs for one paragraph
md_runs <- function(x, size = DOC_FONT_SIZE) {
  parts <- regmatches(x, gregexpr("\\*\\*[^*]+\\*\\*|\\*[^*]+\\*|[^*]+", x))[[1]]
  lapply(parts, function(p) {
    bold   <- grepl("^\\*\\*.*\\*\\*$", p)
    italic <- !bold && grepl("^\\*.*\\*$", p)
    ftext(gsub("\\*", "", p), fp_text(font.family = DOC_FONT, font.size = size,
                                       bold = bold, italic = italic))
  })
}
add_md_par <- function(doc, x, size = DOC_FONT_SIZE, align = "left", space_after = 6) {
  body_add_fpar(doc, do.call(fpar, c(md_runs(x, size),
                                     list(fp_p = fp_par(text.align = align, padding.bottom = space_after)))))
}

# A figure scaled to fit the page width and DOC_IMG_MAX_H_IN, centered.
# Size comes from the saved PNG (600 dpi), so the aspect ratio is kept.
add_figure <- function(doc, png_path) {
  if (!file.exists(png_path)) stop("Figure file not found: ", png_path)
  px <- dim(png::readPNG(png_path))
  w  <- px[2] / 600; h <- px[1] / 600
  scale <- min(1, (DOC_PAGE_W_IN - 2 * DOC_MARGIN_IN) / w, DOC_IMG_MAX_H_IN / h)
  body_add_fpar(doc, fpar(external_img(png_path, width = w * scale, height = h * scale),
                          fp_p = fp_par(text.align = "center", padding.bottom = 6)))
}

legend_par <- function(label, legend) {
  n_words <- length(strsplit(gsub("\\*", "", legend$text), "\\s+")[[1]])
  if (n_words > LEGEND_MAX_WORDS) warning(label, " legend is ", n_words, " words; limit is ", LEGEND_MAX_WORDS, ".")
  paste0("**", label, FIG_LABEL_SEP, legend$title, ".** ", legend$text)
}

new_doc <- function() {
  read_docx() %>%
    body_set_default_section(prop_section(
      page_size = page_size(width = DOC_PAGE_W_IN, height = DOC_PAGE_H_IN),
      page_margins = page_mar(top = DOC_MARGIN_IN, bottom = DOC_MARGIN_IN,
                              left = DOC_MARGIN_IN, right = DOC_MARGIN_IN)))
}

# ---- Main figures -----------------------------------------------------------
fig_doc <- new_doc()
for (i in seq_along(MAIN_FIGURES)) {
  id <- names(MAIN_FIGURES)[i]
  fig_doc <- add_figure(fig_doc, file.path(fig_dir, paste0(fig_file(id), ".png")))
  fig_doc <- add_md_par(fig_doc, legend_par(paste("Fig.", i), FIGURE_LEGENDS[[id]]))
  if (i < length(MAIN_FIGURES)) fig_doc <- body_add_break(fig_doc)
}
fig_doc_path <- file.path(fig_dir, "Figures_and_Legends.docx")
print(fig_doc, target = fig_doc_path)

# ---- Supplementary Information ------------------------------------------------------
si_doc <- new_doc() %>%
  add_md_par("**Supplementary Information**", size = 14, align = "center", space_after = 18) %>%
  add_md_par(paste0("**", MANUSCRIPT_TITLE, "**"), size = 12, align = "center", space_after = 12) %>%
  add_md_par(MANUSCRIPT_AUTHORS, align = "center") %>%
  body_add_break()

for (i in seq_along(SUPP_FIGURES)) {
  id <- names(SUPP_FIGURES)[i]
  si_doc <- add_figure(si_doc, file.path(supp_dir, paste0(supp_fig_file(id), ".png")))
  si_doc <- add_md_par(si_doc, legend_par(supp_fig_ref(id), SUPP_FIGURE_LEGENDS[[id]]))
  si_doc <- body_add_break(si_doc)
}

si_doc <- si_doc %>%
  add_md_par("**Supplementary Tables**", size = 12, space_after = 6) %>%
  add_md_par(sprintf("Supplementary Tables 1 to %d are provided as a separate Excel file (Supplementary_Tables.xlsx).",
                     length(SUPP_TABLES)), space_after = 12)
for (id in names(SUPP_TABLES)) {
  si_doc <- add_md_par(si_doc, paste0("**", supp_table_ref(id), FIG_LABEL_SEP, SUPP_TABLES[[id]], ".** ",
                                      SUPP_TABLE_DESCRIPTIONS[[id]]))
}
si_doc_path <- file.path(supp_dir, "Supplementary_Information.docx")
print(si_doc, target = si_doc_path)

cat("Wrote", fig_doc_path, "and", si_doc_path, "\n")
```


```{r manuscript-stats}
# =========================================================================
# Manuscript numbers
# =========================================================================
# Numbers for the manuscript text, printed in one place. Nothing here is
# recomputed: every value is read from a file written by the chunk that
# produced it (stats_dir and supp_dir). This chunk runs last.

fmt_p_perm <- function(p) sprintf("p = %.3f", p)                               # permutation tests
fmt_p      <- function(p) if (p < 0.001) "p < 0.001" else sprintf("p = %.3f", p)  # analytic tests
read_stat  <- function(name) readRDS(file.path(stats_dir, name))
read_tab   <- function(dir, name) read_csv(file.path(dir, name), show_col_types = FALSE)
section    <- function(title) cat("\n[", title, "]\n", sep = "")

cat("\n===================================================================\n")
cat(" MANUSCRIPT STATS\n")
cat("===================================================================\n")

# ---- Samples and reads (parse-raw-tsvs, Table S1) -----------------------------
section("Samples and reads")
read_totals <- read_tab(stats_dir, "read_totals.csv")
cat(sprintf("  Sites: %d | Samples (site-dates): %s\n", read_totals$sites,
            format(read_totals$samples, big.mark = ",")))
cat(sprintf("  Samples in Table S1: %s\n", format(sum(supp_table_site_metadata$`n samples`), big.mark = ",")))
cat(sprintf("  Reads assigned to zOTUs: %s | chordate: %s | chordate perfect match (>= %d reads): %s\n",
            format(read_totals$zotu_reads_total, big.mark = ","),
            format(read_totals$chordate_reads, big.mark = ","), MIN_READS,
            format(read_totals$chordate_perfect_reads, big.mark = ",")))

# ---- Composition (figure2-composition) ----------------------------------------
section(paste0("Composition (", fig_ref("composition"), ", ", supp_table_ref("composition"), ")"))
composition <- read_csv(supp_table_path("composition"), show_col_types = FALSE)
human_pct <- composition %>% filter(Category == "Human") %>% arrange(`% of site reads (with human)`)
cat(sprintf("  Human %% of reads: min %s (%.1f%%), max %s (%.1f%%)\n",
            human_pct$Site[1], human_pct$`% of site reads (with human)`[1],
            human_pct$Site[nrow(human_pct)], human_pct$`% of site reads (with human)`[nrow(human_pct)]))
dominant_nonhuman <- composition %>%
  filter(!is.na(`% of site reads (without human)`)) %>%
  group_by(Site) %>% slice_max(`% of site reads (without human)`, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup()
cat("  Dominant non-human category (number of sites):\n")
print(table(dominant_nonhuman$Category))
cat("  Sites by dominant non-human category:\n")
print(as.data.frame(dominant_nonhuman %>% select(Site, Category, `% of site reads (without human)`) %>%
                      arrange(Category, Site)), row.names = FALSE)

cat("  Excluded family-level Phasianidae/Bovidae vs resolved reads:\n")
print(as.data.frame(read_tab(stats_dir, "ambiguous_family_exclusion_summary.csv") %>%
                      mutate(pct_of_family = round(pct_of_family, 4))), row.names = FALSE)

cat("  Bird reads, chicken and turkey vs other birds (network-wide):\n")
print(as.data.frame(read_tab(stats_dir, "bird_breakdown_network.csv") %>%
                      mutate(pct_of_bird_reads = round(pct_of_bird_reads, 2))), row.names = FALSE)

# ---- Site fingerprint (fingerprint-stats) ------------------------------------
section("Site fingerprint: Jaccard PERMANOVA, PCoA, dispersion")
permanova_result   <- read_stat("permanova_result.rds")
pcoa_stress        <- read_stat("pcoa_stress.rds")
sample_pcoa_scores <- read_stat("sample_pcoa_scores.rds")
cat(sprintf("  PERMANOVA (Jaccard): pseudo-F = %.2f, R2 = %.2f, %s\n",
            permanova_result$F[1], permanova_result$R2[1], fmt_p_perm(permanova_result$`Pr(>F)`[1])))
cat(sprintf("  PCoA1 = %.1f%%, PCoA2 = %.1f%% (together %.1f%%), 2D fit error = %.3f\n",
            sample_pcoa_scores$pct_var1[1], sample_pcoa_scores$pct_var2[1],
            sample_pcoa_scores$pct_var1[1] + sample_pcoa_scores$pct_var2[1], pcoa_stress))

permanova_result_bray   <- read_stat("permanova_result_bray.rds")
pcoa_stress_bray        <- read_stat("pcoa_stress_bray.rds")
sample_pcoa_scores_bray <- read_stat("sample_pcoa_scores_bray.rds")
cat(sprintf("  PERMANOVA (Bray-Curtis): pseudo-F = %.2f, R2 = %.2f, %s\n",
            permanova_result_bray$F[1], permanova_result_bray$R2[1], fmt_p_perm(permanova_result_bray$`Pr(>F)`[1])))
cat(sprintf("  Bray-Curtis PCoA1 = %.1f%%, PCoA2 = %.1f%% (together %.1f%%), 2D fit error = %.3f\n",
            sample_pcoa_scores_bray$pct_var1_bray[1], sample_pcoa_scores_bray$pct_var2_bray[1],
            sample_pcoa_scores_bray$pct_var1_bray[1] + sample_pcoa_scores_bray$pct_var2_bray[1], pcoa_stress_bray))

permanova_no_ubiq <- read_stat("permanova_result_no_ubiquitous.rds")
permanova_matched <- read_stat("permanova_result_matched_all_taxa.rds")
cat(sprintf("  Taxa at all %d sites removed: R2 = %.2f, %s | all taxa, same samples: R2 = %.2f, %s\n",
            N_SITES_TOTAL, permanova_no_ubiq$R2[1], fmt_p_perm(permanova_no_ubiq$`Pr(>F)`[1]),
            permanova_matched$R2[1], fmt_p_perm(permanova_matched$`Pr(>F)`[1])))

betadisper_overall <- read_stat("betadisper_overall.rds")
cat("  Dispersion (betadisper):\n")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(betadisper_overall))) {
  b <- betadisper_overall[i, ]
  cat(sprintf("    %s: F = %.2f, %s; samples per site vs dispersion: rho = %.2f, %s\n",
              b$distance, b$F, fmt_p_perm(b$p), b$size_vs_dispersion_rho, fmt_p(b$size_vs_dispersion_p)))
}

# ---- PERMANOVA robustness (permanova-robustness) -------------------------------
section("PERMANOVA robustness: month, site-month pooling, thresholds")
print(as.data.frame(read_stat("permanova_robustness.rds") %>%
                      mutate(R2 = round(R2, 2), F = round(F, 2), p = sprintf("%.3f", p))),
      row.names = FALSE)
threshold_grid <- read_stat("permanova_threshold_grid.rds")
cat(sprintf("  Threshold grid: Jaccard site R2 ranges %.2f-%.2f across %d filter settings (standard = %.2f)\n",
            min(threshold_grid$R2), max(threshold_grid$R2), nrow(threshold_grid),
            threshold_grid$R2[threshold_grid$standard]))

# ---- Site metadata on the PCoA (supp-fig-pcoa-site-metadata) ------------------
section("Site metadata fitted onto the Jaccard PCoA (envfit, site means)")
print(as.data.frame(read_tab(stats_dir, "pcoa_envfit.csv") %>%
                      mutate(r2 = round(r2, 3), p = fmt_p_perm(p))), row.names = FALSE)

# ---- Richness and taxon occurrence (fingerprint-stats) -----------------------
section("Richness and taxon occurrence")
richness_by_site <- read_stat("richness_by_site.rds") %>% arrange(n_taxa)
rich_test <- read_stat("richness_vs_samples_test.rds")
cat(sprintf("  Richness: %d (%s) to %d (%s) taxa per site\n",
            richness_by_site$n_taxa[1], richness_by_site$site_label[1],
            richness_by_site$n_taxa[nrow(richness_by_site)], richness_by_site$site_label[nrow(richness_by_site)]))
cat(sprintf("  Richness vs samples per site: Spearman rho = %.2f, %s (n = %d sites)\n",
            rich_test$rho, fmt_p(rich_test$p), rich_test$n_sites))

taxon_occurrence <- read_stat("taxon_occurrence.rds")
cat(sprintf("  Non-human taxa: %d | unique to one site: %d | at all %d sites: %d\n",
            nrow(taxon_occurrence), sum(taxon_occurrence$n_sites == 1), N_SITES_TOTAL,
            sum(taxon_occurrence$n_sites == N_SITES_TOTAL)))
cat("  Taxa at 25 or more sites (most widespread):\n")
print(as.data.frame(taxon_occurrence %>% filter(n_sites >= 25) %>% arrange(desc(n_sites), resolved_name) %>%
                      select(resolved_name, n_sites)), row.names = FALSE)
cat("  Taxa per occurrence bin:\n")
print(as.data.frame(taxon_occurrence %>% count(bin) %>% mutate(bin = factor(bin, levels = DIST_LEVELS)) %>%
                      arrange(bin)), row.names = FALSE)

# ---- What the PCoA axes track (figure3-figure4-pcoa) -----------------
section("PCoA axis correlations (Figure 4)")
corr_tests <- read_stat("richness_fishy_correlation_tests.rds")
bray_tests <- read_stat("braycurtis_correlation_tests.rds")
cat(sprintf("  Samples: richness vs PCoA1 rho = %.3f, %s | fish fraction vs PCoA2 rho = %.3f, %s\n",
            corr_tests$richness_test$estimate, fmt_p(corr_tests$richness_test$p.value),
            corr_tests$fishy_test$estimate, fmt_p(corr_tests$fishy_test$p.value)))
cat(sprintf("  Site means: richness vs PCoA1 rho = %.3f, %s | fish fraction vs PCoA2 rho = %.3f, %s\n",
            corr_tests$richness_test_site$estimate, fmt_p(corr_tests$richness_test_site$p.value),
            corr_tests$fishy_test_site$estimate, fmt_p(corr_tests$fishy_test_site$p.value)))
cat(sprintf("  Site means: pig vs Bray PCoA1 rho = %.3f, %s (without Ottumwa rho = %.3f, %s)\n",
            bray_tests$pig_test_bray$estimate, fmt_p(bray_tests$pig_test_bray$p.value),
            bray_tests$pig_test_bray_no_ottumwa$estimate, fmt_p(bray_tests$pig_test_bray_no_ottumwa$p.value)))
cat(sprintf("  Site means: evenness vs Bray PCoA2 rho = %.3f, %s\n",
            bray_tests$even_test_bray$estimate, fmt_p(bray_tests$even_test_bray$p.value)))

# ---- Fish-dominated samples (supp-fig-fish-dominated-samples) ----------------
section(paste0("Fish-dominated samples (", supp_fig_ref("fish_dominated_samples"), ")"))
permanova_fish <- read_stat("permanova_fish_dominated.rds")
fish_row <- which(rownames(permanova_fish) == "fishy_group")
cat(sprintf("  PERMANOVA, fish-dominated vs other samples, after site, permuted within site: R2 = %.3f, %s\n",
            permanova_fish$R2[fish_row], fmt_p_perm(permanova_fish$`Pr(>F)`[fish_row])))

# ---- Fish (figure5-fish) ---------------------------------------------
section(paste0("Fish (", fig_ref("fish"), ", ", supp_table_ref("fish_classification"), " and ", supp_table_ref("fish_by_site"), ")"))
fish_by_site <- read_csv(supp_table_path("fish_by_site"), show_col_types = FALSE)
fish_mag <- fish_by_site %>% distinct(Site, `Fish, % of site's non-human reads`)
fish_col <- "Fish, % of site's non-human reads"
cat(sprintf("  Fish %% of non-human reads: min %s (%.2f%%), max %s (%.2f%%)\n",
            fish_mag$Site[which.min(fish_mag[[fish_col]])], min(fish_mag[[fish_col]]),
            fish_mag$Site[which.max(fish_mag[[fish_col]])], max(fish_mag[[fish_col]])))
cat("  Fish reads by category (all sites):\n")
print(as.data.frame(fish_by_site %>% group_by(Category) %>%
                      summarise(reads = sum(Reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
                      mutate(pct = round(100 * reads / sum(reads), 1)) %>% arrange(desc(reads))), row.names = FALSE)

# ---- National consumption comparison (Discussion) ----------------------------
# The numbers the Discussion compares with USDA and NFI per capita
# consumption. Two parts.
#
# Livestock. For each of the five livestock taxa, the percent of a site's
# non-human reads, averaged across the 27 sites (each site weighted
# equally, so one high-read site does not carry the mean). Printed for all
# sites and again with the two animal processing sites (Ottumwa WPCF and
# Milan WWTF) dropped.
#
# Fish. Every fish taxon as a percent of the network's fish reads, ranked.
# The Discussion quotes the rank and percent of individual taxa from this
# table. Taxa are listed as resolved, not pooled: pooling salmon species,
# or deciding what counts as catfish or canned tuna, is a judgment call and
# is made in the text, not here.
section("National consumption comparison (Discussion)")

CONSUMPTION_LIVESTOCK  <- c("Gallus gallus", "Sus scrofa", "Bos taurus",
                            "Meleagris gallopavo", "Ovis aries")
PROCESSING_SITES       <- c("IA_Ottumwa_WPCF", "MO_Milan_WWTP")
stopifnot(all(PROCESSING_SITES %in% da_samples$canonical_site))

site_nonhuman_totals <- load_detections() %>%
  group_by(canonical_site) %>%
  summarise(site_reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop")

livestock_site_pct <- load_detections() %>%
  filter(resolved_name %in% CONSUMPTION_LIVESTOCK) %>%
  group_by(canonical_site, resolved_name) %>%
  summarise(reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::complete(canonical_site = site_nonhuman_totals$canonical_site,
                  resolved_name = CONSUMPTION_LIVESTOCK, fill = list(reads = 0)) %>%
  left_join(site_nonhuman_totals, by = "canonical_site") %>%
  mutate(pct = 100 * reads / site_reads)

livestock_summary <- function(d, label) {
  d %>%
    group_by(Taxon = resolved_name) %>%
    summarise(`Sites` = n(),
              `Site-averaged % of non-human reads` = round(mean(pct), 1),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(`Site-averaged % of non-human reads`)) %>%
    mutate(Set = label, .before = 1)
}

cat("  Livestock, site-averaged percent of non-human reads:\n")
print(as.data.frame(bind_rows(
  livestock_summary(livestock_site_pct, "All 27 sites"),
  livestock_summary(livestock_site_pct %>% filter(!canonical_site %in% PROCESSING_SITES),
                    "Animal processing sites dropped"))), row.names = FALSE)

cat("  Fish taxa ranked by percent of the network's fish reads:\n")
fish_network_rank <- fish_by_site %>%
  group_by(Taxon, `Common name`) %>%
  summarise(Reads = sum(Reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(`% of network fish reads` = round(100 * Reads / sum(Reads), 2)) %>%
  arrange(desc(Reads)) %>%
  mutate(Rank = row_number(), .before = 1)
print(as.data.frame(fish_network_rank), row.names = FALSE)
write_csv(fish_network_rank, file.path(stats_dir, "fish_network_rank.csv"))

# ---- Per-taxon mixed models (per-taxon-glmm) -------------------------------------
section(paste0("Per-taxon GLMM: site and month (", supp_table_ref("per_taxon_glmm"), ")"))
print(as.data.frame(read_tab(stats_dir, "per_taxon_glmm_summary.csv")), row.names = FALSE)
glmm_tab <- read_csv(supp_table_path("per_taxon_glmm"), show_col_types = FALSE)
cat("  Most site-restricted taxa (largest site SD, top 20):\n")
print(as.data.frame(glmm_tab %>% slice_max(`Site: random intercept SD`, n = 20) %>%
                      select(Taxon, `Common name`, `Sites detected (of 27)`, `Site: random intercept SD`)),
      row.names = FALSE)
# ---- Distinctive detections (figure6-distinctive-detections) ------------------------
section("Distinctive detections (Figure 6)")
notable <- read_csv(supp_table_path("notable_detections"), show_col_types = FALSE)
print(as.data.frame(notable %>% count(`Common name`, Site, name = "dates") %>% arrange(`Common name`, desc(dates))),
      row.names = FALSE)

# ---- Rats (figure7-rats) ------------------------------------------------------
section("Rats (Figure 7)")
# The map tables exist only when plant coordinates are available (private run).
if (file.exists(file.path(stats_dir, "rat_map_gate.csv"))) {
  rat_gate <- read_tab(stats_dir, "rat_map_gate.csv")
  cat("  Left off the map (any rat on fewer than the threshold % of sampling dates):\n")
  print(as.data.frame(rat_gate %>% filter(!map_group %in% read_tab(stats_dir, "rat_occurrence_for_map.csv")$map_group) %>%
                        arrange(pct_any_rat)), row.names = FALSE)
}
cat("  Species composition by metro area (all sites):\n")
print(as.data.frame(read_csv(supp_table_path("rats_by_site"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
                      distinct(`Metro area`, Species, `Dates detected (metro area)`,
                               `Rattus dates, all species (metro area)`, `% of metro area's Rattus detections`)),
      row.names = FALSE)

# ---- Temporal variation (figure8-temporal-variation) ------------------------------
section(paste0("Temporal variation (", fig_ref("temporal_variation"), ", ", supp_table_ref("elevated_months"), ")"))
print(as.data.frame(read_csv(supp_table_path("elevated_months"), show_col_types = FALSE)), row.names = FALSE)

# ---- Virus and host 12S (figure9-virus-host) ---------------------------------------
section(paste0("Virus detections and host 12S (", fig_ref("virus_host"), ", ", supp_table_ref("virus_host"), ")"))
print(as.data.frame(read_tab(stats_dir, "virus_host_summary.csv") %>%
                      select(Virus, Host, `Paired weeks (n)`, `Weeks with virus (n)`,
                             `Virus weeks with host nucleic acid (%)`,
                             `Virus abundance (RPMT) in weeks with host nucleic acid (%)`,
                             `Virus detected, weeks with host nucleic acid (%)`,
                             `Virus detected, weeks without host nucleic acid (%)`,
                             `Odds ratio, within site (GLMM)`, `95% CI`, `p (LRT)`, `Adjusted p (BH)`,
                             `Site-level Spearman rho`, `Site-level p`)), row.names = FALSE)

# Rat species follow-up and the counts behind the Passerivirus host check
print(as.data.frame(read_tab(stats_dir, "rat_virus_by_species_joint.csv") %>%
                      select(Virus, Host, `Virus weeks with host nucleic acid (%)`,
                             `Virus detected, weeks with host nucleic acid (%)`,
                             `Virus detected, weeks without host nucleic acid (%)`,
                             `Odds ratio, adjusted for other species (GLMM)`, `95% CI`, `p (LRT)`)),
      row.names = FALSE)
print(as.data.frame(read_tab(stats_dir, "rat_virus_by_species_cells.csv")), row.names = FALSE)

# ---- Alpha diversity (supp-fig-alpha-diversity) ---------------------------------
section(paste0("Alpha diversity (", supp_fig_ref("alpha_diversity"), ", ", supp_table_ref("alpha_diversity"), ")"))
print(as.data.frame(read_csv(supp_table_path("alpha_diversity"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
                      filter(Test == "Kruskal-Wallis (all sites)")), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n===================================================================\n")
cat(" END MANUSCRIPT STATS\n")
cat("===================================================================\n")
```


```{r human-read-totals}
# ---- Human vs non-human read totals (Results, first paragraph) -------------
# Prints every read figure in the opening Results paragraph, at each stage of
# filtering, so the manuscript numbers can be checked against one source.
# Human is defined exactly as elsewhere in this file: genus Homo or family
# Hominidae, which catches reads resolved to Hominidae as well as to
# "Homo sapiens".

read_totals <- read_csv(file.path(stats_dir, "read_totals.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

raw_chordate <- read_csv(chordate_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
filtered     <- load_detections(drop_human = FALSE)   # ambiguous family calls removed, as in Methods

human_flag <- function(d) {
  d %>% mutate(is_human = is_human(genus, family))
}

stage_summary <- function(d, label) {
  d <- human_flag(d)
  tibble(
    stage     = label,
    reads     = sum(d$reads, na.rm = TRUE),
    human     = sum(d$reads[d$is_human],  na.rm = TRUE),
    non_human = sum(d$reads[!d$is_human], na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

stages <- bind_rows(
  stage_summary(raw_chordate, "chordate, perfect, >= 8 reads"),
  stage_summary(filtered,     "+ detected on >= 3 dates at a site, ambiguous families removed")
) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_of_zotu  = 100 * reads / read_totals$zotu_reads_total,
    pct_human    = 100 * human     / reads,
    pct_nonhuman = 100 * non_human / reads
  )

cat("\n[ Human vs non-human reads ]\n")
cat(sprintf("  zOTU reads total: %s\n",
            format(read_totals$zotu_reads_total, big.mark = ",")))
cat(sprintf("  Chordate reads:   %s\n",
            format(read_totals$chordate_reads, big.mark = ",")))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(stages))) {
  s <- stages[i, ]
  cat(sprintf("\n  %s\n", s$stage))
  cat(sprintf("    reads     %s (%.1f%% of zOTU reads)\n",
              format(s$reads, big.mark = ","), s$pct_of_zotu))
  cat(sprintf("    human     %s (%.1f%%)\n",
              format(s$human, big.mark = ","), s$pct_human))
  cat(sprintf("    non-human %s (%.1f%%)\n",
              format(s$non_human, big.mark = ","), s$pct_nonhuman))
  cat(sprintf("    check: human + non-human = %s\n",
              format(s$human + s$non_human, big.mark = ",")))
}
```
